**The floor is the way back out, measured.** It is where the last crumb starts (every ancestor at its own width) plus the few characters the last crumb keeps as a stub, never under 20ch and never past the room the bar's first line has beside the drawer toggle (below the shell breakpoint), or the trail would drop under the toggle. A fixed 20ch alone let a seat's trail share a phone's line with its button, cutting the crumb mid-letter with the seat's own crumb out of sight; a trail that cannot show its ancestry beside the controls takes its own line.

- **The trail is what gives way**, and past its floor it SCROLLS rather than clipping: ancestors do not shrink, so once they alone exceed the bar nothing is left to ellipsise. No scrollbar is drawn (on a 52 px bar it would sit on the trail's baseline). While it overflows the trail is a tab stop, so a keyboard reaches what is past the edge; a trail that fits is not one (a dead Tab stop).
- **Each crumb's words are their own box**, and that box ellipsises. A crumb is a flex row (glyph, label), and text straight inside a flex container is an anonymous item no `text-overflow` reaches (the page's `h1` was cut mid-word).
- **The control group may not shrink at all.** It wraps, so shrinking drops the last control to its own row rather than shaving a label, and any factor above zero pushes the star to a second row by a fraction of a pixel (shrink is distributed proportionally in one pass). A `max-width` keeps a group wider than the bar wrapping rather than overrunning.
- **On a phone's width the controls are one line that scrolls**, sharing the trail's or lenses' line when they fit and taking their own when not. It is a container query on the header, because what overflows is the header and a viewport query cannot see a sidebar or a peek. Stacked rows would push the screen a third of the way down. The edge with more past it FADES (a control cut at the edge read as a broken label); a row that fits has no fade.
- **The section tabs never scroll: what does not fit folds into "More".** A fade was too quiet for a strip of places (a section past the edge went unnoticed). The strip draws the tabs that fit, in the workspace's order, and a "More" menu at its end holds the rest, each with its figure. The tab you are on is always drawn, taking the last place that fits; a tab only leaves from the end, so order never changes with width. A tab the reader cannot open draws the lock the sidebar and Settings column draw (the kit's `LockedLabel`), naming the access it needs. **A group the reader holds none of draws its key once** (a Worklet-only reader met a key on 13 of the sidebar's 15 rows: noise, not a reason). Where every row of a named group shares one reason (`groupLock`), the key and reason sit on the group's label and its rows go quiet, each still naming the access as its title and to a screen reader; a group with an open row keeps the key on each locked row. Rows are never hidden and stay focusable; the sidebar and Settings column follow the same rule. Widths are measured, and again whenever the strip or a tab changes size (a figure arriving, the web font loading, the density preference). **An object's own tabs fold the same way** (a seat's Overview … Settings, a turn's sections): a scrolling row hides its scrollbar and left a seat's Settings unseen past the strip's end. **A detail's tab bar stands one step (8px) above its panel**, one token for every tabbed detail (an integration's page, a seat's profile, a turn, the org builder's node editor, a room's details): the panel is the head's own, not a section a section's gap below. **Both are the kit's underline row with `overflow="menu"`**, so the fold, its arithmetic, "More" and the reading note are the kit's: the section strip is `Tabs` in router mode (a `nav` of links, the current one `aria-current="page"`, a folded link taking the kit's `foldProps`), and an object's tabs are its tab list with "More" beside it. The tab, its figure, the accent bar under the current tab and the focus ring are one control across workspace and object.
- **The star is on every page that is one.** A workspace's own page is already a sidebar row, so the star there is drawn unavailable, saying "Already in the sidebar", rather than left out (left out, it moved the header's controls between tabs). Whether a page IS a row is `nav.ts`'s `isSidebarRow`, asked by the inline star and the phone's More alike, never the path's length (the reader's Account is one segment and has no row, so it is starrable). Doclet's landing and pages are the exception: a page is starred from its own More menu, so neither draws the frame's star (`useOwnStar`).

### An open artifact is the screen

Every object page reads the same way: page bar with trail, the object's header (eyebrow, title, facts, actions), then tabs. An open artifact is the one exception: ONE slim bar the height of a large row (`size.row.lg`, 48 px), with the artifact at full size under it.

**Why.** An artifact's page is the artifact (deck, page, sheet, canvas), and every pixel of chrome above it shrinks it. The frame's bar, an object header with a fact line and a tab strip cost about 280 px at 1440 (a deck's slide drawn a third smaller) and most of a phone's first screen, to say things asked once: owner, change time, role. Tabs also split one object into four places to leave the artifact for. A document application draws one bar and opens the rest on demand; so does this.

**The bar** is the kit's `ArtifactBar`, drawn in the frame's place (`OwnPageHeader`, so the frame draws no page bar or trail):

| Where | What |
|---|---|
| Start | the navigation toggle on a narrow window, the way back to the gallery, the kind's glyph, the title as the page's `h1` (an editor renames in place: Enter takes it, Escape restores, a refusal is said at the field), and the version chip (`v3`, or `v2 of 3` in the accent while an older version is shown) whose menu picks a version, with Show latest beside it while an older one is shown |
| Middle | the kind's own views as one segmented control (a deck's Edit, Grid and Present). A view PUBLISHES them (`lib/artifacts/kindControls.ts`), with its own tools (a doc's Edit) and rows in More (Print, the presenter's window), so no kind draws a second chrome row. While a doc is edited it publishes its editing state instead ("Editing", and "Unsaved changes" once anything differs), with Cancel and Save |
| End | the presence stack, Details, History, Data where the artifact keeps any, People, Open in new tab, then Share and More (Rename, Change icon, Move to…, Settings, the kind's rows, Open in new tab, Copy link, Pin, Move to the trash). Move to… is the card menu's own row and Details' Move…, under one rule, so where an artifact is kept changes from the artifact as well as the gallery. Open in new tab is one action in both places under one key (the narrow bar folds the control into More's row); it opens the standalone page (`#/artifacts/{id}/standalone`) at the version on show |

Every control is an icon with its name and key in a tooltip; the name is the accessible name; a panel's control is pressed while its panel is open.

**It folds by its own width** (a container query, since a sidebar or panel decides its room): under 860 px the presence stack folds (People counts who is here), under 720 px Share keeps only its glyph, under 640 px the views and every unlabelled control fold into More as rows with their keys, and the kind's glyph gives the title room. Both arrangements are drawn and the stylesheet shows one, so no control is in two places at once.

**The panels** are the kit's `ArtifactPanel` in its `ArtifactWorkspace`: one at a time at the artifact's side, named by its heading, `panel=` in the address (opening pushes, so Back closes it). Beside the artifact where the workspace holds two useful columns (960 px), over its end edge where not, the whole screen on a phone. Data and History can take the whole workspace (`expand=1`; a comparison always does), the artifact kept mounted behind. Opening a panel moves focus to its heading; closing from inside returns focus to the opener; a panel a link opened takes no focus. `tab=data`, `tab=history`, `tab=settings` and `rail=people` are read as the panel each became and rewritten in place.

**What did not move**: the notices (an administrator's opening, a room that could not be joined, offline, a newer version published) are one-line banners across the workspace top, and following somebody is the `FollowBanner` there. The page still asks the frame for the window's height (`useFillScreen`), so the body scrolls inside itself and a panel beside it stays in view; a kind's view measures the body (`--artifact-view`) rather than reserving room for a header that is not there.

**An empty sheet names its columns in place.** A sheet with no columns (one an agent made bare) asks its editor for column names right in the sheet: a field per column, Add a column, and Save columns, which writes the sheet's one collection with every column as text and the first as the row name, as one confirmed schema change. The collection, its identifier and its policy are the datastore's words and never asked of a person. Data keeps every other column change. A reader who cannot edit is told who sets the columns up.

**On a page of its own.** Open in new tab opens `#/artifacts/{id}/standalone` in a new browser tab: the same page in the frame with no sidebar (`Shell`'s `standalone`, decided on the resolved route in `App.tsx`). Everything else the frame holds stays: session and socket, state bar, Ask and its panel, palette, peeks, keys. A kind's view runs as in the frame, with the same tickets, room and theme. The bar drops the navigation toggle (the kit draws none without a sidebar) and Open in new tab, and its way back leads to the gallery rather than a folder, since the tab was opened beside the dashboard.

**A comment's draft stands beside its pin**, in the kit's `Popover` with `side="right"` and `height="layer"`: right of the pin, left where only that side has room, below or above where neither, never past the frame. Its picture is fitted whole in a well of one height, whether drawing, shown or undrawable. On a phone it is written in the Comments panel.

**Placing a comment looks like the pin it places.** The Comment tool and the panel's Comment on a part carry the pin's glyph (`CommentPinGlyph`), and while placing, the pointer over the artifact is the draft pin (`commentPinCursor`), hotspot on the pin's tip, in the theme's and brand's colours, falling back to a crosshair.

### Asking an agent from a create page is a panel, not a mode

Every kind's create page is the artifact being made (a doc's page, a deck's stage and filmstrip, a sheet's grid, a board, a design's canvas, an HTML page's source). Handing work to an agent does not swap it for a form. The bar carries **Ask an agent**, drawn with the suggested agent's Crewlet character, opening the hand-off panel at the page's side: the kit's `AgentHandoffPanel`, an `ArtifactPanel` like Details or History: a column where there is room, a drawer over the page's end where not, the screen on a phone. The page stays live beside it.

**Why.** A segmented pill ("Write it | Ask an agent" and variants) replaced half the page with a form and made the two ways rivals. They are not: a person lays out a few slides, then asks an agent to write them. A side panel is how Figma's and Notion's assistants and Linear's agent assignment sit beside the work, and it keeps the direct way the page's own.

**The panel, top to bottom**: a line saying what the agent does with the brief; the brief (a composer: Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line) with briefs to start from while empty; the kind's own fields (a design's references); who builds it and in which project (`WhoBuildsIt`); **Goes with it** (what the reader already made: the doc's draft or template, the slides and theme, the board's figures, the sheet's columns and rows, the design's boards, the HTML page's source and what it may use, or "Your brief alone" while nothing) with the task exactly as filed behind a disclosure; then **What happens next**. The send is the panel's foot, "Ask SRE Lead" beside that agent's character, pressed by Enter in the brief or Command+Enter anywhere in the panel; held, it says why in words beside the button, and the engine's refusal is said above it.

The task's text is held to what a task's description holds (32 KiB, `TASK_BODY_MAX_BYTES`) before the press, on every kind, measured as filed (`filedTaskText`: the folder named, and an artifact the press makes first named by an id of its width). A design's boards and references, a deck's plan, a sheet's rows and a page's source ride the brief, and an over-bound text would be refused by the engine after the artifact was made.

The bar's primary stays the direct create, on every kind, in one order: Save in, the kind's tools, Ask an agent, Cancel, then the create. A design's create (**Create design**) publishes the boards as laid out, each a placeholder saying what it is for, with no agent asked, so a person who placed boards themselves can make the design without the panel. Its name is the canvas's own, in the panel that follows the selection with nothing selected (both ways need one), and going back to the layouts marks the one its boards were laid from.

**Two kinds arrive with it open.** An agent draws a design's boards, so its page opens with the panel beside the canvas; an HTML page is most often described rather than written, so its page is the source with the panel open (closing leaves the source to write in). Each arrives open only where the panel stands as a column (a laptop's width and up); narrower it would be a drawer over the first step, so it waits for the press. The state is the address's (`panel=ask`, and `panel=closed` on a kind that opens with it), as an open artifact's panels are.

### Moving, and going back

Every screen, section and filter is in the URL, so a view can be refreshed, bookmarked and shared. What takes deciding is the **session stack**: which navigations leave an entry behind, because that, not the URL, is what Back reads.

| Move | Stack | Why |
|---|---|---|
| a **section** — a tab, a view, opening a peek | pushes | the reader called these screens; Back after three should walk out through them |
| a **filter** — chips, sort, a search box, moving a peek | replaces | four ticked chips are ONE screen; Back means "off this list", not "untick one" |

The line is whether the reader would call it a different screen; it is the only judgement call in the router.

**Scroll is a property of a history entry, not of a URL.** The same screen reached twice is two places the reader has been, and keying by URL collapses them. Each navigation stamps a key into `history.state` and files the outgoing position under it; an entry with NO key is exactly "somewhere new", the only case that starts at the top. A restored position is re-applied for a short window while rows arrive (a scroll is clamped to the height that exists, so one attempt lands short) and abandoned the moment the reader touches the page. A REPLACE restores nothing: it stays on the entry the reader is looking at, and a restore there undid whatever the screen had scrolled into view in answer to its own filter.
### Signing in is a screen outside the frame

Four routes draw no sidebar and no page header: `#/login`, `#/invite/{id}.{secret}`, `#/reset/{id}.{secret}`, `#/enrol` (`FRAMELESS` in `app/nav.ts`); a frame of locked rows only shows what a person cannot open. **They dial nothing that needs a session**: only the frame dials the socket, made at boot (`app/Shell.tsx`), so opening one of these, or `/dashboard` signed out, sends no handshake, refusal probe or degraded-mode snapshot.

**The frame asks who this is once, before anything else**: `GET
/auth/session` (`lib/frameSession.ts`), also read by the sidebar's user block, refusal panel, Account, Home's greeting and People. **It dials for every session it reads.** The socket admits every principal the engine resolves whose stage may act; what a reader SEES is decided per push by access (overview for everybody, a seat's transcript for its lead and an admin, Worklet's pushes for whoever holds Worklet; ADR-0033), so a person with no app still reads the org chart, agent status and their own account.
- A `401` is nobody: sign-in follows, nothing dialled. Any other failed read says nothing about the session; the handshake decides.
- Access changed later reaches an open tab by the engine closing its socket (1013), after which the viewer is asked again. The frame does not poll.
- A socket the engine REFUSES outright (a seat taken out of the chart) is the handshake's refusal, drawn by `app/frame/AccessRefused.tsx`.
- The sign-in asks `GET /auth/session` once, to say whose session the browser holds, and not at all when a `401` routed the reader there. A signed-out `/dashboard` load asks once, as `#/login` opened directly does.
- **A sign-out holds the socket** until answered (`LiveSocket.hold`): the engine closes the session's socket on sign-out, and that close would re-dial into a refused handshake before the reload.

**The session cookie is the browser's only credential.** No token is kept in storage or a URL; every REST call and the handshake carry the cookie, which no script can read. An API token typed on the sign-in screen (Tier A token deployments, machine sign-ins) is sent once in the `Authorization` header of `POST /auth/token`, exchanged for a one-hour session, held nowhere but the form.

**A refused session sends the reader to sign in, and back.** A `401` from any REST call or the socket's plain-HTTP re-ask raises a session need (`protocol/session.ts`) that the app follows by replacing the current entry with `#/login?next=<where they were>`. It is STATE, not an event: the socket can learn it before React mounts, and a sign-in clears it. A `403 second_factor_enrolment_required` does the same toward `#/enrol`. A `4403`, a `seat_unavailable` and a refusal naming an access do NOT: the person is signed in and signing in again reaches the same access.

A tab that was read by somebody (`lib/reader.ts`) and lands here with no session lost it without a sign-out in this tab (one made here empties the tab's storage), so the sign-in says **You were signed out** and what ends a session elsewhere: sign-out from another browser or tab, password change, an administrator, its own deadline. Only a `401` from `/auth/session` says so: a node behind on the identity log answers `503` so no browser is wrongly told, and a throttle or dropped connection says nothing.

**`next` is an address on this page, or nothing.** An outsider can choose it for somebody else (a `#/login?next=…` link), so `lib/session.ts` accepts only a hash route of this dashboard: no `//`, backslash or control character, never one of the four screens above. Anything refused lands on Home.

**A sign-in replaces the history entry it was made from** and goes to `next`, where the frame dials; through `#/enrol` first when the session may only enrol.
- The screen prints the engine's own sentence for a refusal, nothing it composed: a failed sign-in is one refusal on purpose, a distinguishing message would be a roster.
- `second_factor_required` asks for the six-digit or a recovery code and resubmits the same details with it; a `429` says the seconds `Retry-After` names.
- The password form is always there; the API token waits behind **Use an API token instead**.
- Where `/health` says `identity: unclaimed`, nobody has joined (an open invitation does not change that; redeeming it creates its person) and the token is the only way in: its form is open and the page says how to begin. Sign in with the token, open **Company › Structure**, choose your human seat and invite or create yourself on it (every person holds a human seat), or open a link already issued.
- A node running no company has no seat, so the company comes first, created from **Company › Structure** with a seat for yourself (see [How the first person exists](../concepts/identity-and-access.md#how-the-first-person-exists)).
- `unknown` keeps the ordinary page: a node that cannot read its identity estate is not one with nobody in it.
- Somebody already signed in is told who, and offered to continue as them.

**A signed-out load costs one refused request, a two-step sign-in one more, and the dashboard logs neither.** The cookie is `HttpOnly`, so only the engine can say whether the browser is signed in, and its answer for nobody is the `401` the frame, refusal probe and REST calls route on; a `200` meaning "nobody" would be another exemption from the request guard and a second shape of "who am I". So a cold load of `#/login`, or of any screen opened signed out, makes exactly one refused request, `GET /auth/session`. A person with a second factor adds one at the password step: `POST /auth/login` answers `401 second_factor_required`, typed so nothing reads it as signed out, and a `401` because a `200` from `/auth/login` always opened a session. Browsers log every 4xx ("Failed to load resource … 401") and no page can stop it, so those one or two lines are expected; the dashboard calls the console nowhere, and any other refused request or console line of ours is a regression. `app/App.session.test.tsx` holds the cold loads of `#/`, `#/account` and `#/login` to the one; `routes/signin/SignIn.test.tsx` holds the two-step sign-in to its one more and every sign-in path to a quiet console.

**An invitation is read, never spent, by opening it.** The link carries the whole credential in the fragment, which no browser sends to a server; the screen sends the secret BESIDE the id (`X-Crewlet-Invite-Secret` header on the view, the body on the redemption), never in a request URL. Both link headers are declared in `contract/identity.ts` (`INVITE_SECRET_HEADER`, `RESET_SECRET_HEADER`) and held to the views' spellings by an engine test: a header renamed on one side presents no secret, and every link opens as the `410` of an id nobody issued.
- The view names who it is for, who sent it when a person did (one from a Tier A token or service account, the company's first person's above all, names none: `token:founder` means nothing to its reader), and the seat it binds. Every invitation names a human seat.
- Where the chart no longer holds the seat, the screen says before the form that redeeming will be refused and to ask for a new one.
- The form proposes the engine's suggested login (held to the login grammar, said under the field before posting), says which session it signs out if the browser is signed in as somebody, states the password length `/auth/config` asks for, and takes the password twice: a slip in the only copy is an account nobody can sign in to, fixed only by an administrator's reset link.
- A spent, withdrawn or mistyped link is one screen (`410`); a login or address somebody else holds is the engine's own sentence (`409`) over the form as typed.

**A password link is the invitation's screen again, and signs nobody in.** Two links land on `#/reset`: the **reset link** an administrator issues somebody with a password, and the **first password link** a person's create hands back. Each carries its credential in the fragment and sends the secret beside the id (`X-Crewlet-Reset-Secret` header on the view, the body on the spend). The view names whose password it sets and which link it is (`first`):
- Reset: **Choose a new password**; says setting it ends every session the person holds.
- First password: **Choose your password**; ends nothing (told it would, a person just created read their first sign-in as a lock-out).
- Either takes the password twice and states the length `/auth/config` asks for.
- A spent, revoked, expired or mistyped link is one screen (`410`), **This password link can no longer be used**, naming no lifetime (reset: a day; first password: a week; a dead link does not say which it was).
- Setting the password opens no session; the screen ends on a **Sign in** button, where a second factor is asked for, which a link-issued session would skip.

**A required second factor is enrolled before anything else opens.** `#/enrol` asks `POST /auth/totp` for a seed and draws a **QR code** of its `otpauth://` URI exactly as answered, with the key grouped in fours and a link opening the same URI in an app on this device, for whoever cannot scan. It confirms a code from the app and shows the first recovery codes once. The QR comes first because an authenticator usually lives on a phone; typing thirty-two base32 characters risks a slip and a mismatched first code. It is inline SVG from the encoder's module matrix (`uqr`, MIT, no dependencies): no image URL, markup string or fetch, so the Content-Security-Policy is unchanged, and the URI, which carries the seed, goes nowhere but the drawing and the link (no log, URL or storage). It is shown while the seed is, and gone with it. The [Account](#account-the-readers-own-page) page offers the same two steps, and new recovery codes, to add or replace one later.

**A step-up is one modal, and the refused request is replayed.** A `403 step_up_required` is not a screen's to handle: `protocol/rest.ts` asks the one confirmer the app installed (`app/StepUp.tsx`), which opens a single "Confirm it’s you" dialog however many requests were refused. It posts the password to `POST /auth/step-up`, plus a code where the person holds a second factor (read from `GET /iam/credentials`, so the code is asked for, not optional, and the text asks for both), and on success replays each refused request exactly once.
- A wrong password or code is the engine's one sign-in refusal, said as a confirmation refused ("That password or code was not accepted"), not as "sign-in details"; the dialog stays for another try.
- While it asks, a dialog whose write it holds says it waits for the person (`lib/waiting.ts`): button "Waiting for you", close "Waiting for you to confirm who you are."
- Cancelled, each request fails with the refusal it had.
- A refusal of `/auth/step-up` itself is never confirmed, so a confirmation cannot ask for another.

**A sign-out reloads.** `POST /auth/logout` (or `POST /auth/logout/all` for every device) and, only once the engine has answered, a reload into `#/login`: a route change would leave the store, cached answers and the socket's last snapshot in memory for whoever sits down next. The tab's `sessionStorage` (holding the org builder's kept draft, and surviving a reload) is emptied first. A sign-out nothing answered, or a revocation the engine could not confirm (`503` with an `op_id`), is said, and the page stays. Both are drawn from `GET /auth/session`, not the socket's `viewer` question, so a person the socket refuses still has them: the user block offers both under the session's own login, and the refusal's strip has its own **Sign out**.

**A sign-in by somebody else hands the tab over the same way.** A session also ends with nobody signing out (idle deadline, revocation, sign-out in another tab), leaving the last reader's screen in memory. So the tab records WHO it is read by (`lib/reader.ts`: the principal id every sign-in answers, kept in the tab's `sessionStorage`, adopted from `GET /auth/session` by a tab opened with a session already in the browser). A sign-in naming anybody else empties the tab's storage, records the new reader and reloads into where the sign-in was going (the enrolment first, for a session that may only enrol). The same person signing in again keeps the tab and the builder's kept draft; that draft is stamped with its reader, and one kept for anybody else is discarded unoffered.

**And so does a session somebody else left in the browser.** Signing in as somebody else in one tab moves the cookie every tab shares and tries, best effort (a sign-in is never refused over it), to end the session the others were opened with. Where the close lands, each socket closes `4401`, and the socket's `GET /auth/session` before dialling again answers for the new person; the frame's read does too when the tab next becomes visible. Where it does not, nothing on the socket says so, and an open window would keep drawing the last person's screen while its requests go out as the new one. So every request a tab makes names its reader (`X-Crewlet-Reader`, `protocol/signin.ts`): REST reads and changes, an act and its Retry, a download, the degraded-mode snapshot, the refusal probe, and the session keepalive (`protocol/keepalive.ts`), which reads the session every five minutes while the socket is open unless the engine answered something else in the last five.
- A handshake cannot carry a header, so it names the reader in its URL (`/ws/stream?reader=`, `READER_PARAM`), read by the engine on an upgrade alone. The id is no secret, but a proxy's access log of `/ws/stream` records it.
- The engine refuses a request whose cookie is anybody else's with `409 reader_changed` before it runs: a press in that window changes nothing as the new person, a Retry of the last person's change sends their operation as nobody's, and a socket re-dialled under the new cookie draws nothing of the new company (its refused handshake reaches the page as a bare 1006, and the refusal probe reads the `409`).
- Two requests name nobody: the session read itself (how a tab learns whom to be handed to) and the token exchange (which signs somebody in).
- On any of these signals a tab read by anybody else is handed over exactly as a sign-in by them would (emptied, new reader recorded, reloaded where it was), and the socket dials nothing for them first (`lib/session.ts`'s `takeSession`, which `main.tsx` hands the socket, and `sessionMoved`, which it installs for the refusal).
- A window whose socket stays open and that sends nothing is handed over by the keepalive in under ten minutes (two intervals: a tick skips a tab the engine answered less than five minutes before, which may predate the sign-in).

**A tab learns who it is read by before it is served anything.** A tab opened with a session already in the browser records nobody until a session read answers. The frame's `GET /auth/session` records it before the socket dials, and the socket holds every dial for a tab that has still recorded nobody (the frame's when that read FAILED, a reconnect, a signed-out tab returning to view) behind a session read of its own (`protocol/socket.ts`'s `learnReader`): it records whoever answers and dials naming them, a `401` is the sign-in, and any other failure dials nothing and asks again on the backoff, since a dial naming nobody is served as whoever holds the cookie. Otherwise a sign-in in another tab would be ADOPTED as the reader of a tab drawing what it was served for the last one. Outside the check:
- A browser refusing the tab's storage records nobody (`lib/reader.ts` keeps the reader nowhere else), so its requests name nobody and a moved cookie is served rather than refused; the setting that blocks storage usually blocks the cookie, and so the session.
- A screen's own REST read sent before any session read answered names nobody. None is sent today: every screen's REST read waits for the frame's session answer or the viewer, which the socket answers only after a session read.

**A thing worth linking to gets an address, not a scroll position.** A unit has its own address, its panel over Structure's Table (`#/company/org/table` with `peek=unit:<key>`), so it can be linked and carry state; the old `org` address with `?unit=Backend` and its router-level reveal hook are gone, and there is no reveal-on-arrival hook. A selection that belongs in the URL rather than the path stays a filter: Structure reads `unit=` and `seat=` to name the selected node (see the builder's toolbar below) and opens its editor only where the address adds `editor=open`, once; a `DataGrid` scrolls its selected row into view. The ring is static: nothing on a live screen animates for data.

**Work that exists nowhere else is not left behind unasked.** A surface holding it registers a leave guard (`useLeaveGuard`, the org builder's node editor while it has typed changes), and every move to another entry is put to the guard first: a push from code, a link, Back or Forward.
- A guard is handed the destination route and holds only a move that would lose its work. The builder keeps its draft and open editor through a move within the builder (a view or a chart), so its guards let that go (`BuilderContext.keepsTheLens`).
- A replace is never held; it stays on the entry.
- Back has already happened when a page hears of it, so a held one is undone at once and made again only when the reader agrees to lose the work. Every entry carries its session place (`crewletIndex`) beside its scroll key, which tells the router which way to undo.
- The guard that began to hold last is asked first; agreeing asks the next before the move.
- A reload or closed tab gets the browser's own prompt while any guard holds. `useUnloadGuard` asks for that prompt alone, for work a move within the page keeps but a closed tab loses (the builder's draft, in session storage). The page listens for a reload only while something holds, because some browsers keep a page with a `beforeunload` listener out of their back-forward cache.

### Home is the landing screen

`#/` and `#/home` are Home. A reader first wants to know whether anything needs them, but a home that is ONLY that queue renders a healthy company as a blank page, indistinguishable from a broken dashboard.

**So the first fold is the company, then what needs the reader, then what the company did.** That is Home until its reader arranges it (see [Home is the reader's board](#home-is-the-readers-board)). Top to bottom:

- **The greeting.** The reader's morning, by the first word of their OWN
  name as `GET /auth/session` answers it from their directory row (`ownName`)
  — never their seat's, which is the chart's name for a place and often a
  role, so a person with no name was greeted "Good afternoon, Founder"; a
  reader whose row holds no name is greeted without one — and one sentence
  of the engine's: "Nimbus is running on 3 nodes. **3 decisions** are waiting on
  you, 1 condition needs a look, and 4 agents are working right now." The
  decisions figure is weighted; an engine condition — a refused session, a lost
  connection, no configuration, a node that shed its seats — takes the sentence
  over rather than sitting beside it. **Prose never prints a zero as a digit or
  a wrong plural**: "nothing needs your decision", "no agents are working right
  now", "1 condition needs", "2 conditions need" — and a fleet the presence
  read counted as none is "Nimbus is running.", never "on 0 nodes". "N
  conditions need a look" is a link to where they are listed, the Inbox's
  "Needs you" group (opened on the one when there is one). A reader
  nobody bound is told nothing about decisions at all, and before the first
  state arrives nothing about who is working. The **Today · 7 days · 30 days** control
  (`range=`) sets the window every period on Home reads over, the figures,
  Tasks completed, Tokens by team and a section widget's own (Failed turns);
  Today is one company day, cut at the company's midnight by the engine, and
  a longer window opens on the company's midnight that many days back. The choice is kept for
  its reader, so Home opens on it however they come back (see
  [`window=`](#window--one-vocabulary-for-every-time-range)).
- **Five figures** (kit `StatCard`s): *Agents working now* (`working / total`
  from the engine's `activity`, with the state bar of working, waiting,
  stopped and idle, and a sub-line naming only the states somebody is in;
  loading until the first state arrives, never "0 / 0");
  *Waiting on your decision* (the engine's `decisions` count plus the seats
  stopped on their budget that THIS reader can act on — raise the ceiling, a
  `/config` write an admin may make and so may the lead of the
  seat's unit — on a [managed](../concepts/configuration.md#managed-configuration)
  document, only where the reader's credential is one of its writers
  (`mayChangeConfig`) — or hand the item on with
  `update_work_item` — the oldest wait in the warning ink, and **Review**
  into the Inbox's decisions view; a stopped seat the reader can do neither
  about is one of the conditions that "need a look" instead — an em dash and "Not bound to a person" for a reader who is
  nobody); *Tasks in progress* (`work_flow.now.active`, its change over the
  window's length and what is blocked or overdue, with the window's sparkline,
  a fortnight at least);
  *Completed* over the window, against the window before it; and *Tokens* over
  the window, with the **week's** budget meter captioned as the week's ("63% of
  this week's budget · resets Mon") in the engine's own state — or "No weekly
  budget", which links to Company › Budgets for a reader who may change the
  configuration (`mayChangeConfig`: Admin, on a document
  that admits the reader's credential) — who can set one there — and is plain
  text for anybody else. The Tokens tile draws no delta:
  its second line is the budget's, and a bare change in front of it read as a
  claim about the budget. A second line is whole FACTS, so a narrow tile breaks
  between them ("+17 vs 7 days ago" / "· 2 blocked"), never inside one. Each
  figure waits for its own answer and says so; one whose answer has not
  arrived is never a `0`.
- **Needs your decision**, the first three (as many as fit a card given a
  height), newest first, each answerable IN PLACE (`DecisionList`). Asks are
  GROUPED BY WHO IS ASKING: one head, a quiet band, names the asker (the
  seat they asked as, never a credential) with their small face and badge,
  and what every one of their asks shares (the item, the role the reader is
  asked in, how long ago); what differs between
  two asks is said on the ask, and so is the channel an ask promised to post
  its answer to ("answer posted to #releases"). Each question is ONE ROW: the
  question (two lines at most on Home), and under it its key and "Recommended:
  Hold release", with **Accept**, which sends that option, and an outlined
  **Change** at the row's end, centred on the words while the words keep a
  reading width beside them, and under the words, which take the whole row,
  once they do not (the row's own width decides, so long answers such as "Add
  it to the running work" never squeeze the words). No answer's label breaks,
  and a quoted item under the words holds two lines, whole on hover.
  **Change** opens every option as a choice with its detail line and the
  recommended one tagged (the kit's `ChoiceList`), plus **Something else**, whose field (the kit's
  `Composer`, up to 2,000 characters, Enter to send and Shift+Enter for a new line) sends a reply
  instead of a choice; **Submit** sends what is chosen. While the options are
  open the recommendation line is hidden, and only one ask's options are open
  at a time. An ask with no recommendation offers **Answer** in place of
  Accept and Change. A choice is `comment_on_work_item{answers, choice}` and a
  reply `{answers, body}`; the engine wakes the asker with either. An answered
  ask stays as one line, "Answered Hold release (Recommended)", "Answered Ship
  anyway" or "Answered “the reply”", until the card is drawn afresh; there is
  no undo, because the asker is woken the moment the answer lands. An executor parked on a question is answered
  by its turn (`answer_executor`), with how long its box is still held: its row shows
  the question's one sentence, never the context under it, and its **Answer**
  dialog draws the executor's ask as the Inbox does, its options as buttons. A seat the
  engine stopped on a spent budget offers **Raise budget** — a dialog of that
  scope's three ceilings, opened on the seat's own when its own window is the
  one refusing and on the company's when the company's is, with the refusing
  window focused (see [Company › Budgets](#company--budgets-raised-in-place)),
  and **Reassign** of the item it was on. An ask with no options is
  answered in words in place: it says "Asks for a written answer" (what it
  asks for, never "Answered in words", which under an open question read as
  though it had been), and **Answer** opens the field ("Answer CTO") under the
  question and sends `comment_on_work_item{answers, body}`. Every
  control is drawn for every reader and disabled with its reason where this
  browser cannot act. A parked run and a stopped seat sit under the same head
  as an ask, the seat's name said there and not again in the row's title, with
  the item it is on and how long ago beside the name, as an asker's questions
  say theirs. EVERY ROW DRAWS ITS ANSWERS ONE WAY: the first filled
  (**Accept**, **Answer**, **Allow once**, **Raise budget**), the others
  outlined, all at the small size at the row's end. What a row is read from
  (an escalation, a held call's arguments) is a row of its own under the words
  and the answers, across the row's whole width. The
  card's foot, **Show 4 more in Inbox** (**Open inbox** where it lists them
  all), and **Review** both land on `#/inbox`, whose list opens with every one
  of them under Needs you.
- **Live now**: how many seats the engine says are working, and for the
  longest-running four whose turn has an id — the very rows the sidebar's
  Running group names, in its order — what each is on (the item the turn is
  charged to, never a work key), how long, what waits behind it as one quiet
  count, where it is in context → execute → review, and its round and the last
  call it made ("in its box", "round 3 of 24 · sandbox.run go test ./..."), each
  a way into its turn. Every row is one size whatever its turn is doing, the
  elapsed time has a slot of its own, and the card keeps its room for the visit
  as turns finish, so nothing under it moves. **Open live view** for the rest, including a working seat
  whose turn has no id yet: it is counted here and listed there.
- **Code waiting on a person**, where the company hosts code: the changes an
  agent cannot move, for a reader holding Gitlet. For anybody else the card,
  its header and **Open Gitlet** stay, "Seeing Gitlet's changes needs Gitlet
  access. An admin can give it to you." stands in place of both halves, and
  neither listing is asked, as Tasks completed does for Worklet; until the
  viewer has answered, both halves draw as loading and never say "none". Two halves, the first three changes each of two of the
  engine's own listings keeps: *Asking your review* (`code_changes?needs=review`, which names no
  reviewer and so asks the reader's own seat; a reader bound to no seat is
  told a review is asked of a seat, and asked nothing) and *Waiting on a
  person* (`needs=person`: a change whose first unmet precondition only a
  person can settle — a person's approval, a blocker a person raised), each
  row its reference, title, state pill and the sentence its readiness leads
  with, opening the change in the peek. Three rows, as Needs your decision
  draws, and **Open Gitlet** is Gitlet › Changes narrowed to what waits on a
  person. A
  listing is a page the engine read, never a total, so the card counts
  nothing; and a page is the rows it read, not the rows it kept (a change of
  a repository the reader may not read, one that has ended, one whose
  readiness no longer waits on a person is dropped after the read), so an
  empty page can still carry `next`. Each half follows `next` until it holds
  its three or the listing ends, for at most four pages a poll
  (`CHANGES_FILL_PAGES`), and says it found none only of a listing that
  ended: a half that stops at that bound first draws what it found, or, with
  nothing found, says none was among the newest read and links to the rest
  in Gitlet. A half that found none says so on one line; when both halves
  were asked and both ended with nothing, the card says it once, one empty
  state ("Nothing waits on a person") in place of the two halves, rather than
  a line under one half beside a full empty state under the other.
- **Tasks completed** per company day over the window, with the window's total
  (today in the accent), **Tokens by team** over the window (tokens, never money), each
  team's bar split by the seats that spent in it and keyed under the bar (the
  engine's `parts`; a team of more than four seats names its three biggest and
  draws the rest as one part in the residual hue), and
  **Projects**: each project's done, active and to-do work as one bar, its
  lead and its target date.
- **Recent activity** (`company_feed`): work delivered ("approved on first
  review", "1 turn · 38.2k tokens"), filed ("from Slack", off the create's own
  origin), handed on ("hand-off 1 of 8"), pages published and schedules run —
  Everything, Completed, Hand-offs or Schedules (`feed=`) — with Load older,
  and the full event log a link away. A schedule's rows are its RUNS, and the
  engine folds a schedule's consecutive runs into one ("Schedule backlog-sweep
  ran 12 times for PM", "since 02:40"): a tick it skipped is never a row that
  says "ran", and a frequent schedule never buries the work under a page of
  itself. Each row's sentence comes from ONE table (`FEED_PHRASES` in
  `routes/home/model.ts`) keyed on the feed's own kinds. On a phone a row is a
  three-column grid — time, mark, sentence — whose sentence wraps inside its
  own column with the aside under it, so a row that wraps and one that does not
  keep the same alignment.

**Home leaves out what cannot arrive.** Where the company does not run Worklet (see [the sidebar](#the-sidebar)), the *Tasks in progress* and *Completed* figures, **Tasks completed** and **Projects** are neither drawn nor offered in the tray, and New task leaves the page bar: a zero tile would claim a tracker that answered nothing. Where it hosts no code, **Code waiting on a person** is neither drawn nor offered. Decisions, conditions, Live now and tokens arrive under every backend and stay.

Five tiles sit in a row while the page column holds them (five at their 176px floor plus four 16px board gaps = 944px, so the figures' gutters stand on the gutters of the blocks below), then three over two, then one on a phone; the board's blocks stack below the same width. All are measured from the SCREEN's column (`@container page`), which the shell declares on its content as well as its header, because the sidebar and an open peek take their share of the window first.

#### Home is the reader's board

**Edit Home**, in the page bar, turns the page into a board on a fine hatch: drag a widget to move it, drag its corner (a group, its edge) to resize on twelve columns and 16px rows, group widgets under a coloured heading that folds away, add widgets from a tray. While arranged, the page bar holds the editor alone: unsaved-change count, Undo and Redo (Mod+Z and Mod+Shift+Z, the key table's `draft.*` rows), Add widgets, Cancel, Done. New task steps aside until Done.

- **A draft, kept on Done.** Nothing is stored until Done. Cancel with changes asks before discarding, and so does leaving the page. Folding a group outside editing is kept at once: a choice about the page, not a layout change to confirm.
- **The tray** offers Home's own cards (one each: two "Needs your decision" cards would be one decision drawn twice), a single figure, a shortcut to any page, the reader's own notes, headings, dividers and links, and every section's widgets under its sidebar name in the sidebar's order, with a search. A widget with a choice to make (saved view, project, agent) opens a sheet first, with a step back to the tray beside its title and **Add to Home** at its end, disabled until the choice is made; nothing is added until then.
- **A section offers its own widgets.** Each lives in a `home.widgets.tsx` beside the section's screens (`dashboard/src/routes/<section>/`), exporting `widgets = defineWidgets([...])` from `routes/home/board/kit.tsx`; the registry finds every such file at build time, so a new section offers widgets by adding that one file.
  - A widget names the page it summarises by its `DESTINATIONS` key, and takes from it the tray section, the access that opens it and where its card's foot goes. A reader whose access does not open the page is never offered the widget (the tray says how many were held back); one who loses that access later sees a sentence in its place, never the data.
  - Whatever stands in a widget's place (that sentence, a widget that could not be drawn, the failed read of who the reader is, with Try again) keeps the widget's own name as the card's title, so a Home whose every read failed still says which card is which.
  - A widget asks the same questions its page asks and only reads; every write stays on the page.
  - A contribution naming no such page is left out and reported, and `board/registry.test.ts` fails the build on it.
- **A widget never says "nothing" over an answer that could not account for everything.** An answer says when it is short: a record this build cannot read met the read (`complete: false`), or a node did not answer a fleet read (`coverage`). `WidgetQuery` in `routes/home/board/kit.tsx` decides it in one place, over the gaps `gapsOf` reads from every answer a widget draws and the widget's own lines (a muted room, a list cut at its bound).
  - A claim ("You're caught up", "No turn failed in the last 24 hours") is drawn only over an answer with no gap. With a gap and no rows the card says there is nothing to list and why it may be wrong; with rows it says the gap under them.
  - A figure says "May be incomplete" on its second line; a count stopped at its ceiling is written as the floor it is ("50+").
  - A count another surface already says is read from that surface's reading, never the widget's own page: the Inbox card's is the sidebar badge's (`useInboxCounts`), so the two never differ.
  - A widget that follows one thing reads it by its key, never by finding it in a listing page: the Project widget and a pinned project ask `work_project`, so a project past the first page is still the one chosen; a picker whose list the engine cut says so.
  - Every widget module and every card Home's own widgets draw goes through `WidgetQuery`, not `QueryState` or `EmptyState` (`board/kit.test.tsx` holds it); `board/widgets.render.test.tsx` answers every widget's questions short and holds each to saying so.
- **Kept on the engine, under the reader's seat**, so the same person sees the same Home in every browser and on every device (`board/kept.ts`): read through `home_board`, saved through `save_home_board`. A seat's next holder inherits it, and it is forgotten a grace after the seat leaves the chart, as chat read state is. A sign-in that holds no seat keeps its board in this browser.
  - **Every save names the revision it edited.** Done saves at the revision editing started from; a board saved from another browser or device in between is refused, and Home asks: keep editing, use the other one, or replace it with yours. A group folded outside editing is laid again on the newer board without asking.
  - **This browser keeps the last answer** (`STORAGE_KEYS.homeBoard`), drawn on a cold load until the engine answers, so Home never flashes the shipped board. A board an earlier build kept only in this browser moves onto the engine the first time Home loads, where the engine holds none; where it holds one, the engine's is the board and the browser's copy is dropped.
  - Read back as untrusted input wherever it comes from: every field checked, every string capped, every link held to a `#/` or `https://` address. A widget whose section no longer offers it keeps its place and says so. A board past 512 KiB as JSON is not sent, and Home says so.
- **A widget never scrolls.** A list widget's rows are `WidgetList` (`routes/home/board/kit.tsx`, over the kit's `fit` List): at its content's height it draws its first few rows; given a height, it draws every row it read (`WIDGET_PAGE`) and shows those that fit whole, measured again whenever the card is resized, never half a row. Its card's foot is one slim row that opens the page ("Open Executors", "Open inbox") and counts what the card left out ("+4 more", "20+ more" where the read stopped at its page). Home's own cards fit the same way: sized, the reader's own decisions take the room before those waiting on others, an ask being answered stands alone until it is answered or closed, and a note (the reader's own words, not rows) scrolls rather than being cut. `board/kit.test.tsx` holds every widget module to `WidgetList` rather than a bare `List`.
- **Links open in a new tab while Home is arranged**, so following one never leaves an unsaved board. At rest they behave as everywhere else.
- **A short card beside a tall one leaves no hole.** The board is packed (the kit's `ArrangeGrid` `pack`): each card starts under the nearest card above it in its columns, measured from its real height, so the cards after a short one fill its column beside a tall one. The reader's order is kept (no card lands above one before it), cards whose feet are a step apart start the next cards level, and a card sized by its content reaches down to the next card in its columns, so columns end together; a card given a height keeps it. A group's cards pack the same way inside it.
- **Below the stacking width** (944px of the page's own column) every block spans the page and cannot be resized.
- **No star in Home's bar.** Home is the sidebar's first row and has no sections whose bar a disabled star would hold steady (`WorkspaceRow.starless`), so the bar carries Edit Home instead.
### The Inbox is where you act

The Inbox lists what waits on the person (questions put to them, runs parked on them, seats they can unblock), then what reached them. Two columns, each its own scroller: the list, and the open item read in full with its answer. Every visual part is the kit's (`InboxList` and `ReadingPane` in `@crewlethq/ui`); the screen only places them.

**One list, in a fixed order, with no filter bar.**
- **Needs you** leads: asks put to this person and executors parked on a question to them (`decisions`, the read Home's figure counts), seats stopped on a spent token budget, unread notices that an item of theirs is not moving (reason `flow`, counted in the frame's figure until read), and conditions a person decides (`lib/attention.ts`, subjects whose home is `seat`). A notice the engine wrote is answered on the task's conversation ("Comment on ENG-4"), never to the engine.
- **Updates** follows: unread arrivals (`inbox{unread, snoozed: exclude}`, tracker and Gitlet notices interleaved by time) as a closed, counted group ("Updates 12") with the same disclosure as Answered. It is closed on every visit, because what waits on the reader comes first. Opened, its rows step with `j` and `k`, and a link naming one opens it. Mark all read, the Snoozed link, the frame's badge and Home's Updates count the same updates open or not.
- Decisions are never interleaved with updates by time, which would rank "a task you watch moved" above the CEO asking whether to hold a release.
- An ask is ONE row: its notice rides on the decision, not under Updates, and answering marks it read.
- Two quiet links end the list, **N snoozed** and **Earlier updates**, not a scope or chip at the top (a filter bar is read every time). The snoozed count is read whether or not its list is open (`snoozed: only`); Earlier is read only once opened (`unread: false`, of which the read ones are listed). Both page forward fifty at a time with **Show more**.
- Home's **Review** and **Open inbox** land on `#/inbox`, whose list opens with every decision they counted.
- A change the person made themselves is never an update: they write as the seat the inbox is kept under.

**Every item has its own address** under `#/inbox`, which carries ids alone: `ask/<comment>`, `run/<turn>` (an executor's open question, whichever it asks now) and `run/<turn>/<launch>` (one it answered), `seat/<seat>`, `condition/<id>`, `notice/<record>`, `change/<record>/<change>` and `artifact/<record>`. An ask keeps its address once answered; `run/<turn>` opens the question the executor answered last once none is open.
- Every row is a real link: a modified or middle press opens a tab, and the link copies.
- Opening an item (press, Enter, `j`, `k`) pushes, so Back and Forward step between items read; the screen's own moves (next item after an answer, an address said another way) replace.
- Beside the list, `#/inbox` opens the first item not yet dealt with and takes its address in place, so Back leaves the inbox in one step. An empty inbox and the narrow screen's list stay `#/inbox`.
- The address works in a new tab, after a reload and on another device, wherever the item is now: an answered, put-off, snoozed or read item opens its group, and a notice no loaded page holds is read by id (`inbox{record, snoozed: include}`, from the reader's own record). One that resolves nowhere says "This item is not in your inbox" in the pane.
- On a narrow screen the address opens the item alone; its Back returns to the list.
- A `?row=` address is replaced by the item's own.

**Every row says the same three things.**
- Who: the seat behind it, with its avatar. A person's change is drawn as the seat the engine recorded it under; one by a credential bound to no seat (author kind `operator`: a Tier A token's session or a service account, never a person, who holds a human seat) under its own login, the name the record carries (`iam.ActorFor`), never a secret; one the engine made itself (`system`) reads "The engine" with the engine's mark. Never the credential a change came through (`operator_id`).
- What, in up to three lines, never cut at the edge: the question; the stop ("The daily token budget is spent", with **stopped** after the name in the danger ink); a run's question (with **executor** after the name); or what an update did ("Mentioned you") with its excerpt after it in the quiet ink.
- The task it is about, as a quiet link under the row: its key and title (one `work_items{key}` read resolves every row's title), the title omitted where it IS the row's question (an ask filed with its task, `create_work_item{ask}`, asks in the task's title). A plain click opens the task in the frame's side panel, a modified one its page.

An excerpt the engine COMPOSED names its author by name as the head does ("maya-ops put LEAD-3 …" reads "Maya Ops put LEAD-3 …"); a comment's excerpt is somebody's own words, left as typed. Unread is heavier; the open row takes the neutral pressed fill (never the accent, which made rows read as alerts) and is the one row marked current.

**The pane reads one item top to bottom, with nothing to open.** One sentence says who is asking, what is asked and on which task ("CTO asks for your approval on LEAD-12 Q4 release plan", the task by key alone where its title is the question); the time is on the row. Then the question in large type; its context (for an ask filed with its task, the task's description, read for the pane, since the engine files the ask's body as the title and the asker's words as the description); the asker's reasoning on an inset ground ("CTO recommends **Hold release**") with the evidence it cites (a task, page, turn trace, executor or link). An update's pane names what it did as its heading, quotes a comment whole under it, and says why it reached the reader where the heading does not ("· you follow this task", "· snoozed until …").

**A code notice is an intent-first card.** It is listed only to a reader holding Gitlet: the engine lists, counts and pushes none to anybody else (ADR-0110), so their Inbox holds Worklet's half alone, nothing locked in its place, and **Mark all read** sends Worklet's `mark_inbox` alone. A code notice still on screen after the reader loses Gitlet keeps Mark as read and Snooze, saying "This change needs Gitlet access. An admin can give it to you.", and `code_mark_inbox` is never sent.
- A notice Gitlet routed is a row named by its change (`web!42`), the code mark as badge, the change's title as its line, what the record said after it, and as the row's task the work item the change implements.
- Opened, the card says what the change is FOR before what happened to it: its title, "For" the work item, the opening of its author's description ("…" where the engine cut it at a kibibyte), then what the record said, quoted.
- **Where it stands** follows: the engine's one sentence on where a live change's merge stands ("no approval counts on revision 2: it waits on ada"), or for a change that merges nothing its state pill (Merged, Closed); then the open findings seats raised, heaviest first ("Open agent findings: Blocker 1 · Nit 2"), in words, never a hue.
- **Open the diff** is one press to the change's page on its Files changed tab.
- The byline's note says why it reached the reader in Gitlet's words ("asked for your review", "asked to look again"), never the tracker's.
- The LIST ASKS NOTHING per card: it asks the engine for its rows' cards (`inbox{cards: true}`), read once the page is composed, no older than the page, readiness judged for the reader there (`gitlet.NoticeChange`), so a page of fifty cards is one question and no card describes its change as it stood before the row beside it. Snoozed and Earlier ask once each is opened; the badge's count, Home's Updates and the Snoozed link's count draw no card and ask for none, so a read behind every screen judges no merge gate.
- **Its gate** is read for the ONE card open, only for a live change: `code_change` (readiness judged for the reader, and its revisions' facts) and `code_checks` of the change at each check's latest attempt (`latest`, every page, drawn only once whole), so the card never rebuilds a check's standing from history.
- The gate says: what the head revision's REQUIRED checks measured, each one's state and duration (never tokens), only where the readiness judges a `check` precondition; the head revision's change classes (how many touched paths change only whitespace or only comments, and that the rest change code, where every path was classified); and the human paths that asked for THIS reader (the `human_approval` precondition's sentence where unmet and waiting on them). A change into an ungated branch draws no gate.
- Reviewing is the change's own page's; the card's controls are the reader's marks.

**A comment on an artifact is a row and a card of the same parts.** Its row reads "Maya Ops commented on Q3 plan" (or resolved, or reopened), the artifact drawn as a task's key is (its kind's glyph and title), the remark beneath as plain words, never markup. Its card names the artifact, linked the same way, and why it reached the reader ("On your artifact", "Mentioned you", "In a thread you're in", "For your work item"), quotes the remark, and from the list's card the text the commenter selected, whether the thread is open or resolved and by whom, and how many remarks it holds. **Open the thread** goes to `#/artifacts/<id>?panel=comments&thread=<thread>`. Marks go through `artifact_mark_inbox`, every reader's, since commenting is a relation and no app; **Mark all read** sends one mark per domain the page read, each through the newest of that domain's notices on it.

**An ask is answered in one press, through the one write every surface uses.**
- The pane draws `AnswerAsk` in its `buttons` layout: each option SENDS that choice (`comment_on_work_item{item, answers, choice}`), the recommended one first and filled, all through ONE write so a second choice cannot be sent while the first is in flight.
- **Something else** opens the field in their place and sends the answer in words (`{item, answers, body}`); an ask with no options is answered in that field from the start. The field is worded as an answer ("Answer CTO"), never an instruction to the asker.
- Where the ask promised a channel (`decision.inform`) the line under the answer says "Your answer is also posted to #channel" (the engine holds the asker to it, `ExternalNotification.owes`); otherwise no such line.
- A parked executor's pane is drawn as a question is (ADR-0068): its one-sentence question heads it with inline references placed, its context as Markdown, its recommendation with reasoning and cited evidence, its options as buttons (recommended first and filled) with "Something else" to answer in words; an open question is answered in its field. It says how long the box is still held and answers by its turn (`answer_executor`). A question from an older build (one free-text block) draws its first sentence as the heading and the rest as Markdown; nothing is quoted verbatim.
- A stopped seat's pane names the window that is spent and offers two ways out: raise the ceiling, or hand the item on. A condition's says what it costs to leave and where the answer is.

**What is answered moves to Answered, and the next item opens.**
- An answered question or run leaves Needs you at once for the head of the **Answered** group, marked **Answered** in its head (a soft success tag where the time was) with the answer under the question ("You chose **Hold release**", or what was written, with a speech mark), in full ink and never struck through (a strike reads as "cancelled" and cuts through words a reader comes back to check). What was written (a reply, the note beside a choice, a withdrawal's reason) is Markdown, drawn as the conversation draws it: one paragraph quoted in the line, anything more (a list, a second paragraph) under it. The row's line stops at three lines with an ellipsis where it is drawn, never cut in its source; the pane quotes the words whole.
- The next item opens in the pane at once, the group stays closed and counts it, and one polite announcement says both ("Answered. Next: …"). A second press on an answered row moves the reader no further.
- An answer accepted and not yet settled stays where it stood, shown as sent, until it settles. Needs you's count is what is still open.
- A read or snoozed update shows its new state, and 700 ms later (`ADVANCE_MS`) the next item opens, unless the reader has moved on.
- The next item is never a row in a closed group: with Needs you empty and Updates closed, the pane says **All clear**.
- Every item opens at its head: whatever scrolls the pane returns to the row's top, whether an answer, a click, `j`, `k` or a link opened it.

**What was answered before waits in a closed group.** The asks put to the reader and closed in the last week, and the executors' questions the reader answered themselves (`answered_decisions`), are an **Answered** group after Updates, closed and counted ("Answered 4"); its label is a disclosure button inside the heading, so a reader moving by heading lands on it and Enter opens it.
- Each row names who asked, the question, and who answered and how ("Maya Ops chose **Ship anyway**"), since a colleague may answer a question put to you.
- An executor's question the reader answered is a row of the same group: its pane reads the run's ask in full (question, context, options with the chosen one marked) and links to the run, with no conversation, since a run's question has no thread.
- A row answered on this visit is in Needs you, never both. Opened, its rows step with `j` and `k`; a link to one opens the group.
- An answered ask's pane reads like the one it was answered on, with the answer in place of the buttons, a line saying who answered for you where it was not you, **What happened next** as four steps (asked, answered, picked up, acted on: the last two from the asker's seat as it is now and its first record on the task since, a paused or stopped seat marked for attention), and the conversation with a reply box.

**The conversation is the last part of the reading.** Labelled by what it holds: "Replies to this question" under an ask, "Replies to this comment" under an update about a comment (quoted above, so not listed again unless the update carries only a preview), "Conversation on this task" under any other update.
- Read a page at a time from `work_comments`, the newest page polled; **Earlier comments** reads the page before. A reply thread is narrowed by the engine (`thread`), so the button appears only when that conversation has earlier comments; an empty one reads as its heading, "No replies yet." and the reply box.
- A comment's author is the seat a person wrote it as (the engine records it so); one by a credential bound to no seat is drawn under its own login; none reads "The engine"; never the credential.
- The reply box writes as you: `comment_on_work_item{item, body, reply_to}`, which answers nothing. `@` opens a picker over the org that writes `@handle` into the text (the engine resolves mentions from the body, so the picker never sends a list that could disagree); `#` links another task (`update_work_item{linked}`); the paperclip attaches a page, an existing one or new text saved (`write_page`) then attached (`linked_pages`). `Mod+Enter` sends.
- A question answered in words has no second box: its own field above is the answer.

**Every mark is a gesture on exactly what it names, and only an update has them.**
- **Mark as read** marks the open update read and turns into **Mark as unread**.
- **Snooze** offers an hour from now, tomorrow at 09:00, next Monday at 09:00 on the company's clock (each moment once, so a Sunday has no second Monday), or a picked moment; ONLY presets inside the engine's `max_snooze_ahead` (from `work_person`) are offered, since the write refuses the rest.
- A question, run, seat and condition carry none: each leaves the inbox when answered or cleared.
- **Mark all read** is `read_through` at the newest update LOADED: one that arrived after the page was drawn is unseen.
- None sends the inbox back whole (the replaced write did, so a Done in one tab erased a snooze made in another).

**What the list says when it is empty is derived from the answer**, never from the row count: nothing answered yet and a refusal draw no sentence, and "you are caught up" (the person's own `seen_through` watermark exists) is told from "nothing has reached you yet". With nothing left to open in a list that holds rows, the pane says **All clear**; beside an empty list, whose own empty state says so, the pane holds one quiet line ("New updates open here.").

**Two panes on a wide screen, one on a narrow one.** Both columns are present from the first paint and the first item not yet dealt with is open until the reader picks one, so the pane is never an empty box beside a non-empty list. Stepping down the list, or `j` and `k`, replaces history. Under 640px of the SCREEN's width the list is the screen and an item opens in its place, with Back at the start of its byline: on a phone, and beside Ask Crewlet, whose column can leave a desktop window a phone's width. On a phone the page scrolls as a whole; beside Ask Crewlet the screen fills the window and the one pane scrolls itself.

**Three viewer states, three sentences.** A reader with no credential, a reader whose credential no seat claims, and a bound reader. The unbound reader is a token's session or a service account (never a person, who always holds a seat) and is told what binding its row to a human seat would add (`crewlet iam bind`, or a row created with `-seat`). The conditions a person decides are listed for all three; a person's updates and decisions need a credential bound to their seat; every write control is drawn for all three, disabled with the reason.

**Without Worklet the Inbox stays.** Seats stopped on a spent budget, conditions a person decides and comments on artifacts arrive under every backend, so the Inbox is never hidden with Worklet (see [the sidebar](#the-sidebar)): it draws those, and its updates are the comments and, where the company hosts code, Gitlet's. The asks are Worklet's notices.

**A growth decision is decided on its card.** An agent's held spend, publish or account administration call (`ad_spend`, `public_post`, `account_admin`) opens in the reading pane as the engine's card (`GET /mcp-approvals/{id}`'s `card`), never as its arguments: the account with its currency and zone; each change before and after, money in the account's currency; for spend, the account's daily budgets against both caps and the vendor's own rule on spending past a budget; for publishing, every text whole under the review it answers (its stars, author and an excerpt) with its length against the vendor's limit and any reply it replaces, a batch of up to ten allowed or denied together, and a change customers see (a live listing's edit, a delete) as the fields it changes; the vendor's findings, the agent's reason and when the ask lapses. It is answered **Allow once** or **Deny** at a fresh sign-in with an optional note back to the agent, never Always allow. A target that moved holds Allow once, since allowing it would run nothing, and keeps Deny so the agent asks again; a lapsed ask is expired; any act that cannot be undone waits for a tick; an amount whose currency the vendor did not name is never drawn and cannot be allowed there. A refused answer reads the call again, so the card says where it stands. A call whose card could not be read (its vendor did not answer) is decided on the call itself, its question and every argument, Allow once or Deny. A decision row elsewhere opens the same card in a dialog (**Review and decide**). A person allows what they read, so every name and text wraps and none is cut.

### My work is one person's day

`#/me` is everything one person is expected to look at, as the SECTIONS of the page header: **Queue**, **Asked of me**, **Asked by me**, **Unblocked**, **Collaborating**, **Watching** and **Checklist** (the tracker's) and, where the company hosts code, **Reviews**.
- Every tracker tab carries the engine's own count of its claim (`work_my_work`'s `totals`, or `total_hint` for the two that are the work list), a floor (`20+`) only where the engine stopped counting, absent while its read is in flight, drawn at zero rather than hidden.
- A section holds at most twenty rows of its claim, and one holding fewer than its count says which ones.
- The page opens straight on its sections, no explanatory paragraph; each empty section says in its own words what would fill it.

**Each section names its own service and permission; the page names none.** Every section but Reviews is a question about work items: it needs Worklet and is hidden where the company does not run it. Reviews takes Gitlet (`grants: ["gitlet"]`, ADR-0110) and is hidden where the company hosts no code; for a reader without Gitlet it is locked beside Worklet's tabs, and `#/me/reviews` draws the frame's one refusal ("You need Gitlet access") and asks nothing. So My work is hidden, never locked, only where the company runs neither (see [the sidebar](#the-sidebar)).
- A Gitlet holder lands on Reviews where Worklet is not theirs (Worklet's sections locked beside it) and where the company runs no Worklet.
- A Worklet holder without Gitlet finds Reviews locked beside the Queue.
- A reader who can open none finds the row locked, naming what would open it: "needs Worklet or Gitlet access" where the company runs both, Worklet alone where it hosts no code, Gitlet alone where it runs no Worklet.

**Reviews is Gitlet's claims on the person**: the changes asking their review (`code_changes?needs=review&reviewer=`), then their own changes waiting on their fix: a reviewer asked for changes, or a finding stands that no author answered (`needs=fix&owner=`). Each is Gitlet › Changes' own grid over the engine's listing, held to the reader's grant on every repository, paged with Load more, each row opening its change in the peek.
- Its tab carries no count: a listing of changes is a page the engine read, not a total it kept.
- On a reader Worklet does not answer, Reviews asks none of Worklet's questions, so no refusal is drawn over Gitlet's answer.
- A reader bound to no seat, on their own day, is asked nothing (a review is asked of a seat, a change owned by one), and Reviews says so instead of drawing the engine's refusal of a login as a handle.

**Every figure for one person's day counts one named thing.** The Queue's is the open work ASSIGNED to the person, the same reading as the sidebar's My work figure on your own day, so the two cannot disagree. Questions put to you have their own tab. The priorities reading, below, says above its first row what IT counts, because it is a different list.

**Two sections are the work list, held to the person.** The Queue is `ItemsView` with the ASSIGNEE locked (its shapes, Filter, Display, scope, grouping and count line, opening banded by the engine's `due:bucket`). Asked by me is the same list with the ASKER locked, opening on every status (`asked_by=` alone: a question is recorded under its asker's own record name, the seat for a person and the login for a credential bound to none, so one name finds every question they asked, and no question accepts a `viewer=`). A lock is not a chip and not a key on the address: it is what the section IS.

**The Queue's other reading is the order somebody put it in** (`order=priorities`): the person's stored list, numbered, never re-sorted, reordered by dragging a row or with `Alt` and an arrow on a focused row.
- It is a list somebody WROTE and can name a task a colleague holds, so it is not the set the Queue's tab counts. Its first line says how many open tasks it holds and how many are assigned to the person ("5 open tasks on your list, in the order to work them — 2 of them assigned to you. The Queue counts only the work assigned to you.").
- The write is `set_priorities` as the reader, carrying the WHOLE stored list with the moved row at its new place (entries the page does not draw keep theirs) and `if_match` the record's version. The row sits at its new place with a pending mark until the engine answers; a refusal puts it back in the engine's words.
- Nothing is optimistic, and nothing else moves while the write is out: the next move is held, but every row keeps its grip, so the list does not step sideways and back.
- A person's seat page counts the same list as **Priorities** in its "Their day" card, never as their Queue: the Queue is the open work assigned to them, everywhere it is named.

**Asked of me is the decision list Home draws** (`DecisionList`): asks grouped under who asked, each with its recommendation, Accept and Change. It is shared, so how an ask is answered is one rule.

The whose-day picker in the page bar lists yours, then your line, then anybody, each on two lines (the name, then the handle and how much is open on that desk); its panel is tall enough for six before it scrolls. Every list row is the same height whether or not somebody holds its task: the holder's cell keeps a badge's height with nobody in it.

**Whose day it is decides the pronoun and the controls.** The picker names whose day is on screen; a note above the sections carries the stamp, by the person's name, when somebody else put the queue in order; no row repeats the seat's chip, handle or "yours" (a seat's page is reached from Company › Structure). On somebody ELSE's day every row speaks about them ("Rui is the approver") and every change on the page is HELD (`HoldWrites`): drawn, disabled, and explained once above the rows, because the questions put to them are theirs to answer and their work is changed from the work screens. The one change released is a LEAD's reorder (anybody above them in the chart, as Worklet defines a lead), and the page says before the press that the person is told when the reader reorders.

### A task's page is one reading
