`#/worklet/{KEY}` is the approved Issue artboard: a reading column and a rail beside it, each its own scroller and flush with the sheet (the page asks the shell for the window's height, as the Inbox does, and gives it back below a phone's width, where the rail follows the column in one scroller). There is no header card: the page bar's trail names the project by its name with its key as a chip ("Worklet › ENG Core platform › ENG-412"). The bar carries ↑ ↓ "3 of 18" when the task was opened from a list (by its row's link or through the peek's **Open**, which carries the list the peek was opened from), with `k` and `j` stepping to the task before and after (the list's own two keys, standing aside while a grid on the page holds them), **Watch live** while a turn is running on it, Restore for a task in the trash, and a menu with **Open on the board**.

**A task a change carries out has a Changes tab.** Where the company hosts code and the reader holds Gitlet (a reader without it is asked nothing and keeps the task's one tab, since a lock would say a change stands behind it), the page asks the engine for one change naming the task as its work item (`code_changes?work=native:<id>&limit=1`, every state), and only once it finds one does the column open with a **Task | Changes** strip (`tab=changes`).
- A page is the rows the engine read, not the rows it kept: a change of a repository the reader may not read, or deleted and not yet purged, is dropped after the read, so an empty page can still carry `next`. The probe follows `next` until it keeps one change, for at most four pages; a probe that stops there with `next` still set opens the strip too, since a change may lie behind it.
- A task no change names carries no strip, so a company that proposes its code elsewhere never sees a tab that always says nothing; an address naming the tab before the answer lands on the task.
- Changes lists every change of the task, merged and closed as well as open, in Gitlet › Changes' own grid, paged with Load more, each row opening its change in the peek. The rail stays beside both tabs. The activity filter's **Changes** is the task's own history, a different thing.

**The address follows the task.** A move to another project re-keys a task and its old key still opens it, so a page opened at a key the task no longer holds (or at its id, while it has a key) replaces the address with the one it answers to now (`lib/work.ts`'s `movedAddress`), and the trail names the project the task is in.

**A task in the trash reads only.** The engine freezes a tombstoned task (no comment, body, field or relation changes until a restore), so its page offers none: the trash note is its one mark ("In the trash. Moved to the trash by Jane Founder just now. Restore it to change it.", the author by name), with Restore in the page bar, and no editor, comment box, Reply or answer.

**The column is the task in the order a person reads one.**
- The exceptional flags only (blocked, archived; the trash is its note above).
- The title (24px, edited in place).
- The description as prose under a section heading drawn for a reader who moves by headings (its own headings render a level below, so "## Context" is an h3 that needs an h2 above it), edited as its markdown.
- Each named checklist ("Done when") as boxes a writer ticks.
- The sub-tasks as a card whose head is "1 / 3" and a meter, each row the child's status mark, key, title and holder, with a **+** that files a new one under this task. A failed sub-tree read is drawn where the rows would have been (a refusal that drew nothing would say there are no sub-tasks).
- A status mark is drawn in the artboards' own shapes, so state reads by shape as well as hue, everywhere a task is drawn: an empty ring for to do, a half-filled ring for in progress, three quarters for in review, a filled check for done, a struck ring for cancelled, a quiet disc for closed.

**Activity is one timeline read down**, over three histories each read a page at a time (`work_activity` for what changed, `work_comments` for what was said, `work_item_turns` for the agent turns charged to the task), merged only down to the newest point any of them with more pages stopped at, so a stretch it draws is complete in all three; **Earlier activity** reads the history that stopped there. All | Comments | Agent turns | Changes narrows it.
- Each history stays whole while its newest page moves under a reader who paged back (`lib/usePaged.ts`, which a seat's Turns tab pages through too): an arrival at the top pushes the newest page's oldest entry off its foot, so before the list moves the range between the newest page and the pages held is read and spliced in; until then the list stays as drawn. A gap longer than everything paged back through, or one a read failed on, drops the older pages instead, so the reader pages back again from a list with no hole.
- A change is a sentence about the task ("Jane Founder filed this in ENG", "CTO assigned it to SWE: “owns the provisioner”", "Jane Founder ticked 1 on Acceptance — 1 of 4 done", "Jane Founder moved it to the trash"); "changed" goes only before a field's delta, since a kind with nothing to compare is its own verb phrase. A quiet **· Who this reached ›** at the end of its line opens its routing: the reason each person was woken, whether it asked anything, and the three different empty answers in three sentences.
- A comment is a card with its ask, answer or choice and a **Reply** (says something without answering), under its author and the day and minute written. An open ask put to the reader is answered on its own card; an ask with no options says what it asks for ("Asks for a written answer") over **Answer**, never a second Reply.
- Comment prose keeps a reading measure of about seventy characters while a table or code block takes the card's whole width, and a report's headings step it into sections. A comment much longer than a screenful is folded behind **Show more** (the kit's `Clamp`), except the newest; a focus landing in a folded comment opens it.
- Once the thread runs to six entries the head offers **Jump to latest**, which brings the newest entry into view and moves focus to it, with the box to answer it under it.
- A turn is the artboard's card: "SWE ran turn 1", its phases as checked steps (the one a failed turn broke in wears a cross in the danger tone, its pill saying "failed in review"), a pill for a send-back ("sent back for another pass") or a park, what it did in the agent's own words (a turn that failed or parked before writing an account says "No summary. See the trace." in one quiet line), the reviewer's request on the raised rung with the caution ink on its mark, the tools it called as chips ("comment_on_work_item ×4"), and under them, on a line of its own read from the left, its wall time, tokens and **Trace**. The number is the TASK's count of turns, so the newest card and the cost panel agree.
- While a seat's turn is running on this task (joined on the item the engine charges it to, and only while the seat is `working`) the foot of the timeline is the live row in the working state's own ground ("SWE is on turn 3 · executing · for 2m", its pulse static under reduced motion) linking to the live trace. Its words after the turn come from one derivation shared with the task card's strip (the round counted from one, as the stepper counts it, and the phase named: "reading context", "reviewing", "executing"), so the card, the row and the seat's profile never name different rounds of one turn.
- The composer is last: a comment, a reply, or **Ask…**, a question put to one seat, optionally with two to four options, the one recommended and whether the answer is the decision or an input to it.

**The rail is the task's fields, each the control that changes it.** Status, priority, assignee (with **Reassign**, whose dialog asks why), reporter, project, type, labels (the project's declared set), due and start, the estimate, then any custom fields and the record (created, updated, in status since, filed into).
- A field drawn as its value is named by that value first, then by what it changes ("In review, Status of ENG-42"), here and in a list's cells alike: a person who says what they see must reach it.
- A row a change touched after the task was filed says who last set it, named as the person the activity names (the seat the engine recorded it under, as is the reporter); the create itself draws no line, because the reporter row and the record already say who filed it and when.
- Then the relations ("Part of LEAD-12 2.4 release" first, then each link named from this end), the pages it cites by title, **What this task has cost** (turns, tokens and agent time from the task's own counters, tokens only, never money) with the hand-offs against the engine's budget, and who is watching: the kit's avatar stack under the section's label, one size and one overlap for people and agents alike, named once ("Watching: Jane Founder, SWE and CTO"), with **Watch** / **Unwatch** at the end of its row.
- The rail starts on the main column's own top line, so its first field stands level with the title.

**Every change is made as you, and never hidden.** The fields share one `update_work_item` and one refusal line, conditional on the version the page was drawn from, so a race lost names who won it; a checklist tick and following are gestures and carry no version. A reader who cannot act sees every value as a value, every button disabled with its reason, and the reason said once above the title.

The peek (`peek=item:{KEY}`) is the same page in one 420px column: the task's identity as its head, the rail above the body, and no cost or record.

### Structure is the company running

`#/company/org` is **Structure**: one sidebar row (`g a`), two underline tabs over one org builder (`routes/org/Structure.tsx`): the **Org chart** (`#/company/org`, default) and the **Table** (`#/company/org/table`), whose tab counts the seats it draws (a lead's: the units they lead) once the org has arrived. Both show the live company (seat state, status filter, and on the Table run-time controls) and both change the organization. A draft, its selection and the status filter carry between tabs (the row's `keep`).

- The Table filters with chips above its rows. The chart uses the kit's `StatusLegend` in the canvas's bottom right (`overlayEnd`), keying only the four states (`LEGEND_FILTERS` in `lib/seatLive.ts`); a chip with no legend key (no state yet, problems) greys nothing on the chart, rather than grey cards under no pressed key.
- A reader who cannot change the org sees every edit and control drawn held, the reason in a tooltip. A reader the configuration is guarded from (no Admin, no unit they lead) reads the org projection every reader holds (`routes/org/builder/model/projection.ts`). A lead's page and counts are scoped to their units, as their draft is.

The builder's handling of a draft is [The org builder](#the-org-builder); the guide is [The Org Builder](../guides/org-builder.md). Structure replaced the chart, Roster, Teams and **Edit org** pages; their addresses still resolve ([the routes](#the-routes)), each replaced by the tab that holds it.

**Structure keeps its place in its own address**: status filter (`show`), teams closed on the chart (`closed`), Reporting view (`chart=reporting`), selection or open panel (`seat`, `unit`, `peek`), scroll (`at`), chart zoom and pan (`zoom`). `zoom` is put back only on the chart it was taken on: the view is tagged with the arrangement, legend key and closed teams, never with the fit count and loaded company, which restart on every mount. So a crumb back, Back and a reload land in the same place. A seat's page opened from here (a row's name, a **Reports to** chip, a card's **Open seat**, **Open** on the panel **Find a seat** opens) carries Structure's whole address as `from` (`useTrailOrigin`): its trail names the origin ("Structure › Table › Product Lead", "Structure › Org chart › Product Lead") and the crumbs before the seat go back to exactly that place. A seat panel over the Table keeps the Table's scroll; Back takes the panel off.

**Every chart opens whole, and can be read.** It opens fitted and centred. On a fresh arrival with nothing in the address to restore, a chart whose whole fit is below half size (`CHART_LEGIBLE_ZOOM` in `ui/canvasView.ts`; fourteen seats in one rank are 27% at 1440 px, 8% on a phone) opens on its top ranks with deeper branches closed (in the address, as a reader's own closing is) and the selected node's path open (`routes/org/builder/chartPlace.ts`). This is decided on the canvas's first report, before painting, and the canvas is redrawn on the answer, so it neither shows the small chart nor eases from it. Team and company captions count what they hold, so a closed team reads as closed, not empty.

Every layout action then fits whatever it draws, however wide (`CHART_FIT_FLOOR`, 2%; the kit's 25% cut a thirty-seat company at both edges at 1440 px). The kit's `fitKey` names them: Expand all, Collapse all, the Reporting view switch, opening or closing a team, a legend key, returning to the tab, a fresh read of the company. A fit nobody has moved also follows the canvas's box (`refitOnResize`): resized window, collapsed rail, a panel opening beside it. A reader's own zoom or pan holds until the next of those; a live update changes no card and never moves the view. The **Reporting view** switch sits in the canvas's top left, on a bar mirroring the zoom bar: off draws the teams, on draws who reports to whom.

**A card says who it is and what it is doing.** A seat leads with the console chart's mark (an agent's own character on a node in its own colour, a person's glyph in a dashed ring) and its NAME, then kind and handle ("agent · @pm"). An agent's state is a dot on its mark's corner (the kit's `markStatus`), in a fixed spot, explained by the status legend; a person, or an agent with no state yet, draws none. The dot is the only state hue on a node; an agent's colour is its own look (see "The one rule"). No state word is on the card: a node is as wide as its name, and a state word changed the width on every state change and relaid the chart, so a live update changes no card and only a layout action refits. The state's word and the engine's line ("Working · Executing ENG-412", "Needs you · executor parked") are the card's title, read after its name; the word is read with the node.

A unit's card carries its **Reports to** pill on its bottom edge ("Reports to: CTO", marked inherited where it is), the one label for a reporting line everywhere (the unit panel's fact, the unit editor's field); the choice of none reads **No one**. The root card and the Table's company row carry the company's logo: the square mark of the brand adopted in Company › Brand, else its primary logo (`useAdoptedMark`), else the company glyph.

**The status chips** stand over the Table, each a filter: All agents, Working, Needs you, Paused or stopped, Idle, No state yet (drawn only while some agent has none) and **Agents with problems**, named apart from the toolbar's configuration check pill ("Configuration OK", or "*N* configuration problems"), which is about the document, not the agents (`routes/org/structureParts.tsx`). No chip is counted before the first state arrives (a row of zeros is a claim nobody made). A chip prunes the tree to the seats it keeps (a team stays while it holds one); one matching nobody says so, with **Show all agents**.

**The chart's status legend** is a bar in the canvas's bottom right, across from the zoom bar and the same height: Working, Needs you, Paused or stopped and Idle, each with its dot in the cards' tone and a quiet count, the same words as the chips. A pressed key greys the seats it leaves out, at full contrast (the kit's `cardDimmed`), and refits the chart in the room the legend leaves, so no card is under it.

When a model limit stops seats, **one banner** above the Table says it once, in the Inbox's words (`lib/providerLimit.ts`), with how many seats wait and the remedy: **Open models** as its action for an admin; for anybody else "Only an admin can change the company's models." as the message's last line (`LimitCallout`), since a sentence in the action's place squeezed the message onto a third line at 768 px.

**The Table is where the company is watched and changed** (`routes/org/builder/TableView.tsx`, over the design system's `OrgTable`). One row per company, team and seat, in the chart's order, because an organization is the one table a sort destroys. Columns: **Name** (a select box before it; under it "agent · @qa", "human · @avery", a team's type and size, or "company"), **Status**, **Reports to** (the manager, or a team's lead, drawn as their seat), **Problems** (the worst one's tag and a count of the rest, each sentence its tooltip), **Controls**, **Edit**.

It follows the kit's table rules, one track list as a `DataGrid` draws: Name takes the free room above its floor, Reports to fits its content (only a save changes it), and every column a push can change is a length holding one line, so a live change moves no column or row. A seat's Status is one calm line: a dot and the state's word, then a quiet "· *N* waiting" and "· pausing". The work item, who waits, the pause reason and a person's availability are in its tooltip and the seat panel (whole state lines were a wall nobody read). A team's or the company's Status summarizes its agents.

Columns follow the table's own width, so a panel beside it narrows it as a window would: Reports to (below 1100 px) and Problems (below 960 px) go first, then Status, whose words move under the name; on a phone a row keeps its name, one control and its menu, which holds the rest. A seat's problems are folded, not dropped with their column: the worst one's tag joins its Status (or the line under its name), every sentence is its tooltip (a seat whose last turn failed otherwise read "Idle" alone below 960 px).

**The controls are the engine's own, and never look like an edit** (`components/seatControls.tsx`). Edits are the Edit column's and go through a draft and **Review and save**; controls are the Controls column's and act at once:

- **Pause** (`pause_seat`; the running turn finishes first).
- **Pause and stop** (`stop_running` as well: turn and executor end at once, so it asks first).
- **Resume** (one press, one seat).
- **Steer** (a note the turn reads at its next step, `steer_turn`).
- The remedy each state asks for, which leads beside Pause: **Review call** (a held tool call's Allow once, Always allow and Deny) and **Raise budget**, in room the Controls track keeps whether or not any seat has one.

An executor's plain question is answered in the seat panel and the Inbox; its row says **Needs you**. Where a remedy leads, Pause and stop and Steer move into the row's menu. Every reader is shown a seat's remedy, held with its reason where they may not take it, like every other control. Below 960 px of table width (768 px, or the seat panel open beside it) the controls fold to Pause or Resume and the remedy moves into the row's menu with Pause and stop and Steer (a full-width Controls column cut the names, and a remedy under the name changed the row's height); Status gives up some length to the name (`tableColumns`).

A row's dialogs (Pause, Steer, Raise budget) are drawn by the Table outside the grid (`components/dialogPresenter.tsx`): the kit opens a Modal in the nearest layer host and the grid draws one around its rows, so a dialog opened in a cell sat in the table's box, under the sticky bar on a scrolled phone.

A box per seat, team and the company picks agents for the selection bar (**Pause *n***, **Resume *n***, **Pause and stop *n***), the kit's compact one, drawn before the rows in the chips' place and room, so it sticks over the rows as they scroll and no row moves under the pointer between picks (the kit docks it at the foot under 640 px, where the chips stay). On a phone it keeps one row: Pause and Resume by words alone, Pause and stop in **More** (more than that wrapped onto a second row). A control of many seats sends one press per seat and reports once which seats were changed, and which were not and why.

**Only an admin or a lead above a seat may pause, resume or steer it** (`lib/seatLive.ts`, `controllable`); for anybody else each control is drawn held with that sentence (a vanished control would say nothing about why). **Edit, Delete and the row menu are drawn at rest**: a table read in order to act is not hunted across for its controls. Each team and company row carries a small add pill by its name ("Add to *team*": unit, agent seat, human seat), and a purple outlined **+ Add** sits beside **Review and save** in the toolbar (on a phone Review and save is its mark alone, in every state, so the "⋯", the check, Add and the save keep one row). The toolbar's height depends on neither selection nor draft, so a press on a card moves nothing under the pointer: the selected node's menu has a slot with nothing selected too, cutting its name in what the row leaves, and the check is one width while the row is tight, cut with its words in its title. The page bar carries **Find a seat** (name, handle or unit, best match first; `/` focuses it), which opens the found seat's panel over the tab, so the place it was found from stays under it.

**A human seat says what holds it**, in its panel, page and the **Person** section of its editor, for every signed-in reader. `GET /iam/seats` is everybody's (`iam.seats.read`), because who holds each seat is part of the overview; the engine masks it per reader: a holder's name and kind to everybody, person id, login and stage to an admin and the holder, an open invitation to an admin alone (ADR-0033). Every person holds exactly one human seat for as long as they exist ([ADR-0032](../../adr/0032-every-person-holds-a-human-seat.md)), and the company document cannot say who, so the seat does: held by its holder; invited (an address, or *Invited* where this node's keyring cannot open it; to anybody but an admin an invited seat reads as open); or **This seat is open**. A chart card and a table row do not carry it: who holds a seat is not something it is doing. A FAILED read is said where the holding would be (**The identity directory did not answer**, with the refusal's own words), since drawn as nothing an administrator met a seat with no gestures and no word why.

**A vacant human seat is where a person joins.** A person is never invited or created anywhere else: Settings › People lists, changes and removes people but adds none, because a person comes from the seat they will hold. For an admin the seat's panel and page, and the Person section of its editor, offer gestures by what holds the seat:

| The seat | The gestures |
|---|---|
| Vacant | **Invite** and **Add person** |
| Invited — an open invitation names it | **Cancel invitation** |
| Held by a person or a service account | nothing: a holder is moved or removed on their row in People (Service accounts, for a service account) |
| Not answered for — the listing failed, has not arrived, or does not hold the seat yet | nothing: a listing that did not answer says nothing about whether the seat is free |

The dialogs are one set (`components/people.tsx`), each about the seat as it was when the gesture started, not the live row: the listing is re-read the moment the write lands, and a cancellation reading the live row lost its invitation, and its dialog, before a `202` could say it was recorded.

- **Invite** — "Invite a person to Jane Doe": an **Email address** and the **access picker** (see [People](#settings-the-frame-people-secrets-nodes-and-configuration)), opened with every app ticked and Admin not, and the note on what an unticked app costs the person. It sends `POST /iam/invitations` with the seat; the **Invitation link** comes back **once**, with its expiry and the sentence that it is the credential: it works once, this engine sends no mail, and opening it is where the person chooses a login and password, binding them to the seat the open invitation holds until then.
- **Add person** — "Add someone as Jane Doe": an **Email address**, a **Name** and a **Login**, both optional; left empty, the engine proposes the login from the address (as an invitation's screen does) and says which it took; a typed one is held to the person grammar under the field before posting. Then the access picker, on the invitation's terms. It sends `POST /iam/people` (`kind: person`, the seat) under a fresh operation key, and the person is created ACTIVE on the seat at once. The answer names the login taken and shows the **Password link** **once**: it sets their first password, once, within a week, signs nobody in, and until used nobody can sign in as them. The key makes the link survive a dropped answer: the engine derives person and link from the operation, so **Try again** after an unknown answer returns the same link, not a second person; a retry that finds the link spent, revoked or lapsed shows *No link to show* with the engine's sentence naming the way to a new one, a password reset link.
- **Cancel invitation** — confirmed, with **Keep it** as the way out (a "Cancel" beside "Cancel invitation" kept the invitation for somebody meaning to cancel it): the link stops working at once and the address and seat are free again.

Each is one `/iam` write through `lib/iamWrite.ts`, on the terms [People & access](#settings-the-frame-people-secrets-nodes-and-configuration) states for every directory write: a step-up asked and the request replayed, a `202` leaving the dialog only **Done**, a refusal in the engine's words with the access that would admit.

**A seat or a unit opens in a panel over the tab**: a seat's (`peek=seat:{handle}`), a unit's (`peek=unit:{key}`). **Find a seat** opens one; an open panel is moved, not stacked; `[` and `]` step the seats while one is open, replacing the address so Back closes the panel however many seats it walked through. A unit has no page: its panel over the Table is its page, and a team's earlier address opens exactly that. While the org has not arrived, the panel and the seat's page draw a loading skeleton, not "No seat called …", which read as a seat that did not exist.

**The seat peek answers "who is this, and what is it doing".** In order:

- A state card tinted by the state: the line, how long the turn has run, "Turn 2 · executing" (the turn number is the task's own count, `work_item_turns`, asked by the task's id: see [An item's address](#an-items-address)).
- A **controls strip** on the Table's terms: problems as tags, a pause not reached yet ("Pauses after this turn"), the remedy a spent budget asks for, and Pause or Resume, Pause and stop and Steer.
- For an executor parked on a question, a callout under it carrying **Answer**, or for a held tool call **Allow once**, **Always allow** and **Deny**, beside the question.
- Reports to.
- Model: the phase chain from the org projection, which carries it only to an admin (every other reader is told Admin access shows it, never that the seat has no provider), and the model serving the call in flight.
- One row per capped budget window, labelled by its period ("Budget today", "Budget this week"), with a meter in the engine's state; or "No seat budget; the company's … applies" ("No seat budget; the company's 60M/day applies") where only the company's ceilings bind it, "No budget" where nothing does.
- Running on: for an admin the node holding the lease and since when; every other reader reads what the health push says (this node by name, or "another node"), as the profile's Setup card does; no guarded read is sent.
- Open work (`work_workload`): open tasks, load and what keeps the rest from moving.
- Where its tools come from (the projection's `tool_sources`, on the chain's terms).
- Its goal, as the inline markdown it is written in.

A human seat's peek adds **Held by**: the holder's name for everybody; for an admin and the holder their login with, short of active, their stage ("jane.doe (suspended)"; "The service account `ci:release`" for a machine); "An open invitation · sam@example.com"; or "Nobody — the seat is vacant"; never the card's line, which repeats the term. Or it says the directory did not answer, does not list the seat yet, or is still being read, rather than omitting the fact. The peek asks at most three questions: for a human seat one REST read of the directory (`GET /iam/seats`, masked per reader, answered to every signed-in reader), never for an agent's seat, whose holder is the engine; the open work and turn number are Worklet's, asked only of a reader holding Worklet.

While the seat is working the state card ends with **Watch live**, the turn's watch link: the panel, then that link, is the way from the company running to a turn running, with no link nested inside a chart card's tree item, which a keyboard and screen reader could not reach as itself.

**Message**, the primary, and **Assign task** are the rail's foot, pinned to its bottom edge, with **Ask as a task** in its More at the row's end where Message is a conversation (`useAskTaskEntry`, the seat page's own), since a third button pushed Assign task onto its own row. The rail's own bar holds the way to the profile at every width (its **Open**), so the foot offers no second. Beside them, for an admin, the seat's gestures as buttons (**Invite** and **Add person** on a vacant seat, **Cancel invitation** on an invited one), which on a phone are the only place they are.

Where the company runs the engine's own chat and you hold Chatlet, Message opens a conversation with the seat (`#/chatlet?dm={handle}`); elsewhere it opens the New task sheet with the seat as assignee and `ask` set (on the project filed under the seat's own unit, or the nearest unit above with one), so the question is work the seat owes an answer on and the answer lands in the Inbox; that ask is Ask as a task where Message is the conversation. With neither chat nor Worklet Message is not drawn, and without Worklet neither is a seat's Assign (see [the sidebar](#the-sidebar)).

**The peek of your own seat is your own seat's page in small**: Message and Ask as a task are held, saying it is your own seat, held by the button itself (`useMessageSeatAccess`), never by the screen drawing it (a screen-level hold let the peek offer a person on the chart an enabled Message to themselves). Under the state card is the profile's **Your account** card, linking to [Account](#account-the-readers-own-page). No other seat's peek draws either.
### A seat's profile

`#/company/org/seats/{handle}` is the approved Agent artboard. The head sits flush with the sheet: the seat's badge (an agent's own character on its squircle, a person's initials in a circle) with its status glyph, the name, an **Agent** or **Person** pill and, for an agent, the state in the engine's word ("Working", "Needs you", "Paused", "Stopped · budget", "Not placed", "Idle"). Under it is the placing line (handle · unit path · reports to its manager), then the tab strip on the head's own rule. The trail reads **Structure › Engineering · Core › SWE**: the unit links to its panel over Structure's Table, and the seat's crumb wears its badge. A page opened from Structure names that place instead ("Structure › Table › SWE"), and its crumbs before the seat return to exactly the address the reader left ([Structure is the company running](#structure-is-the-company-running)). While the org has not arrived the page draws a loading skeleton, never "No seat called …".

**Four tabs, each a group of sections, and the kind decides the set.** An agent has **Overview**, **Work** (its tasks, then a **Code** section), **Activity** (**Turns**, then **Memory** with its sessions) and **Settings** (its setup, then **Schedules** and **Access**); a person has Overview, Work and Settings. (Eight tabs were a strip a phone folded half away.) Work is drawn where the company runs Worklet or hosts code (`seat/profile.ts`): its tasks only with Worklet (locked for a reader without it), its Code section only for a Gitlet holder, with a compact "You need Gitlet access" lock for anybody else. Turns, Memory, Schedules and Access are properties of a RUNTIME and the engine never spawns a person, so a person's profile has no activity, memory, turn list or phase history.

A `tab=` that names a section (`tab=memory`, `code`, `turns`, `schedules`, `access`) lands on the tab holding it, scrolled to that section (`SECTION_TABS`) and held there while the tab fills (`holdScroll` in `lib/scroller.ts`, the one hold the router's restored scroll uses too); a single scroll landed short of Memory while the cards below had not drawn. A `tab=` naming a tab the seat has not got (a bookmark, or a link from before the rename: `model`, `cost`, `threads`) lands on Overview, and `app/source.test.ts` holds every link to a seat to a tab its profile has. The Work tab counts the seat's open work: the engine's `total_hint`, the same answer the Overview's card reads.

**A person's seat says what holds it.** The company document cannot: the identity directory binds a person to a human seat. So above the tabs a person's profile says it, through the same holding the chart's card and the peek draw (`SeatHolding` in `components/people.tsx`):

- **Held by** the holder's name to everybody; for an admin and the holder, their login too (`jane.doe`; "Held by you, as `jane.doe`" on your own seat; "the service account `ci:release`" where a machine holds it), with the stage when short of active.
- For an admin, the open invitation that names the seat: its address and until when. Until it is redeemed, cancelled or lapses nobody else can be invited or bound to the seat. It offers **Cancel invitation**.
- **This seat is open**, with **Invite** and **Add person**, the two ways a person comes to exist, opening [the seat's dialogs](#structure-is-the-company-running).

A seat nobody holds says so as its Overview's empty state, in the column a person's day and work would fill (its other tabs keep the line above them). The gestures are drawn for an admin. The answer is `GET /iam/seats`, which every signed-in reader is answered, masked per reader: to anybody but an admin a seat an invitation holds reads as nobody's. A failed read is SAID, with the engine's refusal, never drawn as nothing (the gestures live here, and a page without them would say nothing about why); a seat the chart draws but the listing does not hold is one this node has not applied the revision for, which the page says. A dialog opened here OUTLIVES the listing it was opened from: every write re-reads the listing, and a refused re-read (a node behind its identity log, or a refetch as the tab returns from the email the link was pasted into) must not take the open dialog, and the link it shows only once, with it.

**While the seat is working, the page bar leads with Watch live**: the running turn's watch link (its Transcript, the phase it is on open, or the executor a parked turn waits on drawn live above its phases). The **Activity** tab carries the kit's pulsing info dot, the steady-state mark of a state still happening, with its words read after the tab's name ("Activity, running now") because a dot is never the only carrier; folded into the strip's More, the words are the item's second line. Neither is drawn while the seat is idle, needs a person or is stopped, and the Overview card keeps its own **Watch live**.

**The page bar's actions are write controls, each held with its reason** for a reader who cannot make it:

- **Message** writes to the seat. Where the company runs the engine's own chat and the reader holds Chatlet it opens chat's New direct message with the seat chosen (`#/chatlet?dm={handle}`), which is what the word means; the tracker's ask (a task the seat owes an answer on, whose answer lands in the asker's Inbox) is then **Ask as a task** in the bar's More. Elsewhere (a vendor's chat, none, or a reader without Chatlet) Message is that ask, opening the New task sheet with the seat as assignee and `ask` set (`lib/seatMessage.ts`' `useSeatMessage`), because a message filed as a task in a project nobody chose was wrong. Filing work for the seat is Assign task either way.
- **Assign task** finds an existing task by search and hands it over against the version a read of it returned (`update_work_item{assignee, if_match}`), so a task somebody moved in between is refused rather than taken from its current holder; or it files a new one for the seat. Matches list the tasks that CAN move first; the seat's own come last, drawn but disabled and marked "already theirs", so a term most of whose matches the seat holds still offers eight it could be handed.
- **The seat's run-time controls** (agents only), the same ones Structure's Table and the seat panel draw (`components/seatControls.tsx`), for an admin or a lead above the seat, held with that reason for anybody else. **Pause** or **Resume** is in the bar; the rest are in the bar's More menu (beside Ask as a task, "Events" and "Edit in org"), since all in the bar cut the trail's own name and wrapped it onto two rows: **Pause and stop** while a turn runs (a paused seat whose turn is still finishing included), and **Steer**, a note the running turn reads at its next step. Pause asks why, and the turn the seat is on finishes first. Pause and stop sends `stop_running`, which ends the turn and the seat's executor in its box at once, so it asks first. Either way the seat's executor can push or change nothing until resumed (see [pausing a seat](../concepts/agent-runtime.md#pausing-a-seat)). A paused seat's profile says who paused it, when and why, and offers **Resume**; one paused while its turn finishes has its pill read "Working · pausing" and its notice **Pauses after this turn**.

"Events" (the [event log](#the-routes) narrowed to this seat) and "Edit in org" (Structure opened on the seat with its editor open, `editor=open`) are in the bar's More menu on either kind's profile, and the KIND decides the narrowing. An agent's is `seat=<handle>`, which the engine resolves to the id every node derives for the seat, never the name, which a namesake shares. A person publishes nothing under an agent id, but the log names them as its ACTOR, and the name `iam.ActorFor` records for a person bound to a seat is the seat's handle, so theirs is `actor=<handle>` (the display name never matched).

On a phone the bar keeps **one** action in view (Message, or Resume on a paused seat) and folds the rest into the same More menu (Watch live first, while there is a turn to watch), each disabled there with the sentence its inline control is held with. A notice under the tab strip, above whichever tab is open, carries what stops the seat or waits on somebody, in the state's own tone: its last error, a pause, another stop, or its executor parked on a question or asking to make a held tool call, answerable from the notice: **Answer** for a question; **Allow once**, **Always allow** and **Deny** for a call.

**The Overview is the seat's week and its charter.** Four figures, all ONE answer (`seat_activity` with `previous`, every data node's usage rows summed):

- turns over seven company days with the change against the week before;
- the engine's first-pass rate over the turns it REVIEWED (a week nobody reviewed has no rate, never 0%) with how many reviews sent work back;
- the median turn with its p90;
- tokens: the seat's capped window nearest its ceiling, over that ceiling ("of 3M budget"), or the seven days' tokens where the seat has no ceiling of its own. Where the company's own budget caps a window, "company cap 60M/day +1" (and "no seat cap" on hover), because that ceiling binds every seat (one line in the tile, the whole sentence on hover). A shortened token count carries no zero fraction: `60M`, never `60.0M`.

The **current turn** card shows where the turn is: Context, Execute ("in its box" once the turn parks on its executor), Review. There is no delivery step, because whether a turn reached anybody is decided as it closes. It shows the turn's number on its task and the task's title (read by the turn's own task, by its id, see [An item's address](#an-items-address), never looked up in the card beside it), its elapsed time and, for a reader the seat's trail is open to (an admin, or whoever leads the seat, `audit.seat.read`), tokens so far, and the phase's calls, each with the engine's own start time and duration, the running one last. A call reads as words, never JSON: the tool's name whole in a column as wide as the longest name the phase called, then the argument that says what it is about bare (`ENG-38`, the query, the command) and every other argument by its name (`assignee me · open`). Between turns it is the seat's state in one line and its last turn.

Beside it are the seat's open work (the five most urgent, and "All n") and its turns per company day over the fortnight the delta spans, today in the accent. The side column is:

- **About**: the goal to three lines and the first three responsibilities to two each, as inline markdown, and "Show all" where that cut anything. A charter is the seat's prompt text and is never summarised.
- **Setup**: the model chain and tool grants from the org projection, which carries both only to an admin (both derive from the seat's configuration); anybody else is told Admin access shows them, not that the seat has none. The sandbox, placement and workers come from the company document, read by an admin, or for the lead of the seat's unit from the seat's own entity and its home unit's (`GET /config/roles/{handle}`, `GET /config/units/{key}`), which the engine admits a lead to; anybody else is never asked and is told they are unread, with the access that reads them, or absent when the active revision names no seat by this handle. The node holding the seat now: the fleet's lease, asked only of an admin; for anybody else what the health push says, this node by name or "another node" (the seat's peek says it too). And Edit.
- **Memory**: the holder's counted totals and its newest reflection, asked only of a reader the seat's trail is open to; anybody else gets a sentence naming Admin access and that whoever leads the seat reads it too, not a refusal drawn in the side column.
- **Schedules**.

A person's Overview is **Their day**, or **Your day** on your own seat (with the way to your Inbox and My work):

- the unread notices waiting on them (the inbox's own count, the sidebar badge's reading on your own day, "50+" past a page);
- their priorities: the engine's count of what on the list is still open (the figure My work and their Work tab read), never the stored list's length, which still names a task they finished until their next reorder, and who set them;
- pinned views, for the person and whoever leads them, holding Worklet, and an admin; withheld with that sentence for anybody else;
- their open work, for a reader holding Worklet; and About.

On your own seat the whole page speaks to you: the holder line says "Held by you, as `jane.doe`", the work card "Nothing open is assigned to you", the Work tab "What you mean to do first" and "Waiting on your answer". **Message** is held, saying it is your own seat, because a message files an ask only you could answer; the hold is the BUTTON'S rule, so the bar's Message, its phone "More" entry and the seat's peek are held in one sentence. **Assign task** stays: taking a task yourself is a hand-off like any other. The side column leads with **Your account** (the seat is not the account; a person looking for their password or second factor found neither), linking to [Account](#account-the-readers-own-page). The card decides for itself whose seat it is on, so the peek carries it too, and a colleague's seat draws none.

**Code**, the section under the tasks on Work, is what the seat does on Gitlet, agent or person, each the engine's own question held to the reader's grant on every repository it names. It is drawn only for a Gitlet holder (ADR-0110): anybody else gets a compact lock, "You need Gitlet access", and nothing is asked. For a holder, a repository they may not read is absent from its rows. It holds:

- open changes (`code_changes?owner=&state=open`, the owner's listing, which the engine keeps one state at a time), with **Open in Gitlet** for Gitlet › Changes narrowed to the owner, where the other states are;
- the reviews asked of it (`code_changes?needs=review&reviewer=`, the live changes whose ask of it stands), with **Open in Gitlet** for Gitlet › Changes waiting on its review;
- the reviews it gave (`code_reviews?reviewer=`, newest first): each row the change it judged, the verdict in words (a judgement, not a state, so no hue), the revision, the findings it raised and when, opening that change's page;
- for an agent seat, three figures from the same `seat_activity` answer the Overview's tiles read: **Changes opened**, **Reviews given** and **Findings received** (counted on the owner of the changes the findings were raised on). A person's openings and reviews count on no seat's day, so a human seat's tab draws no figures. The figures say how much happened; the reviews and the changes' readiness say how well.

**Turns**, the first section of Activity, is the seat's own turns (`turns{seat}`, the seat's TRAIL, which the engine answers to an admin and to whoever leads the seat, `audit.seat.read`). For anybody else the section is drawn and locked, "This seat's turns needs Admin access", with the sentence that whoever leads the seat reads it too, and nothing is asked. It is answered from every node over the thirty days the event store keeps, fifty at a time with "Load older turns" following the engine's cursor, and a count of what is loaded ("50+" while an older page exists).

- **Running now** leads the section so a turn in flight is on screen as it opens; settled transcripts follow under **Transcripts · newest first**. A turn under Running now opens the phase it is on, as the trace's Transcript does, and STAYS there for as long as the seat's own turn record says it is on it, between phases and while parked too (the rule the turn's page reads). Deciding on "has a phase in flight" moved the card to the settled list between phases, remounted it and shut the transcript the reader was following. Its card moves once, as the turn ends, and opens with the phases the reader watched live still open.
- A running card's header gives ONE duration, how long the turn has been running; the length across its phases is a settled card's.
- A phase that finishes while the tab is open reaches its transcripts off the push, matched on the seat's own id as Live's recent phases are, never its role name, which two unit seats stamped from one template share.
- A row for a turn still running says what the seat is doing and what it is on, from the push ("running — reviewing · round 2 of 4", ENG-32), and draws its iterations and tokens as not settled, not as zeros (`#/live/turns` does the same). On a phone a row's summary takes two lines with its item under it, and a settled turn has no State line.
- **Where its tokens go**: its week by phase and by model (only buckets that spent some; calls that failed before a model answered recorded none), with the way to all of its activity on Live.

**Memory**, the section under Turns, is the seat's TRAIL too (`audit.seat.read`, ADR-0033), so it asks nothing of anybody else and says, as Turns does, what would open it, rather than sending two questions to be refused and drawing the refusals as a seat's memory. It is read from the node HOLDING the seat, whose copy is the current one, and says which node answered. It draws:

- the diary;
- the episodes: each outcome in the reviewer's own tone (`failed` is red here as on a turn); each turn's **Woken by** (the waking event's label, with what it was asked under it) apart from **What it did** (its account), each an opening marked with `…` and a **Read all** that opens the turn whole where the text is longer than the list carries; a compacted row as how many turns it stands for, their pattern and what varied, and how many ended done;
- the skills it taught itself and who it has worked with (when last, relative, as every list on the profile says it);
- each header the holder's total ("Latest 50 of 142" where the list is a page of it).

An episode's conversation is its KEY, the conversation's only identity, with a Worklet task's uuid cut to its head (`work:task:4d631f6d`) and a schedule's parts printed as written (`schedule/unit/eng/weekly report`, not `weekly%20report`), the whole key on the cell's title. A seat no node holds says why it shows nothing.

Under them are the seat's **Sessions** (`session=` opens one): every turn whose executor captured its harness's session, and every turn that read its conversation, from its first launch, the whole record of what its run read, called and wrote. They are read through any node (the rows are the replicated estate's, the bytes the fleet's object store's), on the same `audit.seat.read` as the rest of the tab, the verb an executor's live output is decided by.

- Each row is what its turn was asked, as plain words in two lines, over how the turn ended (its outcome in the reviewer's tone, or `not ended`), the harness and its release, and when.
- The list pages by the engine's cursor (**Load older sessions**), is asked again each minute, and says when the node that answered may be missing rows it could not read. A failed poll says so in the list's own card, never in place of the transcript beside it.
- Choosing one shows it. Beside the list (a wide screen column) the list scrolls inside a box bounded by the scroller's view, handing the wheel back to the page at either end, its chosen row kept in view (a session the address names as soon as the list is drawn), and the chosen session sticks under the page's top. Stacked on a phone, the session is scrolled to and its heading takes focus.

The chosen session is subtitled with its conversation, printed as an episode's is, or "No conversation". Then comes the engine's account of how the turn ended, as the list's row last read says it (a turn's end is recorded with no new capture, so it reaches the list's poll and never the transcript), each only where the ending carries it:

- the decision;
- whether its reply reached the party waiting and on what surface, that it did not, or that this is not known;
- that its newest session was not kept, and why;
- its answer to a colleague; what landed, what blocked it, who stopped it and why, the failure;
- what is kept of the session and its size, and a link to the turn;
- where its first launch was handed a session to continue, a link opening that session here;
- which launch would continue the session and whether it would, as the engine decided: a relaunch while the turn is live, the conversation's next turn once ended, or the schedule's next fire. It would, in whichever box it gets, where that box can take it up and the seat's budget can carry it (a relaunch alone only in the box its run parked in, while held, with the engine's reason no other box would); where not, the engine's own reason; where the engine could not decide (unreadable record, job still working, capture still kept or awaiting the log, holding node not answering, end not on the log yet), that this cannot be said now and why. An unknown is never drawn as a no.

Under it is the **transcript**, a page at a time (**Load more of the transcript**) as the harness recorded it. Each entry is labelled by who it is from (brief, note, late call, model, tool call, result, summary); a subagent's entries name the subagent; a result names its tool and marks a failure. A call's input and a tool's output are blocks under the record ceiling every block in the scroller takes, each a focusable region named by its tool only when it scrolls, with select-all left to the page; the prose is prose. An entry cut to its bound says how large the whole was, and a part of the record that could not be read is a warning in its place. Every text is the engine's redacted one. Choosing another session draws it from its loading state, never the last one's account and entries under its name.

A transcript is of ONE capture for as long as it is on screen. It is not asked again on a reconnect. When the list shows the session captured again since it was read, or its first page (asked again after a write from the tab) is answered for a newer capture, the transcript says so and offers **Read the newer capture**, never drawing it under the pages on screen. A page the engine refuses because it no longer follows on (the session captured again, or a node of another release answering) offers **Read it again from the start**. The pages of two captures are never spliced, and either re-read puts focus on the transcript's heading. A session whose object is gone, does not open, is no archive or is of a format this build does not read is a warning naming which, with the engine's sentence; so is a later page that could not be read, after the entries already read, saying the rest could not be; a page cut where no later page can go further says the rest cannot be shown, or that none of it can where the read reached no entry.

**Settings** is the seat's half of the company document, read by its handle (the seat and its home unit, whose `mcp_env` a seat inherits per variable) through the same one read the Setup card makes (`useSeatSetup`): the company document for an admin, the seat's and its unit's own entities for the lead of its unit, and nothing asked for anybody else, whose tab names the access in the frame's words ("Reading this seat's settings needs Admin access", and, for a seat in a unit, that whoever leads it or a unit above it reads them too). "No company configuration is active" is said only of a read that came back with no document. Every other outcome (still out, waiting on who the reader is included; refused naming the access; absent) has its own sentence, never an empty value.

It draws identity and contacts, the model and budget with each capped window's live meter, and a seat's tool credentials by server and **variable name only**: no value the engine sent for a credential reaches the page, not the reference, not the mask. A person's has no model, budget or credential card, because the engine refuses all three on a human seat. Every value there is changed in the org editor ("Edit in org"). Under the setup an agent's Settings tab carries its **Schedules** and its **Access** (its access to every integration the company has connected, drawn and edited with each integration's own Agents tab narrowed to this agent, so a save here is the same save as on the integration's page), each a section a `tab=` names on its own.

### The attention queue

`dashboard/src/lib/attention.ts` is one derivation because it is one question. The conditions were each known to the dashboard but lived in different screens:

| Condition | Where it used to live |
|---|---|
| an executor parked on a question | a badge (one whose box had been reclaimed appeared nowhere) |
| a seat the engine stopped | a card among the healthy ones |
| a budget refusing charges | a bar on one seat's page |
| an engine with **no active configuration**, dropping every inbound webhook | a line in a popover |
| a live round that has not moved in minutes | nowhere (the row animated either way) |

Ordered by what it costs to ignore, then newest first inside a severity. Every row says what happened AND what it costs to leave it, and links to where the answer is.

**Each condition has ONE home**, by its subject (`WHERE_OF`), so none is drawn twice and none nowhere:

| Home | Subjects | Why there |
|---|---|---|
| `seat`: the Inbox's "Needs you", and Home's "N conditions need a look" | the seats' own state, the token budgets | a person decides these: raise a ceiling, resume a seat, look at one that failed |
| `engine`: the sidebar's engine panel and Home's status sentence | the engine and this node's link to it | a fact about the product on every screen, not an item in anybody's queue |
| `live` — Live › Now running, beside what each is about | a round that has stopped moving (a caution or failure mark on its own running-turn row, never while the turn is parked), every executor parked on a question (a row of **Waiting on a person**, answered in place) | watched rather than decided; an executor waiting on a PERSON already reaches them through their decisions, and an alarm list restating the rows around it was a second copy of each |

On Home the queue is COUNTED, not drawn: the `seat` conditions that are not the reader's own decisions (a seat stopped for a reason other than its budget, a company budget near or at its ceiling) are the status sentence's "N conditions need a look", linked to the Inbox, and the engine's own conditions take the sentence over. What the reader can settle is the decisions card beside it.

**One pause, one row.** A seat the engine paused after the same failure twice (ADR-0117) is said by the advisor's finding for that failure, which names the seat (or every seat the failure holds) and the fix ("Agent X is paused because the sandbox could not start as configured"), and draws no seat row beside it: two rows said one pause twice, the second offering a resume that fails the same way. The finding classes are the engine's (`PAUSED_SEAT_CLASSES` in `contract/advisor.ts`, held to `advisor.PausedClasses`); a pause a person took, or an engine pause no finding says, keeps its seat row.

**What a quiet list says is derived, not written.** Every condition names one of five subjects, `SUBJECTS` maps each to the phrase a reader sees, and a place that lists none draws the phrases of exactly the subjects whose home it is (`watchedIn`). A hand-written "No seat is stopped, no run is parked on a question, and no budget is refusing" covered three of twelve conditions yet read as the whole list. A new condition cannot be pushed without naming a subject, and a new subject fails the build until it has its own phrase.

---

## Markdown is rendered, not printed

Page bodies, work-item descriptions and both kinds of comment are **markdown by contract** (every tool that writes them says so in its schema), so the dashboard renders them rather than printing `## Decision`, `- [ ] ship it` and `[the guide](https://…)` as literal text.

`lib/markdown.ts` renders a CommonMark subset to React nodes. Its grammar is the design system's (`parseMarkdown` and `markdownInline` from `@crewlethq/ui`), the same the rich editor reads a body by, so writer and reader cannot disagree about where a list ends or what a backslash escapes. It is written in-tree because a library's real surface is its HTML passthrough and the sanitiser that must follow it, and this renderer needs **neither**: it emits no raw HTML under any input, so there is no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` on the path and nothing to sanitise.

Beyond the usual blocks it reads a **backslash escape** (`\*` is an asterisk), an **escaped pipe** in a table cell (`a \| b`, a pipe of that cell, inside a code span too, as GitHub reads it), and a **callout** in GitHub's alert syntax, a quote whose first line is `[!NOTE]`, `[!TIP]`, `[!IMPORTANT]`, `[!WARNING]` or `[!CAUTION]`, drawn as a tinted note with its tone named on a line of its own.

Three rules are load-bearing, because a page is written by an agent acting on content it read elsewhere:

- **Raw HTML is text.** A `<script>` in a body renders as the characters `<script>`.
- **A link's scheme is an allowlist**: `http:`, `https:`, `mailto:` and the app's own `#/` routes. Anything else (`javascript:`, `data:`, a protocol-relative `//host`, a bare `/path`) renders as its own **label**, and an image with a refused source as its alt text. An allowlist, because enumerating bad schemes is wrong the moment a browser grows one more.
- **A picture is shown from this origin only.** The dashboard's policy loads images from its own origin (and `data:` and `blob:`), so an image on another host renders as a link to it, labelled by its alt text, rather than as a picture the browser refuses; loading it would also tell that host who reads the page and when. The rich editor shows the same picture as its alt text (`shownImage` in `lib/markdown.ts`). A doc's pictures are files of its version, fetched with the reader's credential, and are unaffected. A link inside a link's label is that label's text.

An outbound link opens in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, and a screen reader is told it does; an in-app `#/` link does neither. A task list's checkboxes are disabled (this surface performs no writes, and a tickable box would report a change that never reached the page), each named by its item's own line. Wherever the renderer draws one (a reading pane's lead holds no `.prose.md`), an item is one line: no marker, the box on the first line of its words, and a wrapped line under the words, not under the box. A table wider than its column scrolls inside a group a keyboard can reach, named by its columns ("Table: Step, Owner"): a group, not a region, because a region is a landmark and two tables of the same columns drew two indistinguishable landmarks.

**A model's words are markdown too.** A round's speech and an executor's report render as markdown, with two options a document does not take (`MODEL_WORDS` in `lib/markdown.ts`), because a model's line breaks are load-bearing but a fenced JSON block must not print as backticks and braces:

- **Every newline is a line break** (`breaks: "hard"`). A document's single newline is a soft wrap, read as a space; a model writes one fact per line and means each.
- **A heading is a styled line, not a heading** (`headings: "text"`, the `.md-heading` block). A transcript item is not a section of the page (the reason a tool row's disclosure renders no heading either), and a model's `## Summary` must not put an `h2` into the turn page's outline. It keeps a heading's weight and air at the body's size.

Everything else is the document renderer's: raw HTML is text, the link allowlist holds, and a fence is a block holding the exact bytes (a round still streaming can end inside one, and what has arrived is shown as code). An attempt a provider abandoned mid-answer stays plain dimmed text: it is evidence of a failure, cut wherever the provider died, and never becomes the round's answer, whereas streaming text is about to become it and is rendered so the block does not reshape at commit.

**Emphasis follows CommonMark's delimiter-run rules.** Snake_case names nobody put in a code span fill model words and prompts ("call submit_work with the result_summary", a tool catalogue's `- list_mcp_server_tools:` line); opening at any `*` or `_` ate the underscores and named a tool that does not exist. A run opens only when left-flanking and closes only when right-flanking, so `*foo *` is not emphasis; an underscore inside a word is a letter of it (`snake_case_name` stays itself, `_word_` and `__init__` are still emphasis); an asterisk inside a word still opens and closes, as the spec says (`foo*bar*`). One walk serves the renderer and the plain-text flattening alike, over the whole text, so a run's neighbour is the character really beside it.

`.prose` on its own stays a `pre-wrap` block, for text whose every space and break is the record (a launch's activity log). Rendered markdown carries `.prose.md`.

**A fenced block wraps rather than scrolling.** The class is `md-code`, in the family of `md-table`, `md-tasks` and `md-task-body`; its recipe wraps, the design system's default for a block a reader *reads*, and unlike a scroll container it owes no tab stop. The old generic `class="code plain"` (`plain` was also a table header's class) gave a fence no surface or padding and a `pre`'s own `white-space: pre` with `overflow: visible`, so one long JSON line pushed the page sideways (1378px of scroll width in a 700px viewport). The class gate now reads both a `className` **attribute** and a `className:` **property** (the renderer writes the latter), and both directions fail on the old name.

The same file also **splits a document into its sections without rendering anything**: `splitSections` for the flat run, `nestSections` for the outline its heading levels describe, and `headingLines` for where each heading's line starts in the source. The one surface needing a document's outline and its source both is a phase prompt, which the transcript outlines, renders one section at a time, and hands back byte for byte on the other view (see rule 11 below); a walk that rendered as it split could give neither. All three read the document through ONE fence-aware walk beside the renderer, because what a heading is and where a fence suspends the grammar are decisions the renderer has already made; copies next to their callers would drift, as `textcut`'s four copies and `whsec`'s two did, the fence clause first.

A page's history shows **what a save changed**, not only what one version said. The two revisions are compared by the design system's line diff (the shortest edit between their lines; past 20,000 lines a side in what changed, or 4,000 lines removed and added, a sentence says the two were not compared line by line, and why, in place of any row) and drawn by `DiffView` ([Every diff is tinted](#every-diff-is-tinted)), over the count of lines added and removed against the revision before. Inside an edited line it underlines ONE run, never a word-by-word diff, because these documents are rewritten in paragraphs and a word diff makes a small edit prettier and a large one unreadable. Unchanged runs collapse to a row saying how many lines they stand for: a silently closed gap makes a document edited at both ends look rewritten in the middle. "This save did not change the body" is its own answer, because a title, a label and a move are saved beside a body and a pane of unmarked lines reads as a failed load.
### What prose names is drawn as what it is

`acme/backend#14` is a pull request, `#ffe100` a yellow, `~design-review` a Mattermost channel, `#launch` a chat room, `ENG-66` a task. Every surface `lib/markdown.ts` renders (page, description, comment, Inbox, Ask Crewlet answer, transcript) draws each with the mark that says what it is, a little below the text's size, just before its words (`InlineRef` from `@crewlethq/ui`); a seat's handle is its words alone:

| Written | Drawn |
|---|---|
| `#ffe100` in words, or a code span that is one colour (`` `#fff` ``, `` `rgb(255, 225, 0)` ``) | A swatch before the value |
| A web address | The mark of its app (or a globe) and the reference it is (`acme/backend#14`, `Message in acme`, `~design-review`, `MOB-12`, `DES page 123`) in place of the address, which the link's title keeps |
| `[label](address)` | Its label as written, after the mark of its address's app |
| `owner/repo#14`, `group/project!7`, `owner/repo@b5362d2` | The code host's mark, linked to the company's code host |
| `owner/repo`, under an owner the company works in | The code host's mark, linked to the repository |
| `#11`, where its message places it | The code host's mark, linked to the issue or pull request |
| A SHA after a reference ("at b5362d2") or after the word *commit* | The same, linked to the commit |
| `ENG-66` | The task glyph, linked to the work item; unlinked once the engine says the reader may not open it, or that it is gone |
| `web!42`, a Gitlet change in prose | The change glyph, linked once the engine says the reader may open it; its words otherwise, since a word shaped like a change is not one until the engine says so |
| An artifact's address (`#/artifacts/{id}`, or the whole address Copy link writes), bare or as `[label](address)` | The artifact's kind glyph and current title (`ArtifactRef` from `@crewlethq/ui`), linked; its words as written where the reader may not see it |
| `#launch`, a chat room the reader may read | The room's mark, linked to the room; `#e2e` and `#2026` too where the company has rooms of those names |
| `@ada` | Its words, linked to the seat |

#### What an engine line names comes first

A line the engine wrote (feed line, turn trigger, wake subject) carries what it names (`refs`, [What a line
names](api-endpoints.md#what-a-line-names)). Every surface showing one (Live and Home's event cards, the event log, an event's page, a trace, a turn's page and its card on a seat, a running turn on Live, the audit log) draws it through one renderer (`EngineLine`, `components/NamedRef.tsx`): each ref's words, found left to right, are the kit's `InlineRef` with its kind's glyph (task, change, commit, repository, page, artifact, turn, schedule, channel, seat, room), its kind said to a screen reader, its title on hover, and a link to its page. The rules below read the rest of the line and the whole of an agent's own words (a turn's account, a review).

Whether the reader may open each ref, and its current name, is one `references` ask for every reference a tab draws in one tick (`lib/namedRefs.ts`), each answered by the question its own page asks, as the reader, and kept for the socket. Until answered a reference is its marked words; open, a link; refused or gone (never told apart), marked words with no link, never a dead one. A row that is itself a link (an event's card, a running turn) opens through a link stretched over it, under the references in its line, so neither link sits inside the other.

`lib/inlineTokens.ts` holds the recognition rules and their reasons. Each rule is a guess that can fail three ways, all refused:

- **Too eager.**
  - A colour in words needs a digit and a letter: `#123` (an issue) and `#facade` (a hashtag) are words. A colour inside a longer code span (`color: #fff;`) is code.
  - A SHA needs a reference or the word *commit* before it, so `deadbeef1` is a word.
  - A key's project must be one of the company's, so `ISO-8601` and `UTF-8` are words.
  - A handle needs a seat, so `@nobody` is a word; an email address is never a mention.
  - A bare `owner/repo` needs its owner named by the company's code hosts, so `and/or`, `src/app` and `2024/10` are words.
  - A `#name` is a room only where the reader may read a room of that name, and a room's name wins over a colour or issue number spelled the same: `#e2e` and `#2026` are rooms where the company has them, colours and numbers where not. A room the reader cannot see (a private room, or a company whose chat is a vendor's) reads exactly as a vendor's channel does. A code span holding just a room's `#name` is code.
  - An address swallows every key and colour spelled inside it.
- **Too trusting.**
  - A mark is chosen from the parsed address a link GOES TO, never from its words: a link labelled "github.com/…" going elsewhere carries no GitHub mark, and a look-alike host (`github.com.login.example.net`, `github.com@login.example.net`) is nobody's.
  - An app is recognised at its public host exactly (github.com, gitlab.com), under its own domain on a dot (`*.slack.com`, `*.atlassian.net`), or at a host the company configured for it.
  - A link's label is read as words, never as a token, so `[https://github.com/a/b/pull/1](https://login.example.net)` draws no GitHub mark.
  - A label built from an address names only what its site vouches for: an unconfigured Atlassian Cloud tenant is said after its key or page ("DES page 123 (evil.atlassian.net)"); a page is named by space and id, never by the title its address carries; a Mattermost channel only by a name Mattermost allows; a path segment that decodes to a slash (`a%2Fevil`) or that no code host allows labels nothing, so the address shows as host and path.
- **Too slow.** Every pattern runs in linear time, since every reader renders an agent's comment, and a run is read once, not on every render of the surrounding surface.

**The company's hosts reach every reader, and nothing else of its integrations does.** A self-hosted GitLab, an Enterprise Server, a Mattermost or a Jira site lives at an address no rule can guess, so the frame reads `link_hosts` once ([API Endpoints](api-endpoints.md)): a kind and base address per configured app, which every reader may ask for (`integrations` is an administrator's). A code host's row also names its owners (organizations or top-level groups the company works in), which is what makes a bare `owner/repo` a repository; it carries no repository, project, team, credential or health.
- A link to a code host is built only to a repository under an owner its row names: `attacker/exfil#1` keeps GitHub's mark and links nowhere, since owner and name are the writer's words.
- A code host whose row names no owners links no reference at all.
- With GitHub and GitLab both configured, a reference goes to the host whose owners hold it; one neither or both hold is words.
- On GitHub a repository is exactly `owner/repo`; a longer path is words.
- With no code host configured, `owner/repo#14` keeps GitHub's mark and links nowhere.
- Project keys are the reader's own `work_projects`, read once by the frame where Worklet is served to them. Room names are the reader's own `chat_room_names` (every room they may read, joined or not), read once by the frame where Chatlet is served to them as a seat, plus any room this tab has seen a live frame for since.
- No mark is ever fetched from anywhere: every mark is the design system's.

**A bare `#11` is placed by its message.** `#11` alone is a list number, a rank or an issue in some repository, so it is a reference only where its message says which: the same sentence binds it (`#7 in acme/frontend`, `acme/frontend PR #7`, read as one reference); the message names that number in full (`acme/backend#11`); or the message names exactly one repository. Otherwise it is words. Chosen trade-off: in a message naming one repository, a rank or heading number ("our #1 priority", a heading "#2 Rollout") is read as an issue in it too, as GitHub's own autolinking does, rather than guess at the words around a number. A message is one comment, page or answer, or an ask's question, context, reasoning and options together (`TokenScope`), so the Inbox's "the #11 PR body" is placed by the `acme/backend` its context names. A render joins a scope only when it says so (`scoped`): a reply drawn under an ask is its own message. A number with a leading zero, inside a word, path or entity, or in code is never one.

**A token is a link only where a link may be.** Inside a control or a link (an Inbox row, an answer's option, a link's own label) a link would be invalid or steal the press, so those draw marks and swatches alone (`renderTokens`).

Where an agent or model that may have read anything wrote the words (Ask Crewlet's answers, the Inbox and an executor's question, `links: "checked"`), a link is live only where the dashboard built it, from checked parts, to a place that is the company's: a key's, room's or handle's route, a reference on the configured code host, or an address on a configured host rebuilt from what it names, with no query or fragment. Any other address is drawn inert: as written, with its mark, in the text's own ink (bare or under a label), readable and copyable, never a control, because `https://evil.example/?q=<what it read>` is how an injected instruction would carry words away. An address an ask cites as evidence is the same: a button only when rebuilt on the company's host, labelled by the dashboard with the reference it is and its app's mark; otherwise the address as written, never the asker's label ([ADR-0061](../../adr/0061-a-read-is-named-in-the-answer-never-drawn-as-a-card.md)).

A chat message is read the same way, whoever wrote it, plus one addition (`links: "own"`, `CHAT_WORDS`): a page of the dashboard's own (a `#/` route, or the whole address a Copy link writes on its origin) opens in place, rebuilt from its path alone (`lib/appRoute.ts`), so no query a writer chose rides along. Ask Crewlet's answers never take it: their one way to move the page is an Open in app card the engine built.

A message's links (`routes/chatlet/MessageLinks.tsx`):
- A task, page, artifact or pull request the reader may open unfurls into a preview the engine resolved as the reader (`chat_unfurls`, with an address the engine built).
- An address of an app the dashboard knows unfurls into its mark, name and reference.
- Every other is the address token; one whose scheme the allowlist refuses is its words.

An executor's question is read so wherever it is answered: its Answer dialog (`components/writes.tsx`), opened from Live › Executors, a seat's page and every decision row, reads the run's context and reasoning `checked`.

An outbound link a token makes opens a tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and says so to a screen reader, as every outbound link in rendered Markdown does.

**The caller reads first.** Ask Crewlet's record chips (`RenderOptions.prose`) are drawn before any token is read, and tokens are read only in the words the chips left, so a record the turn read stays its chip; a search's highlight marks the words left after that.

## ⌘K: search, answer, act

One box for the whole product: where to go, what the company knows, and the three changes a person most often makes from a search. It is the design system's `CommandPalette` (combobox, scope tabs, the answer's live region and key legend are the kit's); `app/palette/` is what it searches and what a row does.

### Seven scopes, three sigils

One index answers only "where do I go", so each question is a tab under the field:

| Scope | Searches | Sigil |
|---|---|---|
| **All** | screens and **Switch project…**; a pasted event / trace / turn id; three projects ranked as the switcher ranks them; three tasks and three pages (two of each under an answer); agents, people and teams; the tools the company connected (never the engine's own agent tools, which Settings › MCP & tools lists; a connected tool opens on its server's Tools tab); **Find “…” in artifacts**, carrying the term into Artifacts; **Find “…” in code**, carrying it into Code (for a Gitlet holder where the company hosts code); the three actions; the answer's remaining sources; **Search all work for “…”**, the full ranked search. Nothing typed: recents, then **Running now**, a row per seat working as the palette opened, oldest first, with badge, name and what it is doing ("Executing ENG-412"), each going to the turn's watch link | |
| **Tasks** | `work_search`, hybrid, eight hits, and a row to the full search screen | `#` |
| **Pages** | `knowledge`, the company's one knowledge backend | |
| **Artifacts** | `artifacts` with the term over everything the reader can open, eight hits, each row its kind | |
| **Code** | Where the company hosts code, asked once the term has rested: from two characters the **Repositories** whose names it begins (`code_repos?prefix=`) and the **Changes** whose words hold it (`code_changes?text=`, every state), five of each, each opening its page; `code_search` from three characters (the shortest Gitlet's plan looks up), eight lines, each `repo:path:line` opening its file at the commit searched with the line picked; and a row to Gitlet › Search with the term. Asked only for a Gitlet holder; for anybody else the scope stays (as Tasks and Pages do for a reader without their apps), asks nothing, and says "Search needs Gitlet access. An admin can give it to you." rather than that nothing matched | |
| **Agents** | the org chart: the engine's own name tiers first (`colleague`), each seat's status glyph from the agents push, then people and teams | `@` |
| **Actions** | the per-browser commands and the three changes; the legend names who they are made as.
