The engine ships SIX builtin views (one per shape, plus the trash); neither strip nor sidebar draws them. The STRIP drops them because a way of drawing is not something somebody saved, and mixed beside an arranged query the two read as one kind of thing (hence `view=` and `shape=` are two keys). The SIDEBAR drops them because a builtin carries no id, so no row to address.
  - The five shapes are the work list's one row as a segmented switch; the strip is a second, in its own well. Both are radio groups with manual activation, because each choice is a URL change that re-runs the list: arrows move focus, Enter or Space chooses, so no history entry per keypress.
  - A strip with more views than fit wraps inside its well; a long name is cut at 200px with its title carrying the rest.
  - The strip is the container's own list: the views THIS reader pinned (★) plus whichever one is running, **+ View** (the query on screen saved under a name, shared or private, shape as its type, without paging or a calendar's month), and the inventory as one glyph named **All saved views** (a real link), because the words pushed the search box and menus onto a second line at 1280px.
  - That the strip is drawn even when nothing was saved is [the sparse state](#the-sparse-state)'s rule.
- **The work list's controls are ONE row, read in the order a reader asks, and it is the only row above the work.** Order: what is drawn (shapes, strip); what narrows it (chips, ending in **+ Filter**, since the control that adds a narrowing follows the ones it adds to); at the far end how it is arranged (**Show**, the scope, and **Group by**, each the kit's quiet picker with its caption inside, "Show Open", spending no width on a label), a board's lanes out of view and the count; last the search box and **Display**. Two rows would cost every Work screen height: one row starts the list 41px higher at 1440px and 45px higher at 1280px beside the peek and on a phone.
  - Each group is one cluster: a narrow row wraps whole clusters, far end right-aligned, the search box shrinking to 140px first, never leaving the count or Display alone on a line.
  - **Display's Sort** is on every shape but the calendar: list and table are also ordered at their column heads, a board and timeline have none, so one picker offers every order the engine takes (on a board, titled with how to drag outside the manual order).
  - NOTHING ELSE sits between this row and the work. The Tasks introduction and the board's "cards move in the manual order" line each cost a row per visit to say something needed once: the first lives in these docs and the empty state, the second is said when somebody tries to drag outside the manual order.
  - On a phone the arrangement opens from Display (its glyph there): two lines (the drawing; "+ Filter" beside the count and tools), a third while a filter is on: the chips, the one run that scrolls sideways, fading the edge with more past it.
- **The landing shape is the CLIENT's fallback, not a builtin the engine marks `default`.** Why it is the list is under [the sparse state](#the-sparse-state). Exactly one view row may carry `default` and the applier settles that in the write's transaction; a builtin claiming it would collide with what a company saved, so `LANDING_SHAPE` holds when nothing claims it.
- **The trash is `removed=true`, which is what the engine says it is.** Its `ViewKeyTrash` says a view carrying that parameter *is* a trash listing. So it is a filter in the Filter menu, not a tab, and the grid takes the removals rather than a flag naming a tab; a trash of one project's bugs is expressible and every view saved with the parameter reads the same way.
  - `show_closed` travels with it: a removed task is very often finished, and the status predicate is ANDed otherwise, hiding every deletion of done work. On the list that is the Show segment's DEFAULT under `removed=true` (All, not Open), so the trash reads the same from the Filter menu or its own address; a Show picked on the bar still overrides it.
  - Its three extra columns APPEND to whichever set is active, so the trash is readable as a list. The removal's actor and instant come from the activity feed (the row carries no tombstone); a row the loaded feed page does not reach says which fact is missing rather than drawing a blank.
  - **Purged work has no row at all**: its history entry is the only evidence it existed and gets a band of its own saying it cannot be restored.
- **Where a WRITE is attributed, the kind of writer travels with the name.** The trash's `removed_by`, the log's actor and the directory's Last change all answer "who did this", and a person removing a task, an assistant removing a subtree and the engine repairing one look identical without it. The name is the grid's rule (**A person in a grid cell is a resolved name** under [Every list is one grid](#every-list-is-one-grid)); the kind is the clause those three cells share, `agent` the ordinary case, left unmarked. Spelled per cell, one checked against a word the engine does not mint and its tag was drawn on every trash row.
- **The list and the table are ONE grid with two column sets** ([Every list is one grid](#every-list-is-one-grid) applied to both). Worklet's own part is the KEYING: `cols.list=` and `cols.table=`, because a column set carries an order as well as a selection, and one key read against both would draw the list's columns in the table's arrangement, which no validation catches. `sort=` is shared: it is a fact about the QUESTION, not the drawing.
- **The table sorts at the ENGINE.** A header writes the query's own `sort=` key, so the whole set is ordered, not the hundred loaded rows. A column the grammar has no key for is NOT sortable, because the grammar refuses an unknown key (one wrong header would take the board down). Key, Status, Type and Assignee sort by meaning (a key's number, the board's status order, the catalogue's type order, a seat's name), which only the engine can give: a comparator over drawn cells would put `ENG-10` before `ENG-9`.
- **A column is headed in words.** Type and Assignee are each a word over a centred mark (glyph heads read as decoration and left no word for a sort button); the type's mark carries its name as tooltip and accessible name. A list held to one assignee (My work's Queue) draws that person on every row, so there Assignee is a column Display offers off, not drawn by default.
- **The four shapes ask four different questions of ONE grammar, each difference its own axis.**
  - Board: `group_by` and no cursor, since across columns there is no single order.
  - List and table: one page with a sort, same rows, grouping, hundred and cursor on Load more (a second arm for the table would copy one paging rule).
  - Calendar: a DATE RANGE and no grouping, because its axis IS the grammar's one `due` key: the month on screen spends it, the Overdue chip is not offered, the count says what it counted.
  - Timeline: a page of five hundred ordered by start; its window is derived from the rows present, so a later page may widen it (the only way to the 501st bar). A bar too narrow for its title carries it beside the bar on a plate of the strip's own ground (a week rule stops at its edge instead of striking through a word), on the side with room (before the bar near the strip's end), bounded by that room so it ellipsises.
  - No shape narrows differently: the FILTERS mean one thing on all four.
- **A view SETS the scope (the Show picker), and the scope is read once rather than per reader.** Open / Recent / Closed / All is the single authority on which finished work a read asks for (the status group, or Recent's `closed_since`): the screen spreads a view's saved parameters, then writes that key from the scope. A constant default made a view saved over closed work unrunnable, so the scope takes its DEFAULT from the chosen view: Recent where the view carries `closed_since`, and on a board that says nothing about finished work.
  - Two absences land on `Open`: a view naming no group is not a view asking for everything, and a group the scopes cannot express (`active` alone) has no reading answering it as saved, so `Open` is the wider set nearer what its author asked.
  - A view that WIDENED (`show_closed` with no group) opens on `All`; seeding `Open` would write the narrow group over the half the view asked for.
  - A `scope=` off the address naming none of the four reads as `All` in ONE place: spelled separately, a hand-edited `?scope=opne` drew an unset switch over every closed task, the combination the scope exists to prevent.
- **A row is a table, and its columns belong to the LIST.** This is the EMBEDDED list (a seat's queue, a person's day, an item's subtasks: the same compact row in somebody else's panel); the work screen's own list is the grid above. Tracks are declared on the list and each row takes them with `subgrid`, so a column is as wide as the widest value in it (a per-row grid sized `auto` tracks on that row alone and put a status badge at a different x on every line). The row keeps a CELL for a missing value: an undated, unassigned, unestimated task lines its status up with the task above rather than pulling later columns left.
  - List width is never a fact about the window (a subtask list is 420px in a peek on a 2000px screen), so the narrow track set is a container query over the list's own box, and the task page's rail-beside-column threshold is one over the page column (window less sidebar less an open peek).
  - The narrow set is declared ONCE beside the wide one: a track list is positional, so a second copy that missed a reordering gives every cell the wrong column silently.
- **A row's own inset comes out of the tracks at its ends.** A subgrid item's padding is SUBTRACTED from the first and last track it spans, and the row pads itself so hover tints edge to edge. A content-sized track gets it back; a fixed one does not, so a fixed opening track the same width as the inset resolves to nothing (the priority mark overflowed a zero-wide cell onto the key: `↑LEAD-3` read as one identifier). An end track states the inset as well as the column, in both sets.
- **A card is four fixed rows, and only the last one comes and goes.**
  - Identity row: the type, drawn only where not the default `task` (so a bug or milestone is what the eye finds across a lane), the key, the size and, at its end, the holder: a squircle for an agent, a circle for a person, the seat's STATE as the glyph on its corner. The dashed "nobody" square sits there when nobody holds the task.
  - Title, clamped to two lines.
  - Facts: priority, blocked, labels, due date, "blocks N" (live tasks waiting on this one), open questions and, at the end, the task's cost in TOKENS. A card on an untouched task has no fact row at all; the predicate deciding it restates each mark's own emptiness rule (the price of asking BEFORE rendering), so a mark that gains a field adds it there.
  - Last row, a STATE and the only hue on a card: blue while a seat's turn is on the task ("SWE · executing · 6m"), amber while an executor on it is parked waiting for the READER ("Waiting on you · executor parked"). The turn is joined on the item the engine CHARGES it to (`live_call.work_item`), never the trigger's `work_key`, which names whatever a webhook mentioned. An executor waiting on somebody else is a fact on the task page, not a call to this person.
  - Labels, "blocks N", open questions and tokens are opt-in row facts (`fields=`) the board asks for and no agent's listing carries.
- **A status is coloured by its GROUP.** Somebody on it (`in_progress` and `in_review` alike) is blue, finished is green, nothing happening is no hue. Amber is reserved across the product for NEEDS YOU, so `in_review` is not amber.
- **A drag is a write, made as the reader.** Dropping a card calls `place_work_item` as the session's principal, naming the card it went above (or the last card of the lane it went to the bottom of) and, across lanes, the lane's status, conditional on the card's version. Never an index: the engine mints the place between neighbours as the board stands when the move lands, and on the company's board a card of another project is no neighbour (a rank is an order within one project).
  - CONFIRMED, NOT OPTIMISTIC: the card is drawn where dropped with a pending mark, and the two lanes' counts move by one with it (a heading with the old tally over the moved card is two claims that disagree). A refusal puts card and counts back and says why in the engine's words; an applied move is re-read.
  - A lane change whose place was refused after the status landed (`placed: false`) stays in its new lane (snapping back would draw an untrue status) and the sentence says the place was not taken.
  - A drag moves cards only in the MANUAL order (a project's default, or Sort → Manual): in any other a dropped card jumps back to where its date puts it, reading as a refusal that was not one. `Alt` with an arrow is the keyboard gesture.
  - A drag in another order is caught (a card is a link, and an uncaught drag drags the browser's address) and answered with the order that moves cards, which the board's Sort title also says.
  - A reader the engine will not move cards for is told why once, above the lanes, in the sentence every write control uses.
- **A card's mark row is one line.** Priority, blocked, due, "blocks N" and open asks stay whole and the token count stays at the right end; the LABELS give way first, to a "+N" naming the rest in its title and to a screen reader.
- **A lane is headed by its status's own mark**: the ring while open, the check once delivered, in the status's tone (the mark the palette, a decision's task and a status-axis list band draw). A task TYPE is never drawn with either: `task` wearing the check made a list of unstarted work read as finished. `lib/work.ts` holds `TYPE_ICON` and `STATUS_SHAPE` apart, and a test says so.
- **A board shows whole lanes and names the rest.** A lane is sized from the board's width: as many whole lanes as fit at a 260px floor, sharing the width exactly with no gap after the last, so the scroller's edge falls between lanes, never through a card, and a scroll snaps to a lane's start. (A fixed 276px lane fitted four at one window width only: at 1440 the fourth ended 8px past the scroller, at 1280 Done was cut mid-title.)
  - Lanes past the edge are COUNTED at the bar's end in one phrasing at every width ("2 more lanes ›", "‹ 1 earlier lane"): a button that pages to them, with a shadow on that side. The names are its accessible name and tooltip (a bare "Cancelled, Closed" read as status words, not a control). A Recent board has six lanes and its scrollbar sits under its tallest lane, below the fold, so nothing else says the last two exist.
  - On a phone a lane is the screen less a gutter, and the next lane's edge is the cue.
- **A lane has a count, a ⋯ and a way to the rest.** The count is over the whole lane. ⋯ opens it as a list or puts it away (`hide=`, which the Display menu names and brings back: a hidden lane on a shared address is a column of work nobody can tell is missing). Past fifty cards the lane ends in "N more", the list narrowed to that lane ("N more this week" on a finished lane under Recent, all it holds there). A turn ending on a card the board draws means the card just changed, so the board asks again then, not a poll later.
- **A row is edited in place, as the reader.** A writer's list and table rows draw status, priority and holder as the same badge, mark and face a reader sees, each the trigger of a menu of its values (never a select in every row). Each change is `update_work_item` conditional on the version the row was drawn at (`if_match`): a change made a second ago is refused, not overwritten, and the refusal NAMES who made it ("changed by Maya since you opened it"), read from the task's newest history entry. A reader who cannot change tasks sees the values and one sentence above the grid saying why, not a hundred pickers that each refuse.
- **Every row is reachable.** A list and table are a page of a hundred, a calendar and timeline a page of five hundred; the rest follow the answer's cursor on **Load more** beside "N of M loaded". A busy calendar day's "+N more" is the list narrowed to that day, bounded by the READER's own midnights (the cell is the reader's day). `[` and `]` walk rows in DRAWN order (lanes left to right, bands top to bottom). A task opened from a list carries that list's question (`list=`), so its page asks the engine where it sits in the WHOLE answer (`around=`) and says "3 of 18" with the tasks either side, not counting the loaded page.
- **A filter's operator is the client's, and the wire gets a list.** Priority is / is not / ≥ is expanded on the way out (`≥ normal` is `priority=normal,high,urgent`) and read back off the list's shape, so a saved view stays a plain list any reader can run and a pasted link draws the chip that wrote it. Labels take the grammar's three modes: any (bare, the engine's default), all (`all:`), none (`none:`).
- **Every row is filtered on its own** (`subtasks=separate`), on every shape and over any saved view. The grammar's default filters ROOTS and lets subtrees ride along unfiltered, which suits a surface folding a tree under its root; no shape here draws one. Under it the Open list showed finished subtasks of open parents and a person's day showed subtasks somebody else held, with nothing on a flat row saying which matched. A task's own subtasks are its page's list.
- **A board draws every lane the scope admits, and a list draws only the bands that hold something.** On a closed axis (status, status group, priority, due bands) the engine's `work_items` carries every column the query's predicate could have put a row in, empty ones at `count: 0`: a young company's open work is three lanes with one card, and a Done lane appears only when finished work was asked for. This is the histogram's rule (every bucket drawn) applied to a board; the shapes differ only in DRAWING: a lane with room is what a board is, a band over nothing separates nothing from nothing.
  - Admission is the predicate's own. The due bands are WHEN work is due, cut on the COMPANY's midnight, not the reader's, so bands, the row's overdue flag and every `due=` filter cannot disagree about a task.
  - An empty scope says which: nothing open yet, nothing finished yet, nothing filed; "Nothing matches" is reserved for a filter actually on. The sentences and their screens are in [the sparse state](#the-sparse-state).
- **A board lane is a range, not a ceiling.** A lane stretches to the tallest lane's height, which answers a short column beside a long one only; a board of all-short lanes (one status, one card) closed the lane at 138px under its card like a stray panel. So a lane carries a floor of two cards' room as well as its scroll ceiling, and the floor wins under a viewport too short for both (a lane that holds one card and scrolls beats one too short to hold one).
- **Priority is signal bars, counted.** Three rising bars filled to the step: one for `low`, two for `normal`, three for `high`; `urgent` is the alert mark, not a fourth bar (urgent is not "more high"). The level is read by counting, so it takes no hue; only `urgent`'s mark is in the critical ink. (A column of chevrons reads as rows that fold.) Where the word is printed beside the mark (the task's header and properties rail) it takes the size and ink of the values around it: priority is a setting there, not a warning.
- **Every step of the scale is drawn.** `normal` is two bars of three on every card and row, as the approved Board draws it; blank, the column was mostly empty, the two-bar state never appeared, and a blank could not be told from a value that never arrived. Urgent rows still stand out as the only alert mark among bars. `none` (the engine's "nobody said") is not a step and draws nothing. A due date drops the year it shares with the reader, because one year repeated down forty rows hides the one row due next year.
- **Reading an item does not lose the board.** A plain click opens a PEEK beside the rows; ⌘-click and middle-click follow the anchor to the item's page (a card that cannot open in a tab is not a link). The peek is the FRAME's: mounted by the shell, addressed by `peek=`; the list only publishes the order `[` and `]` walk (otherwise a rail would step through somebody else's rows).
  - Below the frame's threshold (1158 px at the normal density on a screen like this one; arithmetic at `peekColumnMin` in `app/layout.ts`) it becomes a DRAWER over the content. The threshold governs every screen's peek, so it turns on what all share: a LIST too narrow to read, floor 444px, plus everything in front of it at the reader's density.
  - There is no board-specific threshold (a 292px lane, "overlay below about 1500"): that measured a peek Worklet's screen once owned as its own body-grid column. A board's answer to a narrow body is fewer whole lanes and a pager (see **A board shows whole lanes** above), so the list, not the board, sets the number.
- **The item's peek is the page's header with NO facts under it.** A header and a properties rail stacked in one 420px column say Status, Type and Assignee twice within a hundred pixels, pushing the description down. The page keeps its fact line because its rail is BESIDE the header. The peek resolves its own people: the frame mounts it from a `peek=` token knowing no org chart, so a peek taking the list's chrome got `{}` and drew raw handles while the page named them.
- **A group of absences is ONE sentence, and the caller decides that.** A heading, a hairline and four dashes cost four lines to say nothing is scheduled, so the properties rail takes a `whenAllAbsent` line per group and draws it instead. The rail never does it by itself: a rail of annotation rows would collapse to one sentence the day somebody cleared them, with nobody having decided that. The other three absences stay distinct (a row DROPPED, a row that is a DASH, a row that says something): [Honest empty states](#honest-empty-states) inside one panel.
- **Every project the company has is a page, and its segment is the ENGINE's question.** `shown=active|archived|all` is a SCREEN segment and `archived=` the engine's three-mode enum; one mapping object between them, since collapsing them would put `archived=only` in a shared route or invent a second name for an engine mode. The segment SELECTS a set rather than narrowing a wider one: filtered here, the page past the engine's own 200 held no archived row and Archived said "No project is archived" of a company that retired dozens. The sort travels for the same reason (applied after a capped answer it orders survivors of the key order). So a column the engine cannot order by is not sortable: Lead is resolved against the org chart at read time and Worklet holds no chart.
- **A census on the segments is what stops the directory guessing.** One set per segment makes an empty answer ambiguous (no projects, or all archived), so the engine sends BOTH counts under the same narrowing the rows were read under, never derived from rows (on Active no archived row is on screen). The empty state then says how many are archived and links to them, and a company with nothing filed is sayable from Active.
- **The log pages BACKWARD, and says when it is holding still.** The history screen is the event log's frame: a window, an axis, then rows, with three facet rails: the KIND of change, who made it, and which PROJECT (the narrowing a project's History lens already is, reachable company-wide). Paging was the one borrowed part missing: it printed that older changes existed and said to narrow the window, which moves the NEWEST edge and reaches fewer, newer rows. **Load older changes** fetches instead, and once a head is held the foot says the pages are held still (until then false: the first page is re-asked on every poll).
- **The bars are ours and the rows are the engine's, and the screen says which.** The event log asks the engine for its histogram; this question has no such read, so the axis is bucketed from the pages held. The caption says the bars cover the changes LOADED, the bar says the same about its pickers' counts (once, not under each facet rail, which the one compact bar replaced), and the histogram takes that scope as a REQUIRED prop so the screen-reader sentence cannot drift from the card's. A client-side count dressed as the engine's is never done.
- **ONLY A SCREEN PUBLISHES TO THE FRAME.** The log is a screen at `#/worklet/history` and a lens inside a project; the frame has one coverage slot with one setter. A body publishing inside another screen fought that screen's answer (on a project's history lens both wrote it, the last poll won, and switching to Tasks cleared the slot over a page still showing a project). The lens publishes nothing and states its rows' coverage inline, as the Tasks lens does. The publisher is a COMPONENT, not a bare call, because the rule is conditional and a hook may not be: called with nothing, the publish writes null over what the enclosing screen published.
- **A project opens on its work.** The Tasks lens is the list at the top of the page, as the approved Board draws a project: no container header above the work and no row of lenses; the lenses sit on the page bar beside the name they are lenses on (`Worklet › ENG Core · Tasks | About
  | History | Files`, `PageLenses`, the chips All projects' lenses wear too), controlling the region below by id. What the container IS (lead, unit, target, census, vocabulary, latest changes) is the **About** lens; a finding on the project's own record (a unit the chart lost) is drawn over every lens, being a fact about the work below.
  - The page bar ends with **New task** (filed into this project) and **Edit project**: the lead's target date, default assignee and archive, a company write (`write_project`) whose authority the engine decides (the project's lead or an admin), held with that rule's sentence for anybody else before anything is chosen (`projectEditHold`), titled with the project's NAME and confirmed with the day as the Target fact writes it ("Set Core's target to 30 Oct 2026", never ISO).
  - A project that declares no purpose says so for a person ("Add a purpose in Structure."), not a configuration key in backticks.
- **A lens keeps its filters.** The lenses (Tasks, About, History, Files) are readings of ONE container, so switching keeps the narrowing AND the arrangement: `lens=` is written through the frame's section move, which copies the whole current query and sets one key. A lens building a fresh query would make History a one-way trip, and fail silently since each lens renders fine alone. Only Tasks carries a count, from the project's maintained census: About is a description, and History is PAGED, so a loaded-page count would read as the lens's count.
- **The charts answer the questions the numbers cannot.** A census bar says how far along a project is where four counts say only sizes; a load bar is drawn against the HEAVIEST QUEUE on screen, not an absolute ceiling (thirty is heavy in one company, a quiet week in another). All wear STATUS tones, not the categorical hues, so one fact is never two colours on one screen.
- **A progress meter is the SPLIT of the work, and its whole is stated.** The project census is the kit's `SegmentedMeter` over the maintained `task_counts`: done (success tone) and active (info tone; `in_review` is working) as parts, what is still to do as the quiet remainder, against the whole `todo + active + done`, so the parts ARE the census and the accessible name reads them ("3 done, 2 active, 6 to do of 11"). Closed work is not in the whole: it left the question and has its own column. (An amount of done over everything drew waiting and started work as one blank; a share drew a project holding one open item as finished.) The legend names the three parts in the meter's own tokens. `dashboard/src/routes/worklet/census.tsx` draws the one meter in the About lens's header, the peek and the directory's Progress column (beside the lead's Target date), so they cannot disagree about one row.

---

## The turn trace: four tabs, one clock

`#/live/turns/{id}` is where every deep link to a turn lands. It answers *what did this turn do, in order and how long* and *what is it doing now*. Its header says where the turn is and what a reader can do about it; its body is four tabs (`tab=timeline|transcript|context|tools`).

**The two readings are two kinds of link.** A link into a turn's RECORD (a list row, a settled turn's *Trace*, a monitor's row on Home's Live now and Live › Now running) opens the Timeline, the default tab. A link whose job is to WATCH a running turn opens the **Transcript** (`?tab=transcript`, `lib/turns.ts`' `watchLink`), where the running phase is drawn OPEN with its rounds arriving. Those links are every **Watch live** (a seat's current turn card, its profile's page bar and peek, a task's live row and page bar), the sidebar's **Running** group, `g r` and ⌘K's **Running now**.

**A parked turn is watched on the same tab.** Its executor launched in its box and the turn suspended, so no phase is in flight while the engine still calls the seat working (most of the turn, for hours on a long one). While parked, the Transcript leads with an **Executor** card: its live output (the same `executor_tail` poll the Timeline's launch span opens, read off the waterfall's own open launch span), the harness, and **Open the executor** to `#/live/executors/{turn_id}`; the executor's card it parked in is drawn open beneath. 

**The page moves once, on arrival, and only for a reader who has not moved it.** The live phase's ledger tails its newest round at the bottom of a box as tall as the view; under the header and cards above, that bottom landed below the fold. When the page is reached on the Transcript and the turn's answer has landed (stored phases draw above the live one, so earlier the box would still move), the shell's scroller (`lib/scroller.ts`) moves until that box's bottom is in view and never past its top, and only if it is still at the top. Never on a later push, and never by `scrollIntoView`, which scrolls every ancestor that can.

- **The trail names the turn the way its task does.** On a work item it reads *Live › {agent} › Turn n · KEY*: the ordinal comes off the task's own turn list (`work_item_turns`, asked by the task's id and walked a page at a time until the turn is found; a turn still running is the next after the newest; before any of that is known it is *Turn · KEY*, never a guessed number; see [An item's address](#an-items-address)). Off a task it is the lead of what the turn did. The agent crumb leads to *Live* narrowed to that seat.
- **The status is state, beside the title.** *Running · 6m 12s* off the turn's own start; *Parked while its executor runs*; how it ended, in the reviewer's or executor's word; or *not settled* for a turn no seat is running that published no closing record (its node stopped before it ended; the turns list's *Not settled*). Also the attempt, the problem count and *middle not shown* for a capped read. The facts under it:
  - the trigger;
  - where the turn is: *Execute* with *round 3 of 25* as its note while running (the round its engine last ANNOUNCED, see the Timeline below), *Execute → Review* with its iterations as the note once over, so the value holds one line;
  - tokens in and out, with the workers outside them;
  - the share of input the prompt cache served (**absent, not 0%, when no phase reported one**: a provider reporting none and a cache serving nothing are one wire value);
  - tool calls (a collected executor's calls its record did not keep are included, counted as its round counts them, said in the fact's note);
  - workers;
  - the node that ran it (the answer's `nodes`);
  - wall clock: the engine's own measurement, or on a turn with no closing record the waterfall's window, so the header and the Turn row never print two lengths.

  A fact's note sits under its own value (`.fact-body`), never on a band a neighbour's two-line value can push away.
- **The actions are the turn's.** *Steer* sends a note the turn reads at its next step (`steer_turn`): offered on every turn still going, a parked one included (its note waits on the executor's record), held with the reason only on a turn that has ended. The toast says when it is read, from the answer's `reads`: *at its next step*, or for an executor waiting on a question *once that is answered* (`lib/steer.ts`). What became of a note is the turn's own `agent_turn_steered`, drawn under the waterfall and where it was read: at the round (*read at round 2 of Review*), or for a read inside a launch, on the launch's bar, in the words of its step, owned by the phase whose executor it was: *read by the executor in Execute, in its brief*, *after a tool batch*, *as it was finishing*, *at its next step*. A step a newer build names and this one does not is *read by the turn in Execute*, on the launch's bar where its record names the launch, never drawn or said as a round. A note a later launch's brief told again after a step that never handed it over is *read by the executor in Execute, in its brief, told again after a step that never handed it over*. The other ends, each tagged with its word:
  - *expired*: *the turn finished before it read the note*.
  - *missed*: *taken for the executor in Execute, after a tool batch, but it never reached it* (a hook's serves all lost, a serve's session proving it absent); *taken at round 2 of Review but never handed over* for a review's take whose answer was lost; *taken by the turn in Execute, but it never reached its reader* at a step a newer build names. Drawn at that step, badge *Your note was taken here and never reached its reader*.
  - *unconfirmed*: *handed to the executor in Execute, at its next step, which never confirmed reading it (its session may hold it)*, on the launch's bar (including a note whose every lost serve its harness gave up, since the answer can outrun the cancel). The bar's badge says each end at its step.
  - An end a newer build names and this one does not: *this version of the dashboard cannot say what became of it*, drawn nowhere.

  *Pause* is the seat's (with *Also stop the current turn*); *Open task* is its item, by the task's id, since a turn's item carries no word on whether its key is one another task claimed first. One menu (*More on this turn*) holds the other attempts, the traces, and the turn as JSON: *Copy turn as JSON* and *Download turn as JSON*, each saying what it did in a toast. On a phone Steer stays in view and the rest folds into the frame's *More*.
- **Timeline is a waterfall on the engine's own clock** (`lib/waterfall.ts`). Every instant is one the engine measured (each round's model call, tool call, phase, the prefetch, an executor's launch):
  - a phase's harness runs under it, each a **Harness run N** span from launch to exit (`invocations[]`) with its rounds under it; its detail gives the entry that served it, the rounds it made, whether its harness's record showed them, how it ended and what it spent. A run still going is drawn open from its launch (`run_started_at`), saying what it made lands when its harness exits;
  - a round's tool calls follow its model call (a call the engine timed but did not stamp is run serially from the model's answer and says it was *placed*);
  - a delegate's workers and the round-cap judge sit under the round that spawned them (`host_round`);
  - each executor launch is its own **Launch** span keyed by its `launch_id`;
  - the reflection pass after the last phase: its workers drawn from what each SPENT, one span per `auxiliary_spend` record of the `reflection` stage from first call to last, marked where a call failed;
  - *review pending* while an executor has finished and no reviewer has started.

  The ROUND IN FLIGHT is drawn only from a start the engine announced: a request is in flight from the frame published as its run opens or as the last call of the response before it is answered. `round_started_at` stays the previous round's while that round's tools run, so a start no later than the last recorded round's is that round's tools, never "the next round" drawn minutes early. Several calls of one response running side by side are each drawn running (`running_calls`). The Turn row ends at the turn's own measurement; the reflection pass, which runs after it, trails the bar. A parked turn is one turn: the phase spans the run it waited on. A record that cannot be placed is listed as **not placed on this clock**, never drawn at an invented place. Whether a call was measured is one answer shared with the Tools tab: a submission done inside a millisecond is `0ms` on both, never "not timed" on one.

  The bars carry no hue of their own (a model call solid, a tool call lighter, a container a thin rule); colour only says state: running (a drifting stripe, still under reduced motion), failed, selected. The ruler counts offsets from the turn's start on a 1-2-5 step, as many marks as its measured width has room for (64px a label), so a phone's track reads `0 · 50s`; every label is in the duration column's one format (`500ms`, `1.5s`, `10s`, `1m 40s`, never `10 s`). On a phone the indent halves and the model name beside a round steps aside so the span's own name stays readable. `SpanBar`, `TimeAxis` and `NowLine` (`components/time/`) are this product's compositions on the kit's tokens.
- **A span opens beside the waterfall** (`span=`) from a laptop's page width (a 960px page container; the laptop's is about 1024), and under it on a phone or with the peek open, where the opened span is scrolled into view and focused since it would land below the fold. The rows are one tab stop: Up, Down, Home and End move between them, Enter opens one, Escape closes the open span and returns focus to its row. A span's kind is its eyebrow only where the title does not already say it. It gives the span's offsets on the turn's clock and what only that kind has: a model call's words and tokens; a tool call's input and output, with **Why {agent} called it**, the narration of the ROUND that asked for it, labelled *from round N*, and *this round asked for K calls* where it asked for more than one (a sentence under one of four calls would otherwise read as that call's alone); a launch's box facts, and its transcript once collected.
- **An executor running in its box is watched, not replayed.** While its launch's span is open the trace asks the node that can read the box for its live output every three seconds (`executor_tail`, see [Watching a run live](../concepts/code-sandbox.md#watching-a-run-live)), and only then. Closing the span or the executor stopping ends the poll, and only `not_running` is stopping. These keep asking and keep what is on screen: a launch still being set up (`launching`), a box paused before its record moves on (`box_paused`), a box gone before its record moves on, the launch recorded lost and its round carried on in a fresh one (`box_gone`), a silent node, a failed read. The one failed read that ends the poll is a refusal the engine says no wait clears (`unavailable` whose `retry_after` is zero: a sandbox setup somebody has to fix), since every ask would be answered the same and logged on the node that reads the box; a reconnect, or opening the view again, asks again. A failed read is told in the engine's own sentence (`QueryState`, as every screen tells one), never by its code, over what the view already shows.
  - **The view holds what it was sent.** It asks by CURSOR (the reading it holds, how far, and the host's digest there) and APPENDS what the box's host says it lacks, or replaces what it holds on a reset. `lib/useLiveTail.ts` is that hook, not `useQuery`, because the cursor moves with every answer and a cursor in a query's parameters re-runs its effect the moment an answer lands. It holds at most what the launch's record will (`LIVE_OUTPUT_MAX_BYTES` in `contract/executor.ts`, the engine's `sandbox.MaxRunTextBytes`, held to it by a gate), dropping its FRONT on a line past that; the caption says how much earlier output it no longer holds, every figure read from the answer or the view's own count, never spelled on the screen. A delta that does not follow what the view holds is never spliced in: the view keeps its text and asks for a reset.
  - **It follows the end unless the reader scrolled up.** At the bottom (within about a line, `FOLLOW_SLACK_PX`) the block scrolls to each new line; anywhere else it stays.
  - Bytes the box's host holds back until their redaction is settled (a line not finished, a private key whose end has not been written) are counted under the block, not shown.
  - *No output yet* and *node-b didn’t answer* are different sentences; the second names the node. A screen reader is told the tail's STATE (one status-region sentence, changing only with the state), never the output or the "read just now" clock.
- **Notes sent to a turn** name their sender as a seat's name, as every other attribution does, and say what became of each (read at a round, or expired) without assuming the reader sent it.
- **A turn with no closing record** is *running* while a seat is on it and *not settled* when none is (the same reading on the trace, the Live turns list and a seat's Turns section), and neither while the live view is disconnected, when there are no seats to ask.
- **Transcript** is the phase cards and the story bands above: the first phase open and, while the turn runs, the phase it is on. A card opens as it MOUNTS when its phase is live, so a phase that starts while the page is open arrives open, and one that completes keeps its card and open state (phase cards latch; the reader's own open and close is never overridden). **Context** is what woke the turn and what its prompt was assembled from. **Tools** is every execution with where it ran (built in, or the MCP server), each row opening its span on the Timeline, and above the rows how many more calls a collected executor made that its record did not keep, by tool, as a call's span counts them among the calls its round asked for.
- **The answer is the fleet's.** A node that did not answer the turn read is named above the tabs. The answer is asked again whenever one of the turn's phases lands on the stream, its seat's stage changes, or its reflection pass's `reflection_completed` lands, because what the phases do not carry (a run's announcement, a note's outcome, what the auxiliary model spent, the reflection) arrives only in the answer. The engine publishes a turn's in-turn `auxiliary_spend` before its end and a pass's before its sentinel, so the asks at those two moments read them.


## Executors, agent-to-agent, traces and the event log

The four Live screens beside Now running and the turns are each a list and a page, and each page draws ITS OBJECT ALONE: `#/live/executors/{turn_id}` and `#/live/a2a/{id}` never draw the whole list with the object tacked on under it.

- **Executors** reads the executors' durable record (`executors`) merged with the live projection, on ONE poll, `RUNS_POLL_MS` (20 s) in `lib/runs.ts`. The board, an executor's page and rail, and the attention queue Home and the Inbox draw all name it, so the board and the Inbox cannot disagree about whether anybody is being waited on (a source test holds every reader to it).
  - A parked executor's banner says what it asked, **who it is put to** (the audience the engine resolved when it parked, by name, and the lead chain when the harness's label named nobody), how long its box is held, and carries **Answer**: `answer_executor{turn_id, launch_id, choice}` for an option, or `{turn_id, launch_id, answer}` for words, which reaches it whatever launched it. `pending` is the ordinary outcome: the answer is on the seat's inbox and the node holding the seat launches the executor again with it.
  - A running executor's page polls its live output from the node that owns it (`executor_tail`, by the `launch_id` the row names, every 3 s while the page is open; the same `LiveOutput` the turn trace draws). The view is keyed on the turn AND the launch, so a later launch starts its own view rather than appending to the last one's. An answer naming the launch `replaced` reads the board again at once, so the page follows the launch the row holds now rather than waiting out `RUNS_POLL_MS`.
  - An executor's row is deleted once its launch is collected, and its page still answers: it reads the turn and draws every `executor_collected` its launches published, under *What the executor did* or *What launch N of M did*: what each reported, what it delivered, its tokens and its transcript, named by the task its `executor_launched` carried. A launch given a repository on Gitlet it could push to adds **Pushed** to its section: what its push record says it moved, a chip per ref (`web:feature/x`), followed by the change that branch heads, named by its reference (`web!42`) and opening the change's page. Refs past the record's bound are counted; a record that could not be read says why rather than reading as nothing pushed.
  - Beside a peek the board keeps the seat and the task and drops the harness, the placement and the box, in that order, saying so in its footer.
  - The page reads two sources, and "none" needs BOTH: only when the executor's record and the turn both answered and neither holds one does it say there is none, headed **No executor**. A source that could not be read is named in a warning over whatever the other holds, never folded into "none". "No task was recorded" heads only a real executor whose launch carried no task.
- **Agent-to-agent**: a channel is an authorization record (the pair, the count and the window), so its page reads the words from the log: the channel's own events (`events{channel_id}`), oldest first, a conversation read top down. "Read this channel's events" and "Open in the event log" are the log narrowed to the channel, `#/live/events?channel={id}`. An id the record does not hold is ONE not-found state carrying that link, not a second empty events card under it; the events card still appears when the log holds what crossed a channel whose record is gone.
- **A trace** has no list. Its page states each number once in its header (events, spans, elapsed, when it began, failures) and draws ONE ROW PER EVENT, nested by the span that carried it. A span is not an event: every event of one phase carries that phase's span id, so a tree keyed on the span id would draw one phase's last event over and over and lose the rest. A span holds its events, appears once under its parent, and its events and child spans are interleaved by time. A failed event is marked as the event log marks it: the danger edge and the warning glyph. Each row places its event on a **lane**, a rail spanning the trace's first event to its last with a mark at the event's instant, on a fixed-width track so every row's lane is the same scale; a trace whose events share one instant draws no lane. On a phone the sentence wraps. A node that did not answer is named. "In the log" is the log narrowed to the trace, `#/live/events?trace={id}`.
- **The event log** asks the ENGINE for every filter but the text search: category, actor, seat, one trace, one channel and "Failures only" (`failed=true`) narrow the axis and every page alike, and the live rows are narrowed by the same values each row carries (a live row carries its seat and channel exactly as the store's columns hold them). The search box is the one filter over what is loaded, and an empty search says older pages may still match. The end of the pages is the end of what was ASKED: "No older event in this window matches these filters" under a filter, "That is the oldest event in this window" without; never the store's retention, which a 24-hour window over a thirty-day store does not reach. A node that did not answer is named above the list. The list draws A PAGE AT A TIME: the newest hundred rows, and "Load 100 older" draws the next hundred from what the tab already holds (the live rows and every page fetched) before it asks the engine for more, so the end of the pages is said only once every row held is drawn. A row is drawn again only when it changes: a pushed event draws its own row, and a passing second draws only the relative times whose words moved.
- **An identifier in a header** (an event's wire type, its trace id) is a TOKEN fact (`Fact.token`): it takes two of the fact line's tracks on one line and is cut with an ellipsis, its whole value in the title, only where two are still too narrow. The clamp every other fact takes would split `turn.guard_breach` as "turn.guard_breac" over "h".

### A refusal is read, never parsed

Every refused HTTP request answers the same three-part [envelope](api-endpoints.md#every-refusal-is-one-envelope), and the client treats each part as exactly one kind of thing:

- **`message` is rendered VERBATIM.** It is product copy the engine holds one sentence of per code, so the client shows it as sent: never reworded, never truncated into a toast title, never prefixed with the code. Nothing branches on it or matches its text, so a copy improvement in the engine cannot break a screen.
- **The detail is what the client KEYS ON.** Everything beside `error` and `message` is machine-readable and typed, so a screen reads the field it needs and acts: `fields` puts a marker beside each input an integration is still missing, `problems` puts a located failure beside the line of the document it is about, `current_revision_id` tells a lost update from a stale form, a `503`'s `refusal` names the state log's reason.
- **`error` decides WHICH screen state it is**, because it is the only closed set of the three. A code the client does not know is rendered with the engine's `message` and no behaviour attached, so a refusal nobody anticipated still reads as a sentence, not a blank.

A refusal with no `message` (a route whose code has not joined the shared vocabulary yet) falls back to the client's own line for that code, the same table the socket's query errors use.

---

## The Gitlet workspace

The Gitlet workspace is the company's git repositories as the engine hosts them ([Gitlet](../concepts/gitlet.md)), and the changes proposed to them: a Workspace row after Worklet, `g g`, landing on **Changes** at `#/gitlet`, its sections drawn as tabs in the page header. The tabs count the company's live changes, its repositories and the entries its merge queues hold, from one `code_counts` question each section page asks; a part the engine did not answer draws no figure, never a zero. The workspace is drawn only where the company hosts code in the engine (`services.code` on the org projection) and is hidden, never locked, where it is `none`, an address under it answered by the service notice. It names the **Gitlet** access (ADR-0110): every section reads the code questions (the changes, the repositories, a search, the pushes, the queues, the checks), which the engine refuses a reader without it before reading anything, so the sidebar's row is locked for that reader, as Worklet's is, and the frame draws its one refusal in place of every Gitlet page. For a holder, the engine holds each answer to their own grant on the repository, leaving out of a listing what they may not read, and a write here carries its own reason where it is held: every code write is held for a reader without the access, saying "This change needs Gitlet access. An admin can give it to you.". A change's peek (`peek=change:web!42`, over any page) is not locked by the frame: it asks, as every peek does, and draws the engine's `403` to a reader without Gitlet.

A change and its conversation are the engine's ([Changes](../concepts/gitlet.md#changes), [Reviews and findings](../concepts/gitlet.md#reviews-and-findings)), and reviewing one here is walked through in [Review a change](../guides/gitlet.md#review-a-change). What a record about a change leaves a person is a notice in the Inbox, never a screen of this workspace ([The Inbox is where you act](#the-inbox-is-where-you-act)), and who hears of what is the engine's routing ([Who a change wakes](../concepts/gitlet.md#who-a-change-wakes)).

- **Changes** is `code_changes`, paged in the order of the ONE index its filters lead (a work item's changes, an owner's in a state, a repository's, the company's in a state, or those waiting on somebody). A page is what the engine READ: it can be short or empty with a cursor, and is never re-sorted. **The engine keeps no index of every change**: a listing must name a state, repository, work item, reviewer, need or window, and is refused naming none.
  - Default is the OPEN changes (`state=`, `CHANGE_STATES`, held to `gitlet.ChangeStates`). **Every state** is offered only where a repository, work item, reviewer, need, window or words narrow the walk; elsewhere it is said, never sent.
  - `waiting-on:` is the engine's `needs` (`CHANGE_NEEDS`, held to `gitlet.Needs`): on me, a review, a fix, a person.
  - `updated:` is the engine's `window` (`CHANGE_WINDOWS`, held to `gitlet.ChangeWindows`): moved in the last day, week or month. Beside every state or a merged or closed one, with nothing else narrowing, the engine walks its two indexes of that instant, newest move first. Beside a live state (open, draft) it walks that state's changes and tests the window on each: newest move first, or newest opening first where Sort asks Newest (default where an owner or work item narrows, whose index lists by opening).
  - `repo=`, `owner=`, `reviewer=` are also picked in the list's head (a repository the reader may read, a seat from the chart).
  - **The query bar** holds filters as qualifiers (`is:`, `author:`, `reviewer:`, `repo:`, `waiting-on:`, `readiness:`, `updated:`, `work:`), parsed in the browser into address keys; other words are searched by the engine in titles and descriptions (`text=`). A search says how whole it was (`changes_text`): how far back a still-building index reaches, or that it is catching up or read only the newest; a node that ignored the words is said, its rows not drawn.
  - **A row** (`CodeList`): state glyph; title with tags (waiting on you, queue place or taken out, changes requested, open findings, draft); the placing line; facts: head's checks counted and failures named, readiness, reviewers' faces with verdicts, comments, last move.
  - **State tabs** count the scope (company or picked repository, `code_counts`), never other filters. **Sort** is `CHANGE_SORTS`: Recently updated wherever the walk can order by it (Newest where an owner or work item narrows), held and said elsewhere; the address keeps density. A pairing the engine refuses (a need beside an ended state, Waiting on me beside an owner or reviewer) is said, never sent.
  - **Readiness** narrows open changes to where their merge stands (`READINESS_BUCKETS`, held to `gitlet.ReadinessBuckets`) or to those waiting on a person (`needs=person`); an answer without `narrowed_to` is from a node that ignored the key: said, rows not drawn.
  - **Waiting on you** lists `needs=me` with why each waits (an owner's ask names the paths the reader owns); a reader bound to no seat sees what waits on a person.
  - A row opens the peek (`peek=change:web!42`), which reads `code_change`: branches, owner, revisions, work item (owner's other open changes and every change of the item, one link each), readiness (every precondition in the engine's order, `PRECONDITION_KINDS` and `PRECONDITION_STATES`, held to `gitlet.PreconditionKinds` and `gitlet.PreconditionStates`, with state and the engine's sentence), conversation counts and authors. A reference typed in ⌘K (`web!42`) opens the page, parsed by the engine's grammar; the peek's Open leads there too.
  - Each precondition is a checklist line: glyph (check met, alert unmet, dashed ring while computing; first two in the state's ink, word said to a screen reader), condition, the sentence of what it waits on.
- **A change's page**, `#/gitlet/repos/{name}/changes/{n}` (mirrors the engine's REST path `/gitlet/repos/{name}/changes/{n}`), is laid out as a code host lays one out.
  - Header: reference and title, a live change's readiness meter (the one every listing draws), one sentence: state pill, who wants to merge which revision of which branch into which (or merged/closed it), branch chips that open their code with a copy of the source's name, when opened/merged/closed, work item. Tabs: **Conversation**, **Revisions**, **Checks**, **Files changed**, **More**, each with a glyph, keys 1 to 5 in that order; the row ends in the head's diffstat.
  - It reads `code_change` a part at a time: the detail rides the first page of revisions; each tab asks the part it draws, a code question at the tab's floor. The detail is read every minute; a part is asked again only when the detail says what it reads moved. For a revision's files and a file's patch (git on the home Gitlet node): the change's version, the revision's head and the base its facts record (a retarget's new facts move after the version). For other parts: the change's and its conversation's versions.
  - **Conversation** is ONE TIMELINE down a rail, in the order records landed on the code log, never by a node's clock.
    - Description first, a card by its owner; its menu: **Edit** (title and description in one `code_update_change`, only moved fields, held while the words on screen moved under the reader), **Copy link**, **Quote** (into the comment box).
    - Each revision pushed: a row with disc, head and **Compare with** the one before (`since=`).
    - Each review: a row whose disc wears its verdict's tone (changes requested danger, approval success, comment neutral), verdict in words beside it, summary and findings in a box under. With a change row's verdict corner and a rail reviewer's mark, these are the only places a verdict takes a hue; elsewhere it stays words.
    - Each finding is a card (`change/Finding.tsx`, shared with Files changed) with surrounding lines as its revision's diff marks them (`part=excerpts`, read again only when somebody reviews), its own lines marked, a suggestion as a small diff.
    - Each standing ask for review is a row where made: by whom, of whom, when, a path owner's with the paths it owns ("earlier" past the notices' horizon); a withdrawn ask says so.
    - Each thread: a card beside its writer's face with replies, a one-line reply growing as written, **Resolve conversation**.
    - After a break, the MERGE BOX, its disc on the spine: a section per question the gate asks (reviews, checks, findings, facts with when measured, whether it merges, then any condition none of those holds), each disc toned as the readiness meter tones it. Each check shows its latest attempt of the head (`code_checks` with `latest`), duration or running time, whether required, and opens the check pane. **Re-request**, **Re-run failed checks**, **Rebase**, **Take out of the queue** sit in the section they act on; then the method, **Delete its branch**, **Close** its work item, the count and what it waits on, **Merge** or **Add to queue**, **Override**, and a line saying what the press will do. A merged change's box says into what, by whom, how (`merged_via`), with Revert; a closed one's why.
    - Then the reader's comment in the kit's markdown editor (Write, Preview), sent on Mod+Enter, face on the spine.
  - The RAIL: whom the change asked for review (`part=reviewers`, read with the timeline's asks, paged), each with **Request**, a re-request and their standing verdict (participants', else reviews loaded) in tone and words; readiness (meter, what it waits on); work item, owner, branches with the target's protected tag (`code_refs` in detail), head, checks, participants, reference, whether its newest records notified the reader.
  - The engine pages reviews, comments, asks, findings and excerpts oldest first, so what a page leaves out is the newest. **Load more** under the timeline asks each part's page after its cursor; the timeline is built over every page loaded, so a later-page reply joins its root. Asks are repeated as the change or its conversation moves; every loaded page of reviews, comments, findings and excerpts is re-read only when somebody wrote on the change (the conversation's `spoken_at`, beside the part's count), never on a push or a mergeability its home recorded, which write none of them: a busy target branch re-checks every live change into it, and each held page would be re-read on every push.
  - **Files changed** is the revision's files (`rev=`, head by default; `since=` reads what changed since an earlier revision, the engine's interdiff), paged; **Load more files** asks the page after the cursor.
    - Every file is one STACK, each under a head sticking below the toolbar, patches walked a page at a time as the reader reaches them; a file jumped to is read alone; a file past 400 changed lines is folded until asked. Each hunk opens with git's header; **Expand** reveals hidden lines from the file's blob by its id; `t` goes to a file.
    - **Viewed** on a file's head marks it viewed at the state shown (`code_mark_viewed`); viewed files fold and read unviewed again once a revision changes them; the toolbar counts viewed.
    - **Filter files** and **Filter options** (extensions, With findings from findings counted by path, Unviewed) narrow tree and stack (`q=`, `ext=`, `only=`).
    - The stack (`routes/gitlet/FileStack.tsx`) is shared by a change's files, a commit and a comparison; a change's notes are drawn on its lines by the change page alone.
    - Beside it, the files' tree in its own scroller: directories (a run of single-child directories folded into one row), each file's name, badges (standing findings on its path, the reader's drafts), diffstat-sign counts, status square in the kit's file ink; the kit's tree model, grouped and never re-sorted, so a later page lands each file in its own directory; the file whose head is stuck is marked.
    - Each file's patch as git wrote it under its head (path, what became of it, counts, a menu with the way to the file at the revision's head), in its own `DiffView`, `layout=unified` or `split` (or one file alone split from its menu). A patch past one answer is paged; **Load more lines** asks the next page from the cursor; hunks are drawn from every page read (`lib/patchPages.ts`).
    - Every finding the engine placed in that revision (`gitlet.PlaceFindings`, the rule a seat's `code_get_change` reads by) is a card under its last line (weight, subject, title, who raised it and when; accent bar on its line; suggestion as a small diff). Every thread on a line sits under it; findings and comments past their first page load by **Load more findings and comments** above the diff, each part's next page at one press. What has no line here (a finding whose lines changed, outdated; one whose file is gone; a thread on another revision) is drawn above the diff under a Disclosure that counts it, never dropped.
    - **On the head, a reviewer picks lines by their numbers** and drafts a finding: weight and subject in the engine's words (`FINDING_SEVERITIES`, `FINDING_CATEGORIES`, held to `gitlet.Severities` and `gitlet.Categories`), title, body and, on the newer side, the lines it suggests in their place. A draft is the TAB'S, kept in `sessionStorage` per change and revision, a dashed card edited in place or dropped (one on a line the patch does not draw stands above its diff), until **Approve**, **Request changes** or **Comment** (page bar's Review, or **Finish review**, the tab's one primary, counting drafts) sends every draft of the head in ONE `code_review_change` with the verdict, a summary and the reviewer's own standing findings (each checked, since a review of a later revision supersedes every standing finding of the reviewer's it leaves out). Those are the engine's `standing` part, read to its last page; the press is held, with why, while that read is out or refused, so no review supersedes a finding the dialog never showed. Drafts are forgotten only once the engine took the review.
    - Findings and comments are each read 200 a page, oldest first; where either runs past one the tab says so above the diff.
    - An open finding with a suggestion offers **Apply suggestion** (`code_apply_suggestions`, against the head on screen); every finding and thread a reply; a thread **Resolve conversation**. **Request review** asks reviewers by handle with a note (`code_request_review`); **Close change** and **Reopen** move the change against the version on screen (`code_close_change`).
    - A standing finding offers **Resolve** in one press (an author's, held with why for others) and **Answer** (`code_resolve_finding`): Resolved, Won't fix or Disputed (an author's, which leave a blocker standing for whoever raised it), or Dismiss (its raiser's, a maintainer's or a person's) with a note; the form says a dismissal clears the finding for good; the engine says who may give which.
    - In the merge box, **Rebase** (`code_rebase_change`, from the head on screen) and **Take out of the queue** (`code_dequeue_change`, while queued) are confirmed in the page, saying a rebase moves the branch by one forced push and a change taken out loses its place and stays open. A merged change offers **Revert** instead (`code_revert_change`), confirmed with what it opens and a box to merge the revert once open; while a revert is open or merged (`reverted_by`) the box links that change in Revert's place; a closed one gives Revert back.
    - Every write is the act transport's, through `useAct` and a `WriteButton`, never optimistic: nothing moves until the engine answers, and the answer's position is the floor the page is read at next.
    - The page bar draws what the state leaves: live change, **Close change** and **Review** (menu of the three verdicts and Request review, each held with its reason) and a draft's **Ready for review**, all default buttons; closed, Reopen alone; merged, nothing (Revert is in the merge box). A change's author finds every verdict held ("You wrote this change, so your review would not count"), since the engine takes no review by an author (`own_change`). On a phone Close change folds into the bar's More.
  - **Revisions**: cards on the rail, newest first: who pushed and when, head with copy, facts its home recorded, the way to its head commit, files and what it changed since the one before.
  - **More**: where the change came from, who opened it and with which credential, turn and executor behind it, work item, authors, how it ended, as a properties card; under it, whom each record reached (`code_change_routing`), newest first: a card per record, each recipient by face with the one reason it heard, in the voice of somebody else's notice (`CODE_PHRASES`' `about`, held both ways to `gitlet.Reasons`; `short` is the reader's own, for a notice of theirs); where none is listed, whether nobody was told or the notices were swept with the turn detail they named.
- **Repositories** is `code_repos`, by last push (or name, `sort=name`), paged, narrowed by kind (`kind=`: All, Projects or Scratch, each with its count from `code_counts`) and state. A page is what the engine SCANNED, not kept, so one can be short or empty with a cursor; Load more until no cursor comes back, first page kept live and joined to the pages loaded ([A log is an axis, then its rows](#a-log-is-an-axis-then-its-rows)). The order is the engine's; no head re-sorts held pages.
  - A row: tile, name and marks, each outlined since none is a fault (state where not active, a seat's scratch repository, pull mirror, push mirror, a repository only its owner's seats read, as every person reads every repository; an active project carries none); description under; a line of owner, default branch, size, pushes, last push in words (Gitlet for a merge); at its end live changes, default branch's checks and pushes over the reader's last 14 days, each drawn only where the engine answered.
  - The footer counts the whole listing and its size across pages (`repos_total`); **New repository** and **Import a repository** are in the page bar. `status=`, `kind=`, `sort=` are the engine's own (`REPO_STATUSES`, `REPO_KINDS`, `REPO_SORTS`, each held to the engine's set). A row opens the repository's page. A declared repository's settings are the company document's `code.repos`; an empty listing offers the configuration to a reader who may open it.
  - **New repository** (`code_create_repo`) makes an empty project: name in the engine's grammar, owning unit from the chart, and, only where said, a description, default branch and which seats read it; otherwise the engine's defaults. Held for a credential bound to nobody; an applied create opens the new page. A scratch repository is a seat's own, never made here. A deleted repository is listed under the **Deleted** filter and restored on its own page.
  - **Import a repository** is a person's alone (`code_import_repo`, refused every seat by the authority table): a new project, named in the engine's grammar, owned by a unit from the chart, filled from an https URL at another host (with the token a variable NAMES, one `code.remote_credentials` declares for its host, typed as the name never the token, which the tool refuses) or made a pull mirror of it (**Keep following it**). Drawn for every reader, held with the sentence for one holding no human seat; the dialog's Import is held until the engine takes the form. The new repository reads `importing` until its home Gitlet node landed the source.
- **A repository's page**, `#/gitlet/repos/{name}`, is laid out as a code host lays one out.
  - Header: title is the owner's path off the chart, a slash and the name (the kit's `ObjectHeader`), outlined uncoloured marks (state where not active, Scratch, pull mirror, who reads it, Company or Unit, push mirror) and description. Tabs: **Code** (where it lands), **Changes**, **Commits**, **Branches**, **Pushes**, **Checks**, **Settings**, each with a glyph. Changes counts live changes (`code_counts`); Checks carries the default branch head's verdict (`code_commit_marks`): a dot when passed, a count when failed.
  - It is its row (`code_repo`, read at the tab's floor and every minute, the row alone; path owners and rules' merge gates are Settings' own ask, `path_owners=true` and `gates=true`, read as the tab opens) and its CONTENT, answered by its home Gitlet node: directory listing (`code_tree`, and `code_blob` for a path under the root, which answers a directory's listing where the path names one, so a path is one read), a file's lines (`code_blob`, paged, pages concatenating to the file's bytes), blame (`code_blame`), history (`code_log`), branches (`code_refs`).
  - The address is the place: the Code tab is never spelled, so a file's address is the repository's and its path. `ref=` is the revision (none is the default branch; a branch by name, a tag by its whole ref, which no same-named branch can shadow), `path=` the directory or file, `lens=blame`, `lines=` the lines picked. Pressing a line number picks it, Shift extends the run: selected tint with accent edge, as a coloured diff draws a pick; the run's first line holds its actions: copy the lines, copy a link to them at the commit, blame them. Code is coloured by kind ([Code is coloured by kind in Gitlet](#code-is-coloured-by-kind-in-gitlet)).
  - An address that picks `lines=` (a Gitlet › Search hit, a ⌘K hit, a Permalink) OPENS AT THE LINE: the path's one read asks from fifty lines before it (`code_blob`'s `start_line`), decided before anything is read, because every read streams the whole file from git and answers its line count, so a read from line 1 first would be a second stream nothing draws. A line inside the first page opens fifty lines above it too (at line 1 where nearer). The file pages forward from there, the line picked and scrolled to mid-screen; **Load earlier lines** reads back towards line 1 fifteen hundred lines a press, a page's worth (`start_line` and `end_line`, each step followed through its pages so it meets the lines after it; each step costs the Gitlet node one stream of the whole file).
  - The blame does the same through its own `start_line`, its first range the one holding the line, reading at most `gitlet.MaxBlameLines` (500) lines a range, forward and back, so **Load more lines** reaches the last line. A press picks a line on screen and reads nothing; a line the file lacks, which the engine refuses as a `start_line`, reads the file again from line 1 and says so beside its size.
  - The revision is picked from a panel of branches (by when moved, default first) and tags (newest first); a find asks the engine; the panel reads only while open. At the root the bar beside it counts branches and tags, each a link to its list on Branches. Under a path, the path back up to the root stands: repository name, then each directory, a link. **Go to file** (`t`) finds a file by the characters of its path in order, at the listing's commit (`code_find`), and opens it at the address's revision.
  - Opening a directory or file is a new place in the history; picking lines, revision and lens replace it. A read by a ref answers the commit the ref resolved to; the **Permalink** is the same place at that commit's whole id: an address that says the same tomorrow, which the engine answers immutably.
  - **Code** is the files at the revision. A directory is ONE CARD: the latest commit that touched it across its head (one commit of the path's history, `code_log` with `limit` 1, read at the commit the listing resolved, so bar and entries are one revision): writer's face (Gitlet's mark where Gitlet wrote the merge), subject linking the commit's page, check glyph, id with copy (the kit's `Copyable`, whole id), when, the path's **History**. Then the entries in a table whose head cells only a screen reader reads: glyph (folder, submodule's package, link, executable, prose or code, told apart by drawing never hue), name (kind said to a screen reader), the commit that last changed it and when (`code_tree_commits`, paged at the listing's commit); git's order until the whole directory is here, then directories first by name.
  - At the root, README and LICENSE follow as tabs of one card (`doc=license`), with Edit, read at the commit the listing resolved and rendered by the dashboard's own Markdown renderer (builds every element itself; fenced blocks coloured by info string).
  - The rail: **About** as sentences, **Open changes** (five, open then draft, each with its placing word), **Who pushes here**, **Pushes** over 14 days, **Mirror**, **Tags**. Who pushes here and the spark count the reader's days (`code_repo` with `day_bounds`); pushers count whole UTC days, which their label says; an older fleet's answer without them reads as not counted, never zero. The spark is one series in the first data colour, in a figure its caption names; a vendor's mark is drawn only beside the mirror's link.
  - Under a path the files take the page's width. A file is read beside the repository's tree: a pane of directories at the file's commit, read a directory at a time (`code_tree`) and opened down to the file, revision picker and Go to file at its head, its list scrolling alone. Over the file: crumbs (copied by a press, and **History**) and its latest commit with its check, a card of its own.
  - The file's card heads its lines with **Code** and **Blame** (`lens=blame`, each run headed by its commit, an empty line drawn empty, only a line too long to send by its size), lines and size (and a picked line it lacks), **Raw** and **Download** at that commit (linked once known, never probed), **Copy** of every page, **Edit**, the **Permalink**, **More** with **Delete file**; then its lines, tab four columns wide. A picture (png, jpeg, gif, webp, avif, bmp, ico, svg) replaces its lines, bytes read from the raw route and shown as their own type, up to 10 MiB; the README's pictures that are the repository's files are read the same way from the README's directory at its commit.
  - **Code**, at the root, opens the clone address the engine answers (`clone_url`, from `api.external_url`), its `git clone` command and **Download ZIP** of the commit on show. A deleted repository's Code, Commits and Tags read no content and offer no clone, push or Compare: each says it is read again once restored, and its own Delete brings the Deleted notice into view and focuses it. During an import the header's state mark says `importing`, its title how far it went.
  - **Changes** is Gitlet › Changes narrowed to the repository, in Gitlet's change row (`ChangeList`, `repo=`), the open ones until the bar picks another state (`state=`, every state among them, since the repository narrows the walk), with the way to Gitlet › Changes narrowed alike.
  - **Commits** is the history at a revision, of the path the address names or every path, a timeline of the reader's days each commit was authored: a heading per run of one day, so git's order is never re-sorted. Each commit: subject, author's face, name and when, how it reached its branch (a run for its work item, pushed with git, or who pushed it) where the answering node's index holds the push, id with copy, a way to browse its files, its checks for the branch read, the change it merged or landed with, its tags; a Gitlet-written merge commit carries Gitlet's mark. Load older commits pages on. Narrows by who pushed, from when committed, and words in the message.
  - **Pushes** is the push history, as Gitlet › Pushes draws it.
  - **Branches** is tables in views (Overview: default branch, active ones, newest tags; Active, Stale, All by when moved; Tags by date with the newest Latest), each branch with who moved it and when (Gitlet for a merge or queue landing), checks, behind and ahead of the default branch, its change, with Find a branch. Writes:
    - **New branch** (`code_create_branch`: name and start, default branch when empty).
    - **Protect** on each row opens the protection form on that branch's ref (a branch a rule already names is tagged protected and leads to its rule on Settings, where the form opens on the rule and gate as they stand).
    - **Delete** (`code_delete_branch`), confirmed in the page and sent with the row's head as `expected_head`, so a branch pushed to since is refused rather than deleted unseen; the confirmation says its commits stay in history and a change proposing it loses its source; the toast's **Undo** makes it again at that head. The default branch's row has no Delete: the engine refuses it whoever asks (`default_branch`); make another branch the default on Settings first. Delete is held with the engine's own sentence where rules refuse it.
    - Tags are listed newest first by their own date, each opening its code at its whole ref, with **New tag** (`code_create_tag`: name, target, default branch when empty, a message that makes it annotated) and each tag's **Delete** (`code_delete_tag`), confirmed and sent with the row's value as `expected_target`; the confirmation reads the tag in detail and holds its delete with the engine's own sentence where a protection rule keeps it.
    - New branch or tag takes write, delete maintain, held as such. A repository that is archived, deleted, importing or a pull mirror takes none, each held with that sentence; New branch is held only for a repository holding no branch at all, and one whose default branch holds nothing names where it starts.
