  - **Code** commits from the browser (`code_commit_files`) on the branch the page's read resolved (never the address's spelling, which may name a branch bare, a tag, or nothing for the default), at the commit it stood at (`expected_head`), from the file's card and the directory's bar: **Edit** opens the file (every page read at that commit, joined) in an editor with the commit message (text file of at most 256 KiB; a larger or binary one is held, saying to commit from a clone); **Delete file** confirms with its message; a directory's **New file** takes a path and text. Each is one commit of one file; at a tag or commit they are held, saying to choose a branch.
  - An empty repository's Code tab is one card saying nobody has pushed a branch yet, offering **Add a file** (its first commit, a root commit that makes the default branch, sent with no `expected_head` since nothing was read, so a repository made with New repository is filled without a clone), its clone address with copy, and the two commands that push an existing repository into it. A repository whose default branch holds nothing while other branches are live is not empty: Code and Commits draw the revision picker that reaches them and say the default branch holds no commit and another can be made the default on Settings.
  - **Settings** is a card per section, each titled with what it governs and a line saying so. It shows the repository's settings, protection rules with their merge gates (every field a merge is held to, in one line, `lib/protection.ts`'s `gateLine`: who merges; approvals and the change classes needing none; paths a person approves and the classes exempting each; checks; how a gate requiring a check lands a change through its queue, each change tested merged on the branch before landing, so many candidates at once, so many changes each; whether a change to the checks themselves needs a person; whether path owners approve) and path owners. Its writes each go through `useAct` and a WriteButton, never optimistic (the page is redrawn from the read the write's position brings), each drawn for every reader and held with the sentence saying why:
    - **Edit details**, on the Repository card (`code_update_repo`'s `description`, `default_branch`, `owner`, `visibility`, one call carrying only what moved, the default branch chosen from the branches the repository holds, which is how a repository whose default branch holds nothing is put right).
    - **Rename**, beside it (`rename_to` alone, a record of its own: a project's new name is one label and a scratch repository keeps its seat's `<handle>.`; the old name leads to it for a while; the page moves to the new name once applied).
    - **Path owners**: **Add a path owner** gives a unit or seat of the chart globs over the tree; each owner's **Edit** and **Remove** change or take them (`code_update_repo`'s `path_owners`, globs given and taken by name, never the list whole, so a glob another request gave meanwhile is kept; Remove takes every glob the page read, after a confirmation; a scratch repository takes none; taking a glob while a rule makes path owners approve is a person's).
    - **Search mode** (`code_update_repo`'s `search`, a button per mode of `REPO_SEARCH_MODES`, held to `gitlet.SearchModes`: the current mode is no change; a scratch repository is never indexed).
    - **Mirrors**, a person's alone (`code_update_repo`'s `mirror_from` and `mirror_to`, each set whole from a dialog or removed: an https URL, the credential as a variable's name, a push mirror's seat and refs; refused every seat by the deciding data node).
    - **Unreachable history**: **Purge unreachable history** (`code_purge_unreachable`, a person's alone, on a repository they maintain) opens a confirmation that names, BEFORE the press, who keeps copies of what it drops: every Gitlet node's copy until it syncs past the purge, every earlier backup, the object store for a day (a versioned S3 bucket as long as its own rules keep a deleted object), and every clone and fetch that already took it (a person's, a coding box's, a CI runner's checkout), which nothing on the server reaches, the repository's push mirror by URL among them where it has one, since that host already holds whatever was pushed to it ([Expunge](../concepts/gitlet.md#expunge), "What still holds a purged object"). Only its Purge asks the repository's maintainer; the section says where the last purge stands.
    - **Archive**: **Archive repository** (`archived: true` alone, after a confirmation saying it turns read-only: still cloned, fetched and read, no push) and **Unarchive repository** (`archived: false`) are each a record of their own; a pull mirror is held from an archive, since an archived repository takes no sync.
    - A declared repository's details, name, archive, path owners, search mode and mirrors are the company document's, settled by every activation: held with that sentence, the tab leading to Settings › Configuration. Its purge, which changes no setting, is offered.
    - **Protection rules** are written on a repository the document does not declare (`code_protect_branch`): **Protect a branch** adds a rule for a branch name or pattern (`refs/heads/<glob>`, `refs/tags/<glob>`); each rule's **Edit** changes who pushes directly, whether a push may force or delete, and, behind **Gate merges into it**, every gate field: who merges; approvals and the change classes (`CODE_PATH_CLASSES`, held to `gitlet.PathClasses`) merging without one; paths a person approves and classes exempting each; required checks; once a check is required, whether a seat may approve a change to the checks themselves (`agents_edit_checks`) and the queue's depth and batch (bounded by `CODE_MAX_QUEUE_DEPTH` and `CODE_MAX_QUEUE_BATCH`, a new gate starting at the engine's defaults); whether path owners approve; what becomes of a merged seat's branch. The form sends only fields the person moved, every list item by item (checks and exempting classes by `add` and `remove`, human paths by glob with `put` and `remove`) and the landing a field at a time, so nothing else of the rule is restated and an item somebody else added meanwhile is kept; turning the gate off sends `remove_gate`. **Remove** is confirmed in the page, saying what the refs lose.
    - **Delete repository** (`code_delete_repo`) opens a dialog saying what stops and that it is restorable until its purge, takes an optional reason, and is held until the repository's name is typed. A deleted repository's page says so above its tabs, with when, and offers **Restore repository** (`code_restore_repo`); its Settings cards show what it holds and draw none of the writes above, since it takes no change but its restore. A declared repository's rules, delete and restore are the company document's, held with that sentence.
  - Content is not polled: a reader reads the revision they opened. A commit of its history or a blame opens the commit's page; a branch offers a comparison with the default branch.
- **A commit's page**, `#/gitlet/repos/{name}/commits/{sha}`, names its commit by its WHOLE id, the one spelling no push can move; an abbreviation is no page, as `code_commit` takes none. Laid out as a code host's: subject; who wrote it and when (author's face, where the chart holds a seat of that name), when git says it was committed where that differs, repository, parents, whole id with copy; a **provenance** card in sentences: how it was pushed (who, run and work item, how, to which branches) and how it landed (the change, merge commit, who merged it through its gate: approvals and checks, the train's for a queue landing), each with time in words; then every file it changed as one stack beside the files' tree, as a change's Files changed draws it.
  - It is the commit as the history lists it beside what the ROWS say (`code_commit`): the push that introduced it (by the answering Gitlet node's index of pushes and that push's row: who, when, how, and the turn, executor and work item behind a seat's push, as the engine recorded them, which a commit's author line is not) or, where the index names none, why; and the changes it belongs to (those it merged and those whose revision it heads), each linking its page.
  - What it changed is read against its first parent, as git shows a commit (a merge's change is what it brought into the branch it was made on; a root commit's is every file it holds, from git's empty tree), by both whole ids, so every page is immutable: files paged and the walk of every patch (`code_diff patches=true`), toolbar totals, **Filter files** narrowing tree and stack (`q=`). The file `file=` names opens the stack at it, pages read on until they list it, and `line=` is marked and revealed in its section. A change's revisions link their heads here.
  - Page bar: **Browse files** opens the tree at this commit; **Revert** and **Cherry-pick** (`code_revert`, `code_cherry_pick`) each make one new commit on a branch chosen from the repository's branches, with the head that listing showed as `expected_head` and git's own message unless one is typed; the dialog says nothing is rewritten and a conflict commits nothing; both held as a commit to a branch is. **Tag** tags this commit (`code_create_tag`), held as a new tag is.
- **A comparison**, `#/gitlet/repos/{name}/compare`, compares `head=` with `base=` (none is the default branch), each named as a revision on the repository's page; with no head it asks for one.
  - `code_compare` resolves both in one read and answers how the commits relate (merge base, which contains which, how many commits each has that the other lacks) and the merge preview, asked of the repository's home Gitlet node by the two whole ids the comparison answered, the one merge a change's mergeability is recorded by (where one commit contains the other it is clean, answered with nothing asked of the home): **Merges cleanly**, or **Conflicts** with the paths, or that the home could not decide it in a read's time. The merge preview is the one state the page wears a tone for.
  - What head changed is read from the merge base to head (the three-dot reading), both whole, and drawn as a commit's is: one stack beside the files' tree.
  - **Open change** is one `code_open_change` of the compared branch into the base branch, prefilled with the subject of head's commit and the work item the push that brought it was charged to (`<tracker>:<key>`, as the engine stamped it), each the reader's to change or clear, with reviewers and a draft. Drawn for every reader, held with the reason where head is not a branch, base is not one, the two are one branch, head has no commit base lacks, a live change already proposes head's commit (which it then links), or that commit is still being read. Nothing moves until the engine answers; an applied open leads to the change it opened.
- **Search**, `#/gitlet/search`, is the lines of the repositories the reader reads that match a search (`code_search`): `q=` in Gitlet's one grammar ([Finding code](../guides/gitlet.md#finding-code)), its `repo:`, `path:` and `ref:` filters first, and the bar's `mode=` (`CODE_SEARCH_MODES`, held to `codeindex.Modes`), `repo=`, `path=`, `ref=` beside it: the same filters as controls, every one in the address, so a search is a link.
  - It is asked when the reader presses Search, never as they type: a company-wide search is a request to every Gitlet node. A press is a step Back takes, phrase, path and ref pushed onto the history (mode and repository narrow on screen and replace), and the boxes follow the address whenever it moves, so they never show one search over another's lines. A reconnect asks again only a search that never reached the engine, as ⌘K's Code tab does: a rolling restart reconnects every socket, and each open search re-asked would be one more request to every Gitlet node for an answer that already names its commits. It takes no floor: it answers at the commit each repository was searched at (`tips`).
  - Lines are grouped by repository then file in the engine's order (repository, path, line), never re-sorted. Each file is a card of its matching lines with three lines of context each, near lines joined and a gap between apart ones that reveals hidden lines from the file's blob by its id; each match is marked in the code-match colour where the engine says it matched. A file's head says how many lines matched; past the three drawn, **Show N more matching lines** asks a search of that one file.
  - Each hit's number opens its file on the repository's Code tab AT THAT COMMIT, by whole id, with the line picked (`ref=`, `path=`, `lines=`), so the link says tomorrow what the search said today; a non-UTF-8 path is drawn with no link, since no address names it.
  - Beside the cards, facets count matching lines by repository and directory and narrow the search on the engine; they say Partial where the answer was cut or a file's total was not answered. Above them one line says what was found and on what, and every gap the engine names: quietly for what the search's own terms left out (a grep repository is named with `repo:` to search it), in the warning tone where lines may be missing.
  - ⌘K's **Code** scope asks the same question (see [⌘K: search, answer, act](#k-search-answer-act)).
- **Queue** is the merge queues, `code_queue` with `trains`: a box per repository's target branch, its train base and entries in queue order on a spine, each with its change's title, who enqueued it and its train's required checks as a `SegmentedMeter` with an elapsed bar against the slowest timeout; every repository's trains and ejections, not only a named one's.
  - Each box names its gate's required checks (the branch's matched rules and the repository's gates) and a More menu of what is served: its protection and gate in Settings, its commits, a link to copy. Above the boxes: changes queued and taken out in the last day.
  - **Load more** follows `next` through the pager every code listing shares; each live entry's **Take out** is the change page's (`code_dequeue_change`), confirmed in the page.
  - A change taken out lately is a danger callout with why in words, **View the run** of the check that failed on the train, and **Re-queue**, which adds it again as it was to land.
- **Checks** is where every check stands, `code_checks` with `standing`: each check's latest run on a live change's head, a queue's candidate or a protected branch's tip, running ones included, over 24 hours, 7 days or 30 days, failing first or newest first. The engine counts each state for the tabs and narrows by state, check and repository.
  - A run opens in the check pane beside the list (`run=`): tests counted, facts, **Re-run** of that one run (`code_rerun_checks` by its commit and branch), failures and the end of its output numbered with failing lines tinted.
  - The pane and its log are one component every checks listing shares (`routes/gitlet/checks`): this section, a repository's Checks tab and a change's (`change=`). The log is read by its object, an immutable answer, paged, never until the reader asks.
- **Pushes** is one repository's history, `code_pushes` in brief, a feed on the reader's days: each push one sentence (who, what it did to which refs, the change a merge landed, what a refused push offered), its run, credential and how it was built, refs below. Each day's heading counts its pushes from the engine's day counts (`day_bounds`), "Yesterday 2 of 13" where the page holds part of it.
  - Narrowed to one repository by `repo=`; a name no repository can have (`REPO_NAME`, held to `gitlet.ValidName`) is said in place rather than asked about.
  - A row draws five refs at most, refusals first, the rest counted in one line; **Show all** reads that one push whole at its own position, and the clock re-renders no ref.
  - It is a log, so Load older pushes fetches older rows ([A log is an axis, then its rows](#a-log-is-an-axis-then-its-rows)).
  - It narrows on the engine by who pushed (`by=`) and when (`when=`); a narrowed page that read short says how far back it looked.
  - Its rail draws pushes by day, who pushes here and the repository's protection in the settings' words; its toolbar says how many pushes the repository has had.
**Code is read over REST, never on the socket** (`lib/useCodeQuery.ts`). Its questions are the registry's like every other, one answer on every transport, but the engine answers a socket's questions four at a time and queues the rest (`MaxInFlightQueries` in `internal/api/stream`), the frame's own reads among them, and a code answer is a page, tree, file or diff. So a code question uses the registry's REST form, `GET /query/{what}`, through the one loader (`useRest`): an answer belongs to its key, a refusal replaces what is on screen, the engine's `Retry-After` is the retry. It keeps `useQuery`'s floor: a write this tab makes to the code log raises it (`SESSION_QUERIES.code`), every ask names it, and the write asks again.
- An answer read by object id is immutable (strong `ETag`, `Cache-Control: immutable`) and the TAB keeps the 64 most recently read (`IMMUTABLE_KEPT`), 56 KiB a page at most, so the same question from any screen or pager is answered with no request. The transport asks with `no-store`, so the browser cache answers none.
- An answer the tab dropped while a screen holds it is asked again naming its tag; a `304` is the answer the screen holds.
- The engine's reader gates read a code question where it is asked, as every other. Use `useCodeQuery("…")`, and `codeRest.query("…")` for an older page.

**A window the clock moves is one code question.** Checks' last 24 hours (hour-aligned) and the reader's days that Pushes, Repositories, the repository rail, Commits and Branches read move with the clock; keyed on instants, each move would be a new question and the list would flash its placeholder. A question names its window instead (`CodeWindow`: `7d`, a Branches view); the edges (`since`, `day_bounds`) are sent at every ask and never keyed, so rows stay and the moved window is read within one cadence: the next poll, or on a screen that does not poll a quiet ask at a random moment within a minute (`WINDOW_SPREAD_MS`), since every tab's window moves at once. An answer carries its edges and a pager moves all pages to new edges in one step, so a day's count is drawn under the day it counted. An edge is a `ClockEdge` (`lib/range.ts`), which a code question's parameters refuse by type; a module asking one formats no instant itself (`app/source.test.ts`).

**Changes are listed outside Gitlet in Gitlet's own row.** My work's Reviews, a seat's Code section and a task's Changes tab each mount one fixed listing (`routes/gitlet/ChangeList.tsx`) drawn by `ChangeRows`, the row Gitlet › Changes draws, with its cards, paged the same way, re-read every minute while only the first page is loaded. Home's code card draws its two halves with `ChangeRows`, compact, three each over its own two reads, unpaged. A change shows the same reference, state, branches, readiness, owner and blockers everywhere. A seat's reviews are the one listing of reviews (`code_reviews?reviewer=`), rows naming the change each judged.

**Settings › Gitlet is Gitlet as an administrator runs it** (`#/settings/gitlet`, Admin's, beside the Engine group, hidden where the company hosts no code). It asks no question of its own:
- The code log's retention row, drawn by Backups & retention's own row so the pages cannot disagree.
- Gitlet's alarms on every node, from the fleet's node rows (each node's table at its last beat, kinds `CODE_ALARM_KINDS`, held to the engine's alarm table both ways by `internal/gitlet`'s gate). A node that evaluated no table yet is named apart, not counted quiet.
- The scratch policy as the engine's rows (`limits`, group `code`: `code.scratch.idle_days` and `max_per_seat`), each beside the engine's default with the Settings › Limits pencil to change it in place; and `code.identity_domain` (`settings`, group `code`), beside its default, changed in place by its text field (`TextSetting`).
- The protected repositories (`code_repos` asked with `protected`, walked by an index of those alone), paged with Load more, never every repository filtered here. Each is a fold whose rules' gates are read once from the detail (`code_repo` with `gates=true`) when first opened and kept while the page is; who last changed each rule and when comes from the same answer (`rule_sources`), a caption under the rule (`ruleSourceLine`, shared with the repository's Settings tab).

## Chatlet: a top bar, a Rooms panel, a room, and where you have read to

The company's own chat (`chat.backend: chatlet`), read AS A SEAT: the engine answers every chat question for the seat the principal holds, so the workspace is guarded whole and a principal acting as no seat is told so and how to give it one (see [The sidebar](#the-sidebar)). Where chat is a vendor's or none there is no Chatlet: its row is hidden and its addresses say where the company talks, as for every service the company does not run (see [The sidebar](#the-sidebar)).

Chatlet runs edge to edge under the page bar (the shell's flush fill). Every place is an address: a room by id, or a view beside the rooms, with at most ONE pane named by `pane=` (see the address table above), so Back closes a pane, a reload keeps it and a thread is a link from anywhere (`routes/chatlet/nav.tsx`). A toast stands at the window's foot on its end side and clears what Chatlet docks there (`app/toastInset.tsx`): above the room's foot and a reply box however tall (`useToastClearOf`), beside an open pane, never over it (`useToastBeside`).

- **The top bar** holds, on one line and at one height:
  - **Menu**: slides the Rooms panel in from the start edge (or hides it while pinned); its badge is the sidebar's figure of what waits on you.
  - **Rooms** switcher: named after the open room (the frame's one reading, so a team's room read from outside the team and an archived room are named though not in the list), listing your rooms (Starred, Rooms, Team rooms) with Browse rooms and New room at its foot.
  - **Messages** switcher: named after the open conversation or Direct messages, listing your conversations then the people and agents to start one with, New message at its foot.
  - The open room's actions: members (three faces and the count, opening the details' Members), Search this room, the notification choice (Every message, Mentions, the default, or Muted), and **More**: **Catch up with Ask Crewlet** (or **Summarize**, with nothing unread), details, what was shared, Add people, description and topic, the star, Mark as read, Copy link, **Archive room** (or **Reopen room** on an archived one; both asked in a dialog saying what it does for everybody) and Leave.
  - Each action is offered only where the engine would take it, by the room's one reading of its rules; Archive is the creator's, the team lead's or an admin's, held with that sentence for anybody else (`routes/chatlet/roomLifecycle.ts`).
  - Ask Crewlet is the page bar's button, so this bar has none. The star is More's, so on a room the page bar draws none (`useOwnStar`): one star, and on a phone one "…".
  - On a view beside the rooms (Activity, Threads, Drafts and sent, Saved, New message, Search, Browse rooms) the bar also carries the view's tools (Activity's Unread filter, Browse rooms' New room) before Search, so no view draws a row of its own (`routes/chatlet/ViewHead.tsx`).
  - The bar draws no title: the trail's last crumb names the view and is the page's one `h1`. Focus of a removed control or a move drop (the last card's Unfollow or Remove, a tool left behind) lands on that heading, a reading position with no ring, never the page body.
  - While the panel is pinned it lists what the switchers do, so they are not drawn. A narrow bar drops Menu's word; under 480px search and the notification choice move into More and a view's tools drop their words (the switch's track, New room's glyph), each still named and hinted.
- **The Rooms panel is the row's renderer** (`panel`, `app/nav.ts`):
  - A find row (the filter, a menu for unread only and the order, and the pin), the views (Activity with the accent badge of what waits there; Threads; Drafts and sent; Saved), then four collapsible sections (Starred, Channels, Team rooms, Direct messages) of dense rows.
  - Unread room: primary ink, medium weight. Muted: dimmed, with a bell. With a draft: a pencil. Each has the accent badge of what waits on you in it (a conversation: every unread message; elsewhere: unread messages naming you or the whole room). A collapsed section still shows the open room and the unread ones.
  - Counts are the ENGINE'S. When the cursors could not be read the badges are absent and the panel says so, because a zero would claim the reader is caught up; a list past its bound says so too. Browse rooms and New message stand at its foot.
  - Pinned (per-browser) it is a column beside the conversation; under 760px of chat area never pinned. Pinning eases the column open and shut with the kit's motion at its own width, so the conversation resizes beside it; under reduced motion it simply appears and goes.
- **Panes** stand beside the conversation, never over part of it: a pinned Rooms panel gives way while a pane is open on a chat area under 908px, and a pane covers a chat area under 760px whole. Widths are `app/layout.ts`'s, keeping the transcript to its floor.
- **Keys** (the legend's "In Chatlet"): `Alt+Up` and `Alt+Down` move between rooms, with `Shift` between rooms with unread; `Mod+F` searches the open room; `Escape` marks the open room read when nothing else is listening (a pane, the slid-in panel, a peek, a menu); `Mod+/` lists Chatlet's keys.
- **A room** (`#/chatlet/{id}`) is the transcript, paged back on request, who is looking at it, typing in it or working on a reply, and the composer (`Mod+Enter` sends; `Enter` is a new line).
  - **A room's name carries one `#`**: beside the room's glyph (intro, row, card) the glyph is the sigil and the name bare; in words that stand alone (toast, composer placeholder, search result) a channel reads `#name`, a team's room its team's name, a conversation the people in it (`rooms.ts`' `roomWhere`).
  - A message's links are drawn under it, in room and thread alike, whoever wrote it, as rendered prose draws an address in an agent's words (`links: "checked"`, [above](#what-prose-names-is-drawn-as-what-it-is)): an address on a host the company configured opens as the dashboard rebuilds it, in a new tab (GitHub or GitLab only under an owner that host's row names); any other, the company's own dashboard included, is drawn whole and inert with its host; one whose scheme the allowlist refuses is its words.
  - Ask Crewlet reads every box open on the room as one draft (the message, an open thread's reply, each message open for rewrite) and proposes text into any of them; Send, Reply and Save stay the person's.
  - A room that takes no messages from you (archived, a private room you are outside, a kind this build cannot classify) closes the box and says why in it. A browser that cannot send (offline, a reader the engine posts nothing for) leaves the box open and holds Send, the sentence beside it, as every composer does. Membership, notification and settings gestures are the top bar's.
  - Each change to a message (Edit, Delete, a reaction) is held by its own tool, because the engine serves each on its own, by that tool's rule not the composer's: an archive closes a room to new messages and nothing else, a delete reaches past membership; each is drawn and held with its sentence where the engine would refuse, never hidden. A room whose read failed says so on every control rather than reading for ever.
  - A public room or a unit's room is readable by every seat, joined or not, so arriving from a search outside a room whose whole transcript is on screen is ordinary. A public room's header then offers to join; a unit's room offers neither Join nor Leave, since membership is the org chart's (a seat is in it by being in the unit), and says so.
  - A message is not drawn until the engine has it: what you sent waits beneath the transcript until a read carries it, with **Send again** where nobody can say whether it landed (same operation key, because the engine derives the id from it and a fresh key would say it twice), **Try again** where the node refused it, and **Take it off the screen**, which unsays nothing.
  - A message the node accepted but has not applied (`pending`) is undecided (the room may have been archived, or its author removed, just ahead of it), so the screen asks again under the same key: first after two seconds, the applier's allowance (`contract/chat.ts`'s `PENDING_REASK_MS`, the engine's `chatlet.DecisionWait`), then at doubling intervals up to thirty seconds, until it landed (the transcript brings it) or was refused (the row says why). It waits there while you view another room.
  - **Whom a message reached is a mark, never a sentence** (the kit's `DeliveryReceipt`), at the end of a person's message's last line after any "(edited)": a dashed circle while nobody it reached has answered, a check once somebody has (with the count while others are to answer), the warning where it named an agent and reached none. It takes the next line only when the last has no room or the message ends in a list, quote or code block. Hover, focus or press opens a tooltip (where it stands, who answered and when, who it waits on, when sent); the whole sentence is its accessible name. The composer's line draws whom a draft will reach as faces, the same way.
- **The panes** draw in the kit's side panel: opening moves focus to its heading, Escape inside closes it, closing returns focus to what opened it (a menu's trigger, when a menu item opened it and is gone).
  - **A thread** (`pane=thread:{room}:{root}`), beside the conversation or over it: root, reply count, replies as the room draws them, an agent writing a reply, the reply box where the room takes one, who a reply reaches (faces, as the composer's receipt), Follow. One level deep (a reply offers no thread), paged forwards from its root; its read place moves to the newest reply on screen.
  - **Details** (`pane=details:{room}:{tab}`) groups the room's facts in cards: name (never changes); topic and description, each with Edit where the engine would take it; team, who made it and when, retention (Edit for an admin), whether and since when archived, Leave where a person may; under them Archive room or Reopen room, and for an admin **Delete older messages**. Its Members: find, Add people where the engine adds anybody (suggestions grow to the room the dialog has; on a phone's sheet to its foot), people before agents, each opening their profile. **Shared**: every link said in it, newest first, as the room unfurls it, each opening its message. **Notifications**.
  - **A profile** (`pane=profile:{handle}`): the seat's face, team, what it is doing now, Message, its org chart page, and the rooms you share (`chat_channels{with}`).
  - **Catch up** (`pane=catchup:{room}`, or `summarize` with nothing unread) is Ask Crewlet's brief: the gist, what waits on you, what was said, each point opening its message. It reads only what you can read, posts nothing, and goes on in Ask Crewlet.
- **Activity** (`#/chatlet/activity`) is where Chatlet opens: its sidebar row leads here and the bare `#/chatlet` is replaced with it. It lists every message naming your seat in every room, every reply in a followed thread and every reaction to what you said (`chat_activity`): the whole away story, since the engine sends no email, push or SMS. Filters: mentions, replies, reactions, and unread alone. The chosen row is read beside the list as the room draws it (`chat_message`: the message, and for a reply its root and the replies just before) with a reply box under it; choosing an unread row marks it read through its room's cursor. A narrow column draws no reading pane, so a row opens where it was said. Each row is dated by when it happened.
- **Threads** (`#/chatlet/threads`): followed threads, newest reply first (`chat_threads`), each its root and newest replies with Unfollow and Reply. **Drafts and sent** (`#/chatlet/drafts`): the Drafts tab lists what you have not sent (a message the engine did not confirm, and words left in a box, kept in the tab, never in the address or browser storage); the Sent tab lists what you sent (`chat_sent`). **Saved** (`#/chatlet/saved`): what you saved, newest first (`chat_saved`). A card quotes its message read-only; its actions are a press away in the thread or room.
- **New message** (`#/chatlet/new`, `to=`) takes people and agents as chips in To (`#` there finds one of your rooms), shows the conversation you already share with them, and opens one only when you send.
- **Browse rooms** (`#/chatlet/browse`) lists every room you can read, joined or not, archived ones under their own filter (`chat_rooms`), with topic, size and last message, sorted by activity, name or size; Join where the engine would take one, Open elsewhere. A team's room says in its Topic cell what it is (its members are the org chart's). On a phone each room is a card naming every fact beside its value, since a bare count or dash says nothing without its column.
- **Search chat** (`#/chatlet/search`, `q=` and `in=`) ranks what was said in every room your seat may READ (wider than your rooms) by keyword alone: chat is not in the vector corpus ([ADR-0071](../../adr/0071-chat-is-a-keyword-corpus-and-takes-no-vectors.md)).
  - It searches as you type once the words rest (`lib/useQuiet.ts`), keeping the settled words in the address by replacement.
  - In and From narrow at the engine (`channel_id`, `author`); Who (people or agents) narrows the page the engine ranked, and says so. In, From and Who are the Messages tab's; before a word is typed each tab says how it searches.
  - A phrase past the engine's bound is not sent, and the screen says why.
  - It asks for the engine's page (forty hits, `contract/chat.ts`'s `CHAT_SEARCH_PAGE`, the engine's `search.MaxChatSearchLimit`) with no next page, so a full page says there may be more matches and how to narrow, not that it is everything.
  - The People tab matches the org chart's seats, the Rooms tab every room you can read, on the words each row draws.
  - Wherever a list offers seats to pick or open (Add people, New message, People) the line under an agent is what it is doing, else its state ("Idle", "Paused"); under a person, their team.
- **On Home**, Chatlet offers two widgets (`routes/chatlet/home.widgets.tsx`; see [Home is the reader's board](#home-is-the-readers-board)), each asking what its page asks and re-reading on its page's frames. Neither marks anything read.
  - **Unread rooms**: the rail's rooms with something unread and the engine's count on each. A muted room is left out and counted; a rail cut at the engine's bound is said to count only the most recently active rooms; a room a newer engine made is counted as left out; a rail that met a record this build cannot read is said incomplete; where cursors could not be read a sentence says so. None is ever drawn as "caught up".
  - **Mentions**: Activity's newest mentions; a mention in a thread opens the thread.
  - The rooms are the frame's one reading, the one the sidebar badge and the Rooms panel draw.
  - They are the Chatlet app's: a credential acting as no seat is told so in a line and asked nothing; a company whose chat is a vendor's or none is offered neither.
- **Live, by evidence.** A chat frame carries no body: it says a room moved, and the screen re-reads, a burst coalesced into one read. What a reader has paged to is re-read only where a frame names something on it:
  - Room: the newest page on every frame in it; then, once that page has caught up with the frame on the log, the page ending at an edited, deleted or reacted-to message it does not reach, or every page below it for an erase or prune.
  - Thread: the first page for its root, the page holding a changed reply, the last page for a new reply.
  - Mentions: the newest page on every frame, and a page below it for a change to a mention on it, an erase or prune in a room it holds a mention from, or a membership change.
  - A page read again is put back only once it still meets the next page: a room joined makes mentions said in it visible, so a page can return holding the same number over a shorter range, and the range it no longer reaches is read in before anything moves, not drawn as a hole.
  - A tab that let a frame go unseen (a bound, or a frame naming no room, which is the engine saying it dropped some) re-reads everything it holds, since what it missed is unknown.
  - Presence is pushed whole for the rooms the tab says are open.
  - Your read state reaches every tab of yours as `chat_cursor_moved`, the writer included (which also has the write's own answer); the rail asks again once when its revision moves, whichever lands first.
- **Where you have read to** is written as you read: every `READ_FLUSH_MS` (15 s), at once on leaving a room, hiding or closing the tab, through `mark_chat_read`, the same audited act as every change. A badge clears when a flush lands, not on the scroll. A message counts as read only once on screen while the room is in view: tab in front, nothing over the page. Ask Crewlet as the whole window or over the page's end edge covers the room, as do a dialog or the palette; Ask Crewlet's column only narrows the page. What arrived while covered counts once in view again.
- **A seat that moves is a new screen.** A write goes out as the seat the engine resolves on arrival, so the whole screen is mounted under the seat the viewer names and redrawn when the directory binds the person elsewhere: the last seat's unsent messages with their Retry, a draft, an open thread and a half-filled dialog go with it, and what it had read but not written is not written as the next seat (a cursor only moves forward, so it would mark rooms read for good). A different person signing in hands the tab over by a reload with storage emptied, as for every screen.
- **Offline**, chat is like every socket screen: it keeps what it last read, the frame's banner says the live channel is down, and it re-reads on reconnect. Nothing more is said; a message is never queued.
- **On a narrow screen**, a phone's or one narrowed by Ask Crewlet's column, the rail stacks above the room, each taking its share. The screen still takes the window's height, since a transcript inside a scrolling page is two scrollers under one wheel. Widths are in [The frame](#the-frame).

## Doclet: the spaces, a landing, and search with real modes

Doclet is the approved **Home** layout. No navigation column stands beside the screen (the section renderer is `none`, `app/nav.ts`): the spaces are ONE ROW at the top of every Doclet screen, the search sits in the page bar of the landing, a space and the results, and a page is read at the sheet's full width. A page's bar and the composer's hold that page's own actions and no search: the trail is the one thing on a bar that gives way, and a search field with its ranking menu cut ancestors to stubs at 1440 and took a phone's bar to three rows. There `/` opens the palette, which searches pages too. The landing, a space and the search answer take the sheet's whole width with no cap of their own (`styles/frame.test.ts` refuses a screen capping itself at the kit's content maximum). Agent skills and Agent diaries are reached from the landing, the palette and the trail.

- **The spaces row** (`SpacesRow`) is a navigation landmark named Spaces: a link per space with the folder every space wears and its key (`KeyChip`), drawn with the design system's chip tabs. The space being read is `aria-current="page"`; a space's page count and purpose are its title.
- **The search** is a field and, BESIDE it, the ranking mode in a menu: Hybrid, Keyword or Meaning, sent as `mode=hybrid|keyword|semantic` (the word for `semantic` is the reader's, never sent). The menu is beside the field, not inside, because a control inside a text box is one a pointer reaches by missing the box. Enter goes to the results with phrase and mode in the address, so a search is a place to return to.
  - The menu learns what the backend serves from the `knowledge` PROBE, the question asked with no phrase, which runs nothing and answers `modes` and, asked for `semantic`, the reason the others would degrade (`no_embeddings`, `unsupported`).
  - A mode the answer does not list is **disabled with that reason as the item's second line**. Before the probe answers nothing is disabled: "not known yet" is never a reason to take a mode away.
  - **The default is a mode the engine serves**: Hybrid where served as asked, else the first mode the probe lists (Keyword with no embeddings provider). An address naming no `mode=` runs in that default: the results wait for the probe rather than running Hybrid first and reporting "asked for Hybrid, served Keyword" about a choice nobody made. A mode named in the address is the reader's and kept; the answer says what served it.
- **The landing** (no phrase) is TILES SIZED BY WHAT EACH IS WORTH, on one screen (the approved Bento layout).
  - The newest save, comment, rename or new page across the company takes the big tile, answering WHAT CHANGED AND WHETHER IT MATTERS, in order: the page's space by name and its title (the one way into the page); the save's note (or comment's words); who, when and how much, in words ("9 words added, 8 removed, in 3 places"; a new page's length); then the change itself, READ AS THE PAGE READS (`lib/proseDiff.ts`, drawn by `components/ProseDiff.tsx` with the design system's `DocumentDiff`).
  - Versions are compared by block (a list item and a table row each a block); a removed and an added block of the same shape sharing most words are one block edited: only changed words are marked, in place, with a link read as its label and compared whole, so no markdown, link target or id reaches the reader and no paragraph is drawn twice. The heading a change sits under is kept; unchanged blocks are counted where they stand.
  - A change of at most three blocks and sixty words is shown open; a longer one is folded behind **Show the change**, and past eight changed blocks it counts the rest and links the whole save in the page's History. A save too large to compare says so and links it. A new page shows its opening once, and no note repeats it.
  - Under the change, the page's **Earlier saves** (**Recent saves** under a comment or rename), three at most, each as above: note, who, when, how much, its change one press away. Cost: ONE `page` read, of the featured page alone, and a `page_revision` per version compared. A change to a purged page never leads, nor one to a page in the trash, which keeps its title and is told by the `status` each change carries.
  - **Recent activity** runs down the right with the rest of the same `page_activity` read (forty changes): ONE ROW PER PAGE with its newest change, eleven pages at most, never the featured page again, under the COMPANY's days (Today and Yesterday cut at the company's midnight). By page, because three people answering one comment were three rows of one page; named for activity, since most of what moves a page is its discussion. Home's widget of the same name folds its rows the same way. Each row says its time of day on that clock (its age is the time's title) and its note: a save's own, a comment's words or a new page's first line, never the title again. **Every change** opens the audit log narrowed to Doclet's changes. With nothing written beside the featured change the column is not drawn, the big tile being the whole of it.
  - The tiles share one inset and three equal columns. Four small tiles list three pages each and say one line when empty: **Continue reading** (pages this browser opened last) and **Pinned** (pages this reader starred from a page's More menu), each read for its title now and who last saved it; **Watching** (pages this person follows: `pages{watcher}`, asked by the seat they act as, not asked at all for a credential bound to no seat, which follows no page and is told so); **For the agents** (Agent skills with the engine's count of published tool skills; Agent diaries with how many agents keep one and when the newest reflection was written).
  - The grid places each tile by a named area, so markup keeps the reading order at every width: below 928px the feed moves under the newest change and small tiles pair up; below 640px one column.
  - Where knowledge lives in a vendor's wiki there is nothing on the engine to browse, and the landing says so rather than drawing an error.
- **The results** are the ranked answer GROUPED BY SPACE beside a PREVIEW of the chosen result. Grouping never reorders the engine's rank: a group is one space's hits in engine order, groups follow their best hit, every hit keeps its rank number; **Ranked** draws the one list as it came. A space filter narrows what is shown of the ranked answer, because the engine's search takes no space. `j` and `k` move the choice; the preview reads the chosen page: space, Author, Last saved, Read by agents, Linked from, and its opening with searched words MARKED (`Highlight`, never inside a word).
- **Results say what ranked them**: "ranked by Keyword" in the head; a sentence above the hits when the engine served other than asked (`served_mode`, `degraded`); a warning when the fan-out was PARTIAL, naming the buckets nobody scanned and the node that did not answer (`coverage`), because a short list from two thirds of the corpus otherwise looks like a small corpus. On Doclet the search reads this node's own copy of the pages. The results end with how to move through them (`j` and `k` move, Enter opens).
- **A search that did not run** says which of `no_company`, `no_backend`, `no_scope` or `building` it was, with that reason's remedy: a backend to set, spaces to add to `knowledge.scope`, or, while a recently joined node is still indexing, try again shortly. The fifth reason, `no_access`, is the READER'S not the company's (a caller holding Worklet and not Doclet, whose question searched nothing) and is said in the words every lock uses ("Search needs Doclet access. An admin can give it to you."), nothing to configure. The dashboard asks only of a Doclet holder (`lib/useSearchQuery.ts`), so it is drawn only for an answer that raced an access change.
- **A space's peek** (opened from a list elsewhere) reads one window of 500 and COUNTS off the listing's `total`: Recent pages and "n more pages in this space" are the space's, never the window's. When the space outgrows the window, Recent pages and Who writes here each say they cover the first pages by title, since the listing is ordered by title not time.

Who files into a space and the tracker project it works in are named for a reader who may read the company document (an admin) in four states: read (which may be "No team owns this space"), not held (the reader lacks Admin), read in flight, refused. "Needs Admin access" is said only to a reader without it. A space's head leaves out the team it is named after (a team's own space takes the team's name) and says "Also filed by" for another team filing there. A project the space's key does not already name is drawn beside it as a dashed key, not only in a tooltip.

### A space: its head and its outline

`#/doclet/{CONTAINER}` is the space's head over its pages as an OUTLINE. The head names the space and its key, its purpose, its page count, when somebody last wrote in it (the newest change to what a page says, from the space's change log, `page_activity{container, kinds}`, never the newest row of a listing ordered by title), who files into it, the tracker project its units work in where the key does not already name it, and when it was made.

- **The outline** is the design system's tree grid (`TreeGrid`) under a head: each row's title and Draft mark, who last saved what the page says (the engine's `saved_by`, drawn as an author is below) and when (`saved_at`, never `updated_at`, which a label or watch moves). The row is the page's link; Enter opens it. On a phone a row is the title on its own line, wrapping, with who and when under it.
- **A head orders each level among itself** (`sort=`), never across parents; the tree's own order is the default, which no head marks; Create and More stay last. A LEVEL WITH MORE TO LOAD KEEPS THE ENGINE'S ORDER, A to Z, and its More row says so: ordered here it would read as an order over pages nobody has read.
- **One level at a time.** The top level (`pages{container, roots}`) and a page's level (`pages{parent}`) are each read the moment the row opens, never before (`defaultExpanded="none"`), in windows of 500 with **Load more** and "n of total". A row opens where the engine counted pages under it the same listing would show, and on a FOLDER (a page with nothing written in it) even when it holds none, so its Create row can be reached.
- **Create** ends every open level. **Document** goes to the composer filed where the row is; **Folder** turns the row into a name field, and Enter writes it at once as a page with an EMPTY BODY (`write_page`), which is what a folder is: the engine derives it on every read and stores no kind for it. Escape lets the name go. A name taken in the space is the engine's refusal, drawn under the field. Create is drawn for every reader, disabled with the reason for one who cannot write.
### A page: the document, its outline, and what it is connected to

`#/doclet/pages/{id}` is the document in one column with its outline to the left, following the scroll (`Outline`, `useActiveHeading`). Below the phone breakpoint it is one column and the outline is not drawn.

Headings step by one under the trail's `h1`: the page's title is an `h2` (`DocumentTitle as="h2"`, as every object's title is in the frame), and the body's shallowest heading is an `h3` whatever `#` it was written with, each deeper one stepping from it (`renderMarkdown`'s `headingsFrom`). A second `h1` gives a screen reader two page titles, and a body written from `##` would open two levels under it.

- **The page bar**: **Watch** (or **Unwatch**), **History**, **Edit**, **More**. Watch is words, since an eye alone can read as a preview. It watches or stops as the person (a `save_page` carrying only `watch`); the count beside it opens who is told: watchers less those who muted the page (an unwatch mutes, not deletes), drawn "N watching". A watch is kept under the seat the person acts as, because a wake reaches only a seat, so for a credential bound to no seat Watch is disabled with that reason. More holds **Star this page**, **New sub-page**, **Publish** on a draft or **Move back to draft** on a published page, **Rename**, **Labels**, **Move**, **Move to trash**, **History**, **Copy the page's address**. Move's places are a list in its dialog (the kit's inline combobox, as Artifacts' Move): every page of the space but the page and what is under it, plus the space's top, filtered by words from a title or path, the current place marked, nothing covering Cancel and Move. The star lives only in More; the page tells the frame to draw none of its own (`useOwnStar`).
- **The properties**, minimal: Space (with the pages above this one), Author (who started it), Last saved ("2 hours ago by SWE", the revision and its note on the line itself, read on hover and by a screen reader), and Kind where the page is not plain prose: Draft, Onboarding, or a tool skill with who it reached as a skill over thirty days ("loaded as a skill by SWE", "offered" when no seat asked for the body, "not loaded in 30 days" when neither). A kind is words, never a state's colour. Every name here (author, last saver, commenter, a revision's or change's author) is drawn as a task's reporter is: a handle the roster holds is that seat (people write as the seat they hold); anything else is the login of a credential bound to no seat.
- **A draft says so above its body**, in a neutral notice ("This page is a draft. Search leaves it out until it is published."; it is still listed in its space, and its Kind line says "Draft" alone) with **Publish** beside it, a `save_page` carrying only `status`. In the editor a draft's Save reads **Save draft** and **Publish** sits beside it, saving and publishing in one write; with nothing edited it sends the status alone, so no revision is written. Who may publish is the engine's to decide (`pages.publish`: the page's creator, its space's lead, an administrator); its refusal is said in the notice.
- **Tidying a page happens on it.** Rename is `POST /doclet/pages/{id}/rename` (the title is the page's address in its space; links name it by id). Labels replaces the whole label set; Move files it under another page of its space or at its top (every page but itself and those beneath it, which the engine refuses as a parent); both are `save_page` against the version on screen. Move to trash asks first and is `DELETE /doclet/pages/{id}`. Each route write is keyed, so a retry after a lost answer is the same write. A trashed page is still read by id and says so above its body ("This page is in the trash") with **Restore** (`POST …/restore`) and, for an administrator, **Delete permanently** (`POST …/purge`, the title typed back and a reason, since nothing undoes it). It READS AND TAKES NO CHANGE: Edit, the watch and New sub-page are held with one reason ("It is in the trash. Restore it first."), its comments read with no field under them, and the engine refuses every write but restore and purge (save, label, watch, move, rename, every comment gesture). A space lists what it holds in the trash under its outline, each linking to the page. Who may rename, trash and restore (creator, space lead, administrator) is the engine's to decide; its refusal is drawn in the dialog that pressed.
- **The body** is the design system's `Document` over the dashboard's renderer, with anchors on its headings; a first heading repeating the title is not drawn twice. A FOLDER says it groups pages and lists what is filed under it.
- **Comments**, then **Connections**: three cards, *Linked from* (tasks by key with status, one whose key another task claimed first linking by its id, then pages by title), *Read by agents* (last 30 days: each seat with its read count, then how it reached the page and when, linking the turn; the way-read cut with an ellipsis so the age never wraps onto a third line) and *Under this page*, three rows each and "Show n more". A signal this node cannot answer is not drawn rather than drawn empty: no readers on a node without the usage domain, no *Linked from* on one without an index. A node holding an index that cannot answer says why instead of "No page or task links here" (`linked_from_status` `building` or `unavailable`). The capped-reads note is worded company-wide ("Some reads may be missing."), because `elided` counts what the cap dropped on every page.
- **History** swaps the outline for the revisions and the comments for the page's changes, each drawn as the person, the change and the turn that made it. It reads one revision in the page's place, as what it changed against the one before (by line) or as its full text, headed once by the title that names the revision.
- **Edit writes as you, in place.** The page becomes the editor (the design system's `RichEditor`, [ADR-0044](../../adr/0044-a-page-is-edited-in-place-and-saved-as-the-markdown-it-was.md)): it looks the same edited as read, blocks come from a slash menu or Markdown typed as Markdown, a selection gets a formatting toolbar, and the bar's Edit becomes Cancel and Save. The body stays Markdown, and a save with no edit sends the bytes that were opened, so only lines a writer changed move. It saves through `save_page` on [`/operator/act`](api-endpoints.md#operatoract--the-dashboards-write-surface) with the opened revision as `base_version`. The page keeps being read while open (every 20 s), so another's save is SEEN before Save: the editor says "Somebody saved revision n while you edited", offers their change as a diff, and "Keep editing on top of it" MERGES it into the draft by line before the base moves (`lib/merge.ts`, a three-way merge over the revision the edit started from, each side compared with it by the design system's line diff; a side that diff does not compare is one clash of the whole page, the person's to settle). A change only one side made is taken as is; where both changed the same lines the base stays behind and each clash is shown, their lines beside the draft's, to keep theirs, yours or both, nothing pre-chosen and the draft held until applied. Moving the base without the merge would let the next save be accepted against the new revision and delete what they wrote, which is what the engine's stale-base refusal prevents. Save and Command or Control with Enter read one answer for whether a save can be sent. A page link is inserted from the slash menu's "Link to a page" by picking a page, written in the address the backlinks read (`PAGE_ADDRESS_PREFIX`, held against `doclet.AddressPrefix` by a test). The note kept with the revision is a line under the page, beside its word count.

### The composer: a new page

`#/doclet/new` writes a new page, filed by the address (`?space=…&parent=…`): **New page** in the bar, a space's Create row and a page's **New sub-page** each open it filed where pressed. It is written at the measure it is read at (`--size-measure`, the page's reading column), with Similar pages and Labels beside it.

- **File it in** names the space and the page it goes under (or the space's top); both can change. Until a space is chosen, the row says so beside the space field ("Choose a space first. Save as draft and Publish file the page there."), the one hold nothing else shows. **Start from** offers a blank page or a template (a design for a work item, a runbook, a decision record); a template takes only an empty page, or one still holding the template it started from, so it never replaces writing.
- **The title is the page's address in its space**: a title already taken there is said under the field as it settles, beside a way to open that page, and holds both presses. Title size, body (512 KB) and labels (32, each 64 bytes) are held at the engine's caps (`PAGE_TITLE_MAX_BYTES`, `PAGE_BODY_MAX_BYTES`, `PAGE_LABELS_MAX`, `PAGE_LABEL_MAX_BYTES`, held against `internal/doclet` by a test) and said, never cut.
- **Similar pages** is the knowledge search on the title, asked once the title rests, so a page that already answers this is found first. **Labels** are typed in place.
- **Save as draft** and **Publish** are one `write_page` with `status`: a draft is listed in its space, marked Draft, and found by no search until published. The writer lands on the new page by the id the engine answered with.
- **Discard** asks first when anything is written, and so does any move away (`useLeaveGuard`).

A reader without a write credential sees every button with the reason it is unavailable, never a button that fails.

### Agent skills

`#/doclet/skills` has two kinds behind one address.

**Tool skills** (`kind=pages`, the default) lists every published tool-skill page with who it reached over thirty company days (the `pages` listing's `skill_loaded_by`, read with the listing, not per row) and the listing's total, with Load more past a window. Order is the ENGINE's, asked by the **Skill** and **Updated** heads and kept in `sort=`: by name (`sort=title`, the knowledge base's order) or newest first (`sort=-updated`, the listing's `order: "newest"`, by when each skill last changed, from the skill rows' own index). A head asks and never sorts here: sorting one window's rows would put, past a window, the newest of the alphabetically first skills on top. The engine reads each order one way, so a second press goes back to the default. Home's **Agent skills** widget asks for the newest the same way. **An empty catalogue says where a tool skill goes**: the space the engine names for them (`containers` answers `skills`, its key), linked, and **New page** filed in it, held for anybody but an admin, who alone may write there; a company with tool skills turned off is told so.

**Learned** (`kind=learned&seat=`) is one agent seat's synthesized skills from `agent_memory`, answered by the node holding the seat, with "n of total" when cut. Order is the HOLDER's for the same reason, asked by the **Uses** and **Updated** heads and kept in `sort=`: most used (`sort=-uses`, the default) or most recently changed (`sort=-updated`), asked as the question's `skills_order` (`uses`, `updated`) and applied to the seat's whole set before the page is cut.

### Agent diaries

`#/doclet/diaries` lists EVERY agent seat in the chart, from `memory_overview`: each agent's newest note, when written, and its entry, episode and skill TOTALS, counted by the node holding the agent. No row names that node: which node runs an agent is the fleet's business (Settings › Nodes, the seat's own page), and a column of node names is the one a narrow screen keeps longest. An agent no node holds says so and shows no counts, since no copy of its memory is current; one whose holder did not answer says that instead of drawing zeros, and the partial callout every fleet answer draws names the node and why. The landing's **Agent diaries** row counts the agents listed. `#/doclet/diaries/{handle}` is one agent's diary and episodes (the same two cards its page's Memory section draws, from the same holder-answered `agent_memory`), with when it last wrote or the reason nothing is shown, and the way to its whole memory: a link to the seat's learned skills and remembered colleagues, or plain words when it has neither.

## Spend: tokens by phase, agent and model

Spend is Settings' **Spend** group: what the engine's runs spent, read by every reader. The ceilings are [Company › Budgets](#company--budgets-raised-in-place); Settings lists readings, never ceilings, and Budgets is not a second row here.

`#/settings/spend` is one window of **whole company days**, 7, 30 or 90 (opens on 30, a daily chart's shortest useful run and the monthly budget's scale), or two dates a reader names (the custom picker takes two dates on the company's clock, both counted: the answer is company days and a minute picker would offer false precision). Everything is that window, read from the replicated usage domain, and every card names the window in words built from the ANSWER (`last 30 days`, or the dates), not from the control. There is no live rolling window: a "24 hours" beside company-day charts puts two incomparable windows on one screen.

**A window the engine refuses draws no figures.** More than 90 days, or a start before the history's floor, is refused in the engine's own sentence (which says which and what to change), shown once at the top and nothing under it: the previous answer is not kept beneath a control naming a different window, and Export has nothing to export.

**Three rows, each one height.** The hero beside the daily chart; **By agent** beside **By model** and **By team**, stacked; then the **most expensive tasks** beside the **auxiliary model**.
- The two rows under the hero share one pair of tracks (1.7 : 1), so the gutter runs down the page as one line: the wide track holds what is read along a row (the seats' table, the tasks' titles), the narrow one the ranked lists. The three ranked lists give their words one column, half the card, so bars start at one x and a team's name is not cut at the kit's 128px.
- Every card in a row stretches to the tallest. A stretched card keeps content at the top and its foot on the floor; an EMPTY card's state stands in the middle of what its head and foot leave. The stacked lists' last card takes what the stack leaves, and a card whose partner is absent (no task spend to rank on a tracker that is not Worklet) takes the whole row.
- In the top row the hero's figure stays at its top while the budget and the tiles stand on its floor, level with the chart's split control; a tile with nothing to say is not drawn and the other takes the tiles' whole row. Where the hero is taller, the chart's plot takes the spare height (the kit's `height="fill"`, never under 12rem), so the split control stands right under the dates.
- Below a page column of 900px every row stacks, the table first; the width is the page column's, not the window's.

- **The hero** is the window's tokens, the change against the window before it (the engine's `previous=true`, cut on the company's calendar, and "nothing was spent" rather than a percentage when the window before spent nothing), and where the history's floor is (`horizon.floor`).
- **This month** is the budget gate's monthly window from the `budget` push: "used of limit · resets Oct 1" on a kit `Meter` handed the engine's `state`, never a fraction judged here, the reset on the company's calendar. With no monthly ceiling it says so and offers **Set one** (to `#/company/budgets`) only to an admin, and only once a report has SAID so: before the engine's first report the push is `null` and the tile waits, because "nobody has read the counter" is not "no ceiling" (Home's weekly line reads the same slice the same way).
- **The prompt cache's share** is `cache_read_tokens / input_tokens` (input already includes the cached prefix). A window in which nothing reported a cache has **no cache tile**, not 0%, which would claim something nobody measured.
- **The median task** is Worklet's `totals=spend_tokens:median` over tasks FINISHED in the window that spent anything, with how many. Where none finished, the figure is `EmptyValue`'s mark ("No task finished in this window spent tokens") and the line under it ends "none in this window" ("No tasks" in the figure's place reads with the label as one phrase). Where the tracker is not Worklet, `work_items` is not served and the tile is not drawn.
- **A reader without Worklet is asked nothing about tasks.** The overview is everybody's and a task is Worklet's, so the median tile and the most expensive tasks card each say *Needs Worklet access* (the card with no **All** link, since the list is Worklet's too), and no `work_items` is sent: asked, the engine's refusal drew a callout offering to sign in to somebody already signed in.
- **Daily tokens by phase** is the kit's `StackedColumns` over the engine's four bands, each in its `BANDS` hue; the legend is always those four (the engine answers an unspent band at zero). The split control offers the contract's six `GROUPS` (Phase, Model, Provider, Agent, Team, Worker; each `label` and the title's `noun` are the names the cards use, so the control says Agent and Team, not Seat and Unit). Any split but phase draws the engine's top four and a residual, listing only bands that spent (the engine names a band for every team or model that made a call, a zero-spend call included); "The four biggest, and everything else as one band" is said only where the engine folded a residual. A seat band is labelled with the seat's name as the table under it names it, a team band with the unit's. **A window that spent no token is one empty state**, never an axis: the figure is tokens, so it is empty when nothing spent, not when nothing was called, and a window of refused calls says "No tokens spent in this window" with how many calls were made ("887 calls, none spent tokens") and why they spent nothing. The comparison is the hero's; the chart draws no ghost of the window before. The legend stands at the end of the title's row; on a card too narrow for both (a phone) it takes its own row under the title, still at the end.
- **By agent**: turns, tokens, share, **budget today** (the seat's daily window from its overlay, `exhausted` where the engine says `refusing`) and tokens per ended turn. A PERSON the auxiliary model spent for (`person: true`: their questions answered with `answer_knowledge`, and the background passes of a unit they lead) is a row of their own, keyed by handle, whose turns and per-turn cells say it is auxiliary model spend for that person. A row opens the seat in the peek. On a phone a seat is one compact two-line row at every density: name, tokens and share, then turns · today · per turn, each with its unit, today as its percentage alone (the day's bar is for scanning a column, which a compact row has none of). **Recent turns by tokens** goes to `#/live/turns?sort=-tokens` over the same window where the turn list has it (a quarter goes to its thirty days, and a caption beside the link says so): a company day holds no turn, so per-turn spend is the turn list's.
- **By model** is the engine's `by_provider`: each configured provider entry, the models it answered with, who used it (top three and how many more) and its tokens. An entry whose calls spent nothing is no row; where none spent, the empty state counts the calls made, as Settings › Models & Fleets counts them, rather than claiming no model was called. **Which calls a count counts** is said once, in `lib/spend.ts` (`UNSPENT_CALLS`, `callsWords`), for every screen drawing calls beside tokens (Token spend's chart and By model, Models' tokens tile and a model's usage card): the engine counts every call made, a refused or failed one included, and such a call spends no token. **By team** is `token_series{group: unit}` asked for every team. **Auxiliary model** is `by_worker`: what the seats' cheap model spent, by purpose (`memory filter`, `condense thread`, `persist decider`, …) and its provider calls. It is a breakdown, not an addition: each call is already in the row of the seat or person it was made for, under the Auxiliary band. The embedding pass is metered nowhere and is not claimed.
- **An empty card says so one way**, the kit's compact empty state, whether it holds a ranked list, a table or the chart.
- **Export** is a client CSV of the rollup and the by-agent table, every row labelled with its window and section, tokens only, every text cell guarded so a spreadsheet opens a name as text, not a formula.

`#/settings/spend/tasks`, **Expensive tasks** (the Spend group's second row, not offered where the company does not run Worklet), is the tasks last changed inside the window, bounded at both edges (`closed_since` plus `updated=range:<since>..<until>` from the spend answer's own instants, so a window that ended last month lists nothing that moved only this week), most tokens first (`sort=-spend_tokens`, the engine's order), each with what drove it from `fields=spend`: its turns, and its reopens, workers and send-backs where not zero, and a bar beside the figure scaled to the top task (not a percentage: a lifetime's tokens are a share of no window's total). A task's tokens are its whole life's (Worklet charges a task, not a day), and the list says so. The overview shows the top three. A refused window has no list: the page says the refusal and nothing waits for an answer never asked. On a phone each task is the overview card's compact row (key and title with what drove it under, tokens at the end), not a labelled card per task.
## Company › Atlas

`#/company/atlas`, the row after Integrations (`g o`): what those connections,
the company's settings and the engine's records say it runs on
([the atlas](../concepts/atlas.md)). It belongs to the **Atlas** app, given only
on purpose, so the row is locked, never hidden, for a reader without it, the
lock naming the access to ask for. One item is an **entry** everywhere ("48
entries").

**On Home** the atlas offers one widget (`routes/atlas/home.widgets.tsx`; see
[Home is the reader's board](#home-is-the-readers-board)), `atlas.attention`,
**Atlas attention**: the counts of Alerting and Needs a look as two stat tiles,
then the four most urgent entries, each a kit list row (the list's `template`
gives health, a status dot and word, its own column so names start at one edge)
with name and the engine's one-sentence reason, linking to
`#/company/atlas/<id>`, and "N more on the page" when counts exceed the rows. It
asks what the page's band asks (`atlas_facets`, `atlas_entries` sorted by
health) every sixty seconds. States:

- **Nothing wrong**: "Nothing is alerting" with the entry count, only over reads
  whose every source was read in full.
- **Empty atlas**: "Nothing in the atlas yet".
- **A source not read**: the rows it has, then one line a source ("What people
  recorded in the atlas was not read, so this may be short."); with no rows,
  "Nothing to list" over the same lines, never "nothing is alerting".
- **Loading**: the card's header alone. **A refused or failed read**: the
  refusal its page would draw.
- **No Atlas access**: "You no longer have access to Atlas." in the widget's
  place, not offered in the tray. The module is not mounted so nothing is asked;
  the engine refuses both questions anyway: no entry's name reaches them.

**It is one page**: band, toolbar, coverage line, map, catalogue. No view
switch: map and catalogue are one answer drawn twice, sharing one search, one
set of filters and one selection, all read from the address. Every part is a
kit component; `styles/atlas.css` only places them.

**The band** is four kit `Card` tiles: one row on a wide page ("Needs attention
now" takes the leftover width so each card says name and reason on one line);
two columns with that tile across both on a narrower page; one on a phone.
Beside an open sheet (a third narrower) it keeps one row of its first two tiles
and the map keeps its height. It is about the company: search and filters do not
narrow it.

- *The company runs on*: a `StackedRing` round the count of entries the filters
  leave, split Quiet, Needs a look, Alerting (`atlas_facets`), beside its
  `Legend`.
- *Needs attention now*: the two most urgent entries (`atlas_entries`, health
  order), each with disc, name, the one-sentence reason on two lines, a second
  signal named and more counted. The card is a button selecting the entry on the
  map and bringing the map into view under the sticky band; it is named by its
  own words, the whole reason among them, and the kit's tooltip (never a native
  title) shows the whole reason on hover and focus. Below, links one per health
  (*Alerting 2*, *Needs a look 4*) to the catalogue and map narrowed to it
  (`health=`). Count and cards are two reads: cards are a skeleton until theirs
  answers, and "Nothing needs attention." is said only where the count agrees.
- *Recorded this week*: the atlas log's lines of the last seven days as one
  figure over an `ActivityStrip` of its fourteen (`atlas_activity`).
- *Where it comes from*: vendors' marks over a `StackedBar` of Confirmed, Likely,
  Unconfirmed with its `Legend`.

With nothing in the atlas and no filter set the band is not drawn: a ring of
zeros is a claim nobody made. **Nothing on the page is a rate, a latency or an
error budget**, because the engine holds none: health is its word for an entry's
open signals, activity a count of log lines, and the map's moving dashes show
direction, never volume.

**The map** is the kit's `GraphCanvas` in the kit `Canvas` (zoom bar, keys, fit,
fullscreen), in one look: fine grid, see-through cluster panes with the title in
the outline, outlined cards on the ground's colour, right-angled lines routed
round every card. That drawing stays inside the map's world; legend, dock, hover
card and zoom bar are the kit's own shapes. Lanes are the engine's (`lane` on
every entry), read in three rows (`MAP_ROWS`): what a request travels (Entry,
Services, Data), what that stands on (Runtime, Platforms), what stands around it
(Code and delivery, Observability, Tools and models).

**The lanes are arranged for the canvas** (`routes/atlas/arrange.ts`): which
lanes share a row, how many columns of cards each takes and how wide a card is
(the kit's to twice it) are chosen from the map's box (the screen when
fullscreen) and what each lane holds, so the fitted map fills its canvas. A row
of `MAP_ROWS` is split into consecutive rows or stood whole beside the next,
never mixed with part of another, so the reading order holds. Each arrangement
is scored by the fit it gets, planned with the kit's sizes and chrome: nothing
under the zoom bar; no name drawn smaller than a tile's 10px (from half size to
about three quarters a card draws its name at its own scale, so such a fit
draws tiles with wider cards instead), clear of each level's edge; a zoom
within a tenth of the largest; every lane's title showing its first letters
and its figures (ahead of the zoom where every fit draws marks); then the card
width that says the most names whole, and the arrangement nearest `MAP_ROWS`.
The same entries on the same box arrange alike. A new arrangement is drawn
on the same canvas and fitted (`fitKey` carries it), and the kit fits it
again once its cards are measured at the new width (`Canvas`'s `refitKey`);
a new canvas would drop the screen a fullscreen map holds. It follows the
box, or the screen while the map is fullscreen, when that changes by more
than 3%, and is held while an entry is selected, so a sheet opening beside
the page never moves the entries. **Every lane is drawn**: an
empty one says what in this build fills it (the Cloudflare integration's zones,
the SSH servers, the integrations' accounts, Gitlet and the repositories the
code hosts name, the models and tool servers) or, for a lane only people fill,
that a person adds one with Add entry, never a promise. A link to fill it (Open
Cloudflare, Open SSH, Open Integrations, Open Models) is drawn only for a reader
who may open it. With a filter set, an empty lane says nothing matched.

A card is one line: the kind's glyph in a ruled cell, the vendor's mark on its
corner, the name, then its key or "Last seen 9 days ago" where no source has
seen it lately.

- **Health is a notch on the card's leading edge with a badge**: danger for
  Alerting, warning for Needs a look, said in words to a screen reader; each
  cluster's title tallies its own.
- **Open work is the same notch in the info tone** ("Being worked on") on a
  quiet entry an open Worklet task names (`atlas_work`, asked only for a reader
  who uses Worklet). Health keeps the notch on an entry needing attention; the
  hover card says how many open tasks name it either way. A quiet entry nothing
  names draws none.
- Confidence is a line, never a colour: an unconfirmed entry has a dashed edge.

The map asks for every relation (`atlas_map` with `relations=all`) and draws
each in the engine's family: `calls` at rest, dashes moving the way it points;
`runs_on` at rest as one trunk per pair of clusters with its count; `around`
for the entry a reader stands on. The legend switches each family and keys the
notch, Quiet and Unconfirmed, and Being worked on for a reader whose work is
read.

Past 150 entries drawn (`ATLAS_OPEN_MAX`) entries stand in closed groups by
vendor inside their lane, each one card saying what it holds, with the vendor's
mark where the kit has one and the card's glyph where not; under it every entry
is its own card. A service on a call chain stands one column right of the
deepest service calling it; one on none flows across the lane like any other
lane's entries, and a chain deeper than the lane is wide ends in its last
column. A narrowed map draws only the lanes holding what matched (every lane
while nothing does), arranged like any other, so a few matches open at a
readable size, on a phone too. A map past what the engine
draws at once arrives with groups the engine closed (`collapsed`), named in a
banner above the map with a link to read each in the catalogue, so a partial map
is never taken for the whole.
