**The map opens fitted to its view** (kit 0.127.0): all of it, centred, at the
zoom that fits its box and the level of detail that zoom draws (a large company
as tiles or marks, never blank boxes), with no other view painted first. The kit
fits again when its first entries arrive and when its box is resized while
nobody has moved the view; a poll keeps the reader's view. Under half size an
empty lane is its dashed outline, words returning with the cards. It fits again
when the answer it draws is for other filters, keyed on what the answer on
screen was read with (`fitKey`), not the question being asked, since a changed
filter keeps the last answer on screen until the new one lands. A selection the
address arrives with (`sel=`, or `peek=atlas:{id}`, which **Show it on the map**
and a sheet's link carry) opens the map on that entry instead (the kit's
`initialNode`): in the middle of the room the bars leave, at up to three
quarters, or on the fit where that already draws it as large. It is read once,
when the map is first placed, so a later selection never moves the view.

**One selection** (`sel={id}`, or the entry the sheet is open on) is lit on the
map along its whole path both ways, the rest receding to a fifth and lit lines
under a glow with faster dashes, and is marked in the catalogue. The dock at the
map's foot names it (disc, name, kind, health, "Over every hop, 7 entries rely
on it and it relies on 1": the set the map lights, said as every hop so it never
reads as the sheet's count one step out; none is "nothing relies on it"), with
**Details**, which opens its sheet and leaves fullscreen first since the sheet
is the shell's, and a clear button. A press on the selected card, the ground or
Escape also clears. A link with `trace=up` or `trace=down` narrows the lit path
to that side; selecting another entry drops it. Pointer or focus on a card lights
its neighbours and opens a card beside it (disc, name, kind and vendor, health
word, the reason it is not quiet); the entry is lit in the catalogue too, and
the row under the pointer is lit on the map (`hoveredId` and `onHover`,
`isPointed` and `onRowPoint`). Every motion stops for a reader who asked for
less.

**The toolbar** is the search and one **Filter** control. The control is a kit
`Popover` holding five menus (Kind, Lane, Vendor, Health, Confidence, each
listing the values with entries and counting each over every other filter,
`atlas_facets`), **Show unconfirmed**, **Show retired entries only**
(`show=retired`, retired entries alone, where the Retire dialog sends a reader),
and Clear all filters; its button carries the count of filters in force. A
closed filter's address value is kept only where the dashboard's word tables
know it (`parseFilters`); an unknown one is not applied, sent or drawn as a
chip, and a warning banner names it with **Remove it**. While any filter is set,
each is a removable chip (kit `FilterPill`, "Kind is Server") in a row under the
toolbar with Clear all; none set, no row. Filters narrow map and catalogue
alike. **The search does not remove anything from the map**: the catalogue lists
what matches (a name, key or id, asked once typing settles), and the map keeps
its shape and pushes back what does not, the matching set being the engine's own
answer. An entry only an agent reported, with nothing the engine could check, is
left out of every read until a person confirms it, so the switch is off by
default and says how many it would add; choosing Unconfirmed under Confidence
shows them and holds the switch on, with its reason.

**The coverage line** (kit `PageNote` under the toolbar, which wraps on a phone)
is how many entries the filters leave and which vendors they come from, most
entries first, four named before "and N more": "48 entries, from GitHub,
Cloudflare, Gitlet and Anthropic". It never says complete. Its notes are what
the read could not read in full, in the engine's reason (Gitlet for a reader who
does not use it), and how many values were left out for looking like a
credential, counted, never shown. Drawn once the first count arrives.

**The catalogue** is the frame's grid in bands, one per health, most urgent
first, each heading with its mark and its whole group's count. It reads
`atlas_entries` fifty a page with Load more in the engine's health order
(`sort=health`), so a page never splits a group and the grid sorts nothing. A
row is:

- the entry: disc with vendor's mark, a ring and badge when it needs a person, a
  dashed edge while unconfirmed, then name and kind;
- its vendor; its owner as a chip or "No owner yet";
- health word and mark, with a second line where open work names the entry (a
  kit `StatusDot` in the info tone and "2 open tasks", a link to the entry's
  Work tab);
- how many entries use it and how many it depends on;
- activity (a fine `Sparkline` of recorded lines a day beside their count, from
  `atlas_activity`);
- last change (when, and the log line's sentence) and confidence word.

Columns give way in order on a narrow grid; a phone reads each row as a card. A
row opens the entry's sheet and selects it, a modifier press opens its page, and
the foot says "That is all of it" with the count once no page is left.

**The sheet is the peek** (`peek=atlas:{id}`), so a reload, Back or a link lands
on the same picture; its entry is the selection, which stays lit when the sheet
closes. It holds:

- the header: disc beside name, kind and key, health word, owner, confidence
  word, the one line a person gave it, vendor, when last seen, number of
  sources;
- signals ("Nothing is wrong with it: no source reports a signal on it." when
  none, never "open", the word the Work tab counts tasks in);
- **What it touches**: how many entries rely on it and it relies on, in the
  engine's counts, none said as nothing ("Nothing relies on it, and it relies on
  nothing.", alone with no diagram for an entry with no relation); otherwise over
  a still `GraphCanvas` of the entry among its neighbours, each in the cluster
  saying how it relates: Relies on it, This entry, Depends on, Runs on, Around
  it;
- facts with where each came from, what relies on it, what it relies on, what
  stands around it (`relatedOf`, the diagram's own clusters, so list counts are
  the sentence's; six each, then a pointer to the page);
- its **Work**: open tasks naming it, five, then a pointer to the page's Work
  tab; locked with its reason without Worklet;
- **Recent changes** as a kit `Timeline` from `atlas_log` (six, then a pointer);
- the way to show it on the map.

**An entry's page** (`#/company/atlas/{id}`) is the same header and five tabs.

- **Overview**: signals, what it touches with the diagram drawn wide, facts
  grouped Identity, Meaning, Details, each with a by-line of where the value came
  from and how far it is trusted ("seen by Cloudflare · confirmed · 4 min ago",
  "observed by sre · likely · turn"), use channel by channel, agents holding an
  account at it, the exact keys merged into it, its eight latest changes, then
  the way to History.
- **Relations**: what relies on it, what it relies on, what stands around it
  (the tab counts all three), the seats, units and pages it names, and
  everything relying on it over every hop (`atlas_trace`), with the way to show
  it on the map in a link underlined as one set inside its sentence. A purge of
  the entry itself leaves it: its sheet closes, or its page goes back to the
  atlas.
- **Work** (`tab=work`): Worklet tasks naming the entry (`atlas_entry_work`),
  open ones most recently changed first, then "Finished in the last 30 days",
  drawn by Worklet's own task rows and opening the task, "50 of 120" where a list
  is cut at its page. The tab counts the open ones and says so in words while
  any exist (the kit tab's `live`). A reader with Atlas but not Worklet sees tab
  and panel locked with "Needs Worklet access" (kit `LockedLabel`), unasked;
  where the engine read no work for another reason, its sentence is the empty
  state.
- **Sources**: where sources disagree, first: each fact or relation with the
  value shown, every other value beside it and the rule in words (a person's
  value is shown over a newer report, or the newest of two equally trusted
  sources), and in every case that the entry waits for a person: nothing is
  settled on the reader's behalf, each carrying its decisions as buttons (keep
  the value shown, take another). Then every source and what it says. A
  disagreement marks the tab.
- **History**: every line of `atlas_log` for the entry, a page at a time.

**On a work item**, the rail's **Atlas entries** group is the other end of the
same link (a task's `atlas_entry` links, ADR-0140). With Atlas, each entry is a
kit `Tag` with its kind's glyph and name (`atlas_named`, one ask for every
linked id) opening the entry's sheet and removed with its own control; **Link an
atlas entry** opens the entry picker in a dialog loaded with the atlas's chunk;
both are `update_work_item` with `linked_entries`. An id naming no entry any
more is a warning chip "Missing entry" beside "1 entry is no longer in the
atlas.", removable. Without Atlas the group is one locked label, "3 atlas
entries" with "Needs Atlas access": the engine sends a count
(`entries_withheld`) and no id, and the atlas is asked nothing. A task's history
words the change as a count ("Atlas entries: 2 → 3").

**The writes** are the operator catalogue's atlas tools through `useAct`, each
row of `contract/actions.ts` naming the atlas's questions as `refreshes`, since
the atlas's log is no session domain and its reads take no floor. **Add entry**
ends the toolbar and opens a kit `Modal` form (kind, vendor for an account, name,
key, vendor account, owner, purpose, the Doclet page), one `atlas_add_entry`.
Under an entry's header, on sheet and page: **Confirm**, **Correct** (a dialog
showing the value the atlas holds with every other value beside the field) and a
kit `Menu`, **More** (Set owner, Add relation, Remove relation, Link a page,
Merge with, Split, Retire or Restore, Purge). Merge and Split draw what they do
before applying; Purge is held for anybody but an administrator, typed back with
the kit's `ConfirmField`, its press the danger fill. Fact and relation menus are
read off `ATLAS_FACT_SPECS` and `ATLAS_RELATION_PAIRS`, the engine's vocabulary
held both ways by a Go gate, so a control offers only what the engine accepts.
Every control is drawn for every reader and held with its reason; the engine's
refusal is drawn under the control in its own words.

**Review** (`#/company/atlas/review`) reads `atlas_review`, computed on the read:
kit chip `Tabs` by reason with counts (`kind=`), one outlined `Card` an item
with its box, entry, the value shown and every other beside it, and its
decisions. Picked items are decided together from the kit `SelectionBar`; a bulk
decision lists what it decides in a `Modal` and sends only on that dialog's
press, one write an item, an agent's entry listed with who reported it. An
agent's record carries its evidence: the by-line every claim has (seat,
"observed", the turn's link, when) and under it the call it cited, the tool's
name in the mono face an entry's key uses and what a call of that tool is
evidence of, in the secondary ink; drawn under an entry that waits as a whole
(`reports`) and beside an agent's value in a disagreement. Only drift on what the
reader set reaches the Inbox: the shell asks `atlas_review` with `mine` for a
holder of Atlas who acts as a seat, and each item is a caution row under Needs
you (subject `atlas`, "what you set in the atlas" in the quiet band's clause)
opening the entry's Sources tab. **Changes** (`#/company/atlas/changes`) is
`atlas_activity` as an `ActivityStrip` over `atlas_log` for the company as the
same `Timeline`, each line led by its entry. The band's *Recorded this week*
leads to Changes and *Where it comes from* to Review with its count and to
Sources; a tile's title is one line at every width.

**Sources** (`#/company/atlas/sources`) reads `atlas_sources`, the collect duty's
standing per integration off the coordination store, on the atlas's poll. One
kit `StatusCard` a source: name as title, when read and when read next under it,
and its state as the card's `Tag` (Read, Partly read, Last read failed, Not read
yet). The body is the last whole read as a flush `StatGroup` of four `StatCard`s
(entries, vendor calls, values withheld, changes recorded), what the read was
refused or how it failed as a compact `FindingList`, and for servers a kit
`Table` with each server's last whole read and its standing as a `StatusDot`. A
withheld value is a count, never drawn; a fault's own text is drawn for an
administrator, every other reader is told the read failed. *Refresh now* is the
card's one action, a `WriteButton` over `atlas_refresh`, held with its reason
while an ask already waits and inside the engine's five-minute floor
(`refreshable_at`), so a press is never sent to be refused; the standings are
asked again once it is answered.

**An internal address says so**: a value on a private network carries an
Internal tag, because the atlas keeps the company's own map rather than hiding
it. **Nothing leaves the screen**: no export, print or share, and the page bar
holds none. Every screen asks again every thirty seconds (`ATLAS_POLL_MS`), the
cadence of a screen whose signals nothing pushes. Screens, sheet and map code are
one chunk (`routes/atlas`), fetched on first open or by the idle prefetch.

## Company › Budgets, raised in place

`#/company/budgets`, the last row under Company (what the company decides; what
it spent is Settings › Token spend), is every scope's three calendar windows on
the company clock (day, ISO week, month) from the `budgets` answer: what each
has spent, its ceiling or **No ceiling**, when it resets and, while the gate is
refusing it, since when.

- **The company** first, as one row: everything a seat spends is the company's
  spend and its ceiling binds every seat at once.
- **Agent seats**: one table with a column per window, so the seat near its
  ceiling is found down a column. The company's row stands on the table's own
  columns (one track list handed to both), each window over its column, its first
  track saying once what the windows are: every seat together, on the company
  clock, when each turns over.
- **Ask Crewlet, per person**, on the same tracks: the ceiling every person's
  Ask Crewlet questions are held to (`assistant.token_budget`), each person on
  their own. Figures are the reader's own spend against it, drawn only where the
  engine counts one (`counted`: a person, under a company that caps a person's
  spend); elsewhere ceilings and no figure, since a zero nobody measured is not
  "0 tokens".

A window's bar is a kit `Meter` handed the engine's `state`; the page divides
nothing. A window with no ceiling draws no bar (nothing to be a fraction of). A
counter nobody could read (`durable: false`) says so and draws no figures.

**Every ceiling is editable in place by an admin.** The pencil turns the figure
into a field taking the spelling the screen draws (`40M`, `2.5M`, `750k`, or
digits) and **empty for no ceiling**; a 0 is refused before sending, in the
engine's terms (empty is the only "none"). A save is **checked first**, against
the revision it was read from, and only the warnings the change *introduces* are
shown (a seat ceiling at or above the company's, which can never refuse a turn,
is the one this screen exists to catch), with **Save anyway**.

- The company's ceilings are written as a merge patch of the windows that changed
  (`null` removes one); each person's Ask Crewlet ceiling as the same patch one
  level down (`{assistant: {token_budget: {...}}}`), leaving the rest of the
  `assistant:` block; a seat's by replacing that seat
  (`PUT /config/roles/{handle}`, its check the same request with
  `dry_run=true`), because a patch cannot address one seat in a roster. The
  revision's summary says whose ceiling, which window, from what to what.
- After a save the figure shows the new ceiling marked **applying…** until this
  node has applied the revision, then re-reads, judged by where this node stands
  on that revision (`lib/nodeStanding.ts`), never by its applied epoch alone,
  which a refusal leaves where it was.
- A node that refused it restores the ceiling the gate still enforces, marked
  **refused by this node**, until the pencil is pressed again or a later revision
  it applies settles it. A save a later activation passed before this node
  applied it settles on the re-read like an apply.
- The mark follows this node's LAST health push (`lib/useLastHealth.ts`): a
  dropped socket clears the store's health slice and is no news of the save, so a
  refusal stays said through it.
- A conflict saves nothing and offers **Reload**; so does a request that may have
  landed.
- Pencils are drawn for every reader, disabled with the reason said once above
  the page in the standard notice, for a reader without Admin, except a seat's,
  for the lead of its unit, whom the engine admits to that seat's write
  (`useOrgWriteAccess`, `lib/leadScope.ts`).

**There is no reset.** A window's `used` is what it spent; room returns when it
turns over, or now by raising its ceiling. The Inbox's and a stopped seat's
**Raise budget** open the same write as a dialog of one scope's three ceilings
(`RaiseBudgetDialog`), each field captioned with what that window has spent and
when it resets. A reader who may not raise that scope's ceiling is not handed
the button: the row says who can instead ("An admin can raise this ceiling.", the
units a lead leads, or who manages the document). The company's ceiling is no
lead's, so a lead is told who can raise it as any reader without Admin is, never
which units they lead.

**Each ceiling is a section a refusal opens.** A refusal or notice a token budget
caused names the setting behind it (ADR-0060's remedy), and `lib/remedy.ts` is
the one table from a setting to this screen and its section: `section=company`,
`section=assistant`, or `section=seat:<handle>` for a seat's row. The section is
brought into view, focused, and marked as the one the reader came for (the
card's `selected`, the seat's row as current); a press on the address already
open arrives again; a section the screen does not draw for the reader (a seat it
no longer lists) reveals nothing. The press is offered by the gate the editor is
drawn by (`useOrgWriteAccess`), so link and pencils cannot disagree: a reader the
gate refuses is told who can raise it, never handed a link to a screen whose
controls are all locked. It is drawn on Ask Crewlet's refusal of a question and
on a turn a budget stopped, on a refused act (the palette's knowledge answer
among them), on the Inbox's company budget condition, and on Home's spent week.

## Account: the reader's own page

`#/account` is the signed-in reader's own page, opened from **the menu their own
name opens** in the sidebar's user block, from the **Your account** card on their
own seat's page and peek, from the palette or with `g u`. It has **no sidebar
row**: the user block already is the reader. **Every way a person looks for their
own security leads here**, since the name opens the seat, the seat says nothing
of a password, and Settings is all locks to a reader holding only their own
account. **Every read and write on it names the caller and nobody else**
(`GET /auth/session` for who this browser is, the self arm of `/iam/people/{id}`
and its sessions, `GET /iam/credentials` and a token's mint and revocation with
no `?person=`), so the page holds no id it could be talked into swapping.

- **Profile**: login, name, address, seat and **Access** (the People list's
  words: Admin, the apps they hold, or Overview only), read-only, at the card's
  own inset, with "Only an admin can change these." (an admin is linked to their
  own row in People): a person changing their own would be the escalation the
  directory exists to close. A sealed value reads *Locked*, never blank. The seat
  is badge and name then `@handle`, the handle alone where the chart cannot be
  read; it links to the seat's page for every reader but one the engine refused
  the company (a seat taken out of the chart), for whom that page is the panel
  refusing them.
- **Security**: a line each, gesture beside it, in the order a person checks
  them: **Two-step verification**, then, beside an app, **Recovery codes**, then
  **Password**, whose **Change password…** opens a dialog like the
  authenticator's setup (a form in place is four fields tall and pushes the
  second factor below the fold at 1280×720 and on a phone). Each line says what
  is true now (the Password's when last set: its credential's own instant); what
  a change does is said in the dialog. Each line is two tracks, words wrapping
  beside the gesture; a wrapping row sized the words to their one line, so at 390
  the longer sentence dropped its button under it while a shorter kept it
  beside.
  - **Change password** takes the current one, a **Code** (for somebody holding a
    second factor: the app's current code or a recovery code, as at the sign-in)
    and the new one typed twice against the floor `/auth/config` names. Password
    and code are the proof, a step-up's taken in the one request, so no step-up is
    asked. The Code field is drawn when the credential list says a factor is
    held, and once the engine answers `second_factor_required` for a list that
    was behind; never for somebody holding none.
  - The change ends every other session and every personal access token the
    person holds and keeps this browser signed in, which the page says. A `202`
    (this node has not applied it yet) ended this browser's session too and
    cleared its cookie, so the tab goes straight to the sign-in with a toast
    saying the password changed and to sign in with the new one; the page reads
    nothing more, every read being refused.
  - A wrong current password or code is the sign-in surface's one refusal, about
    what was typed, and never sends the person to sign in: the engine names a
    wrong current password itself, and a refusal naming no field after a code was
    sent reads as the step-up dialog reads it ("That password or code was not
    accepted"), the code cleared.
  - **Two-step verification** sets up or replaces the authenticator app. The seed
    is drawn as `#/enrol` draws it (QR code with key and link beside it);
    **Confirm** stands beside **Cancel** in the dialog's footer, as every
    dialog's gestures do (`#/enrol`'s page keeps Confirm under its steps, the page
    being the form). A first app issues a first set of recovery codes, shown
    once, as `#/enrol` does, with **I've saved them** in the footer; a
    replacement keeps the set held. **Create new codes** issues a set, offered
    only beside an app, because recovery codes held alone are a second factor of
    their own, which the engine refuses to issue.
- **Where you are signed in**: live sessions, each led by its device ("Firefox on
  macOS", from the session's `user_agent`) over the address it signed in from
  (`remote`), with **This browser** marked by the lineage `/auth/session` names;
  any other is signed out by name (`POST /auth/logout/{lineage}`), and **Sign out
  everywhere** asks first (here and in the user menu, which closes to ask),
  saying it ends every personal access token too. It stands in the card's body
  beside that sentence, not in the header, where on a phone it cuts the title.
  Every gesture reads `/auth/session` again (the frame's read, through its
  reload) before the lists, because a gesture the engine asked a step-up for
  replaces this browser's session under a new lineage, and a mark read before it
  would offer this browser a named sign-out.
- **Personal access tokens**: tokens acting as the reader, each with what it
  carries and when it expires, **Revoke** on a live one, and **New token**: a
  label, a lifetime (empty takes the engine's default) and grants out of the
  reader's own, the value shown once with the sentence that it acts as them. The
  same dialog Settings › Service accounts mints a service account's token with
  (`components/people.tsx`), minting with no `?person=`.

A session exchanged from a Tier A token is the deployment's credential, not a
person: the page names it (*signed in with this deployment's API token `ops`*)
with its grants and draws none of the sections above, each of which the engine
would refuse. Its note says it has no password, second factor, sessions or
tokens and that its session ends within the hour; the person's note, promising
those, is never drawn for it.
## Settings: the frame, people, secrets, nodes and configuration

Settings is what the ENGINE runs and the company-wide basics it runs on. It is
the one workspace that draws its sections as a **column** beside the screen, not
as page-bar tabs, in five groups:

- **Company**: General, the landing (the company's clock, which every day, week
  and zoneless schedule is cut on).
- **Runtime**: Models, MCP Tools, Secrets and Limits.
- **Spend**: Token spend and Expensive tasks, readings never ceilings. The row is
  not called Spend: without Worklet it is the group's only row and read "Spend ›
  Spend".
- **Access**: People, Service accounts, API tokens, Sign-in policy, Delegated
  decisions and Audit log.
- **Engine**: Nodes, Configuration, Backups & retention and File storage.

**It lists only what lives in it.** A place that moved to Company (the charter,
policies, Integrations, Budgets) is found there, by the sidebar and palette,
never as a second row here. The reader's Account is the user block's and how this
browser looks is the preferences popover's, so the column has no group of the
reader's own and no row that leaves Settings. Every row's title is its hint, the
words the palette shows under it.

**The column stands beside the section only where the window holds both**
(`SECTION_COLUMN_MIN`, 1210px: sidebar, sheet, column and a 720px section floor,
in `app/layout.ts`); below that it folds to the one-row picker the phone draws,
naming the current section, and the section takes the full width (at 1024 a
beside column left a 489px section with 46px table columns).

A section closed to the reader draws a lock naming what it lacks and **is never
hidden**: a vanished section is one the reader cannot know exists. Closed is one
rule, `sectionOpen`, which the sidebar locks a row by (only when nothing in its
workspace is open, so Settings never, since Spend always is) and the frame draws
a section's refusal by:

- Token spend's readings and Models are open to everybody (each model's condition
  tells a member why a seat waits; every action stays an admin's).
- Expensive tasks is Worklet's.
- Delegated decisions names no grant: its read is an administrator's and the
  people a rule escalates to, whom no grant names.
- Every other section is admin's.

A section that reads a service the company does not run is not drawn, by the
sidebar's rule (Expensive tasks without Worklet). The landing, Models
(`#/settings/models`, where the sidebar's Settings row goes), is one of the
column's sections, so its trail reads **Settings › Models & Fleets**.

**On a phone the column folds to one row naming the section**, "Section ·
Models" (the word said: a bare name read as the page's title, not a control). It
opens the list and folds again once a section is picked, the current one
included (stacked whole it took ~520px, pushing content below the fold). A LINK
to a section arrives folded, the section right under the picker. The Settings
row's own address names no section anybody chose, so **arriving there opens the
list**, every group in it; a pick that lands on that address (Models) folds it.

**Beside a section the column stays put**: it is the scroller's height, so it
sticks while the section scrolls, its hairline runs the window's height, and a
list longer than a short window scrolls inside itself. On a phone the picker is
its own height and the section takes the rest. An address naming no screen is in
no section, so a mistyped one is never drawn beside a column claiming one.

**A section's name is its trail, not a heading over the section — the one place
the approved Settings artboard is deliberately not followed.** The artboard
repeats the name as a 24px heading above its lede, 36px in from the column. The
page bar's last crumb IS the page's `h1` (see `header/PageHeader` under
[The frame](#the-frame)), so a second heading gives two level-one headings, and a
screen's lede (`PageNote`) opens its body at the shared content padding, not an
inset of its own.

**The figures beside a section are the engine's, and absent is never zero.**

| Row | Figure | From |
|---|---|---|
| Nodes | nodes holding a presence lease ("1 node live"); a warning dot and "*n* behind on config" in the row's name when a node does not run the revision the fleet activated (older epoch, refusal or partial apply, another revision, or no apply reported; same count as the Nodes screen's "Behind on config", one rule: `lib/configStanding.ts`) | the health push, and `fleet` |
| Configuration | "epoch *n*": the epoch this node applied, in words | the health push |
| Backups & retention | how many alarms it draws stand (every kind but the model, MCP and Gitlet ones, which Models, MCP & tools and Gitlet draw), drawn only when one does | `retention` |

`fleet` and `retention` are admin's answers with no push, so those figures are a
poll, **asked only while the Settings column is on screen, and only of a reader
the section opens for** (`useSettingsSidebar`, at 30 s and 60 s) by `sectionOpen`,
so none is asked beside a lock. The frame outlives every screen, so an
unconditional hook would put two operator questions on a timer behind every
screen of every tab, and two refusals behind every non-admin. On Nodes the column
asks no `fleet` of its own: the screen hands the frame the reading it polls every
15 s (`usePublishFleet`), so the row's count and the screen's tile are one
reading, not two clocks disagreeing up to 30 s.

**The charter is Company's, not Settings'.** **Company › Principles**
(`#/company/principles`, the sidebar's **Principles** row and the Company landing
at `#/company`) is what every agent is told about the company, in the order an
agent reads it. Read from the org projection, every signed-in reader can open it.
Under its heading (the kit's `ObjectHeader`: *Who the company is and the rules
every agent works by.*) are three kit `Card`s, each a region named by its title
and headed by its glyph:

- **Mission** (a target) and **Vision** (a telescope): two equal cards side by
  side, neither outranking the other, each holding its statement as the kit's
  `passage` text. The mission is one line by the engine's rule and wraps as prose;
  the vision may hold paragraphs, kept as written. The pair shares its rows on a
  subgrid (equal heads and equal bodies). Below 720px of the page's own width they
  stack.
- **Standing policies** (a scroll of text): one card across the page, its count in
  the head once there is one, rules numbered (a reader cites "policy 2") in the
  kit's compact divided rows, each one line by the engine's rule, wrapping as
  prose at the kit's wide reading measure.
- **An unwritten part says so** in its card, as the kit's inline empty state
  saying what the part is for, with its own way to write it (**Add a mission**,
  **Add a vision**, **Add a policy**) for a reader who may write the charter. A
  written part has its own **Edit** in its card's head.
- **A reader who may not write the charter** sees no control at all: no Edit, no
  Add, no disabled copy (see
  [A write control is never hidden](#a-write-control-is-never-hidden)).
- **Engine limits** follows as a related row, for a reader who may open Settings ›
  Limits.

**Writing the charter happens on the page, one part at a time.** Edit (or Add)
opens that part in place as the kit's `InlineEditor`: the field, then a bar with
editing status, Cancel and Save. The other cards stay as they read and several
parts may be open at once. Each save is one configuration revision whose summary
names the part ("Changed the mission", "Standing policies: added 1, reordered"),
since a page mode saving three unrelated edits as one revision was declined. Source:
`dashboard/src/routes/settings/principles/edit/`.

- **Who may write it.** Admin, on a company document this deployment lets the
  reader's credential change (the viewer's `config_writer`, ADR-0030):
  `useMayWriteCharter`, which the org builder's company node also asks. Anybody
  else gets no control. An admin on a document another system manages is told so
  above the cards instead of finding no Edit. Offline or while the browser is
  still being identified, the controls stay, held with the reason.
- **The fields.** The mission and each policy are one line, because each is
  inlined in every seat's prompt (a policy as one list item); a long one wraps so
  it is read whole while written (the kit's `singleLine` textarea: no line break,
  a pasted one folds to a space). The vision is paragraphs. Each statement and
  policy shows its count as it nears its bound, in characters as the engine counts
  (1024 mission and policy, 2048 vision, 25 policies, from `contract/config.ts`).
  Policies are the kit's `ListInput`: edited in place, added with Enter, moved by
  a grip, by `Alt` with an arrow or by buttons, removed with an Undo where the
  policy was. A policy typed in the new box and not yet added counts as a change
  and is saved; a blank row is dropped. A repeated policy is said under its later
  copy; Save waits while any problem stands. Only what the person changed is held
  to the rules, as the engine holds a write: a policy or statement stored before
  the rules and left alone is a warning above the bar (*Saved before the current
  rules*) and never holds Save.
- **Saving.** The editor starts from the engine's own charter
  (`GET /config/charter`), not the page's possibly lagging copy. Save reads it
  again and writes it with only this part replaced, conditional on its tag
  (`PUT /config/charter`, `If-Match`), so a colleague's change to another part is
  kept. The card then shows the saved words until this browser's chart carries
  them, with *Saved. This page shows it as soon as this node applies the new
  revision.* under them, and a toast says it saved. The answer names the stored
  revision beside its epoch, and the card follows this node's standing on it
  (`lib/nodeStanding.ts`): once this node refused it, the card draws the part as
  this node still runs it, with *Saved, but this node refused the new revision and
  goes on running the one before. Settings › Nodes says why.*, until a later
  revision settles it; once it applied the revision, or passed it for a later one,
  the card draws the chart. It reads this node's last push
  (`lib/useLastHealth.ts`), so a dropped socket leaves a refusal said. A refusal
  keeps the draft and says why once, beside the Save (the editor's own alert, no
  toast); a save that got no answer is settled by reading the charter back, never
  sent twice.
- **A colleague's change to the same part** is never written over unseen. The card
  says the part changed, shows what changed line by line (the kit's `ConflictNote`
  over a [diff](#every-diff-is-tinted)), keeps the draft, and offers **Keep my
  draft** (save over theirs knowingly) or **Use theirs**.
- **Unsaved writing is never lost to a stray key.** Cancel or `Esc` on a part with
  changes asks first (*Discard your changes?*), as does a move to another page
  (*Leave without saving?*) and a reload or closed tab. Focus goes into the field
  as a part opens and back to its Edit (or Add) when it closes.

The company's name and clock are not principles and not on the page: the name is
the shell's, the clock the company document's.

The caps the engine holds a turn to are not policies for agents to read: they are
**Settings › Limits** (`#/settings/limits`), in Runtime, the engine's own answer
for each (the turn's guardrails, delegation, notifications and a scheduled turn's
timeout; a ceiling a cap is refused above, such as the most turns a worker may
ask for, is a row beside it, so a refusal names a value the page shows and
changes). Each group is a card holding the kit's `SettingsTable` (as Sign-in
policy's): the cap's name with the control that copies its key, the value in
tabular figures, and its source: *Default* as a quiet word where the value is the
engine's, a marked *Changed from* the default otherwise, *Off* rather than 0
where a value switches its limit off (the answer's `off` and `default_off`).
Every cap the document carries (the answer's `settable`: all but a scheduled
turn's timeout, the engine's constant each schedule sets itself) has a pencil
beside its value, drawn for every reader and disabled with the reason for one who
cannot write the document. It opens a field in a popover: the typed value is read
only as far as its unit (whole number, seconds, percentage), the engine checks it
against the whole company (`PATCH /config?dry_run=true` under the read's
revision) and refuses one it cannot run in its own words, a warning asks for a
second press, and the save carries a summary naming the cap. An emptied field is
the default, which removes the key rather than writing today's default. The saved
value is drawn marked *applying…* until this node applied the revision and the
answer carries it. Limits is admin's; Principles offers it as a related row to a
reader who may open it.

**A setting is changed where it is read, by one editor.** Every company-document
value a page draws as a row is the engine's own row of it, never the document
beside a copy of a default: a number is a `limits` row (`queries.LimitRow`, with
the range its validator holds it to), any other value a `settings` row
(`queries.SettingRow`: text, a time zone, a space key, a list of space keys or a
switch, with its default and whether the document sets it). Both are drawn and
changed by `SettingEditor` on the kit's `SettingsTable` (DataGrid's anatomy:
column heads, row height, hairlines, hover, under a card head with icon and
count): name, key, value, source, and at the row's end a pencil opening the kit's
one-setting panel (`SettingForm`), whose Save reads the document, checks the
change (`PATCH /config?dry_run=true`), stops on any new warning with **Save
anyway**, saves, and draws the value as applying until this node applies it.

- **Fields.** Number: the kit's `NumberField` (steppers held to its range, the
  range said under it as "1 to 10"); duration: `DurationField` (amount and unit
  picker, common durations as chips); share: a percentage with common shares;
  choice: a segmented row or select; text: a field. Each shows its default as
  placeholder and a **Default** chip or option, never a sentence.
- **Reset to default**, beside the pencil on a value that differs from its
  default, asks inline first ("Reset to 3?") then saves the default on the same
  checked path, opening the panel where the engine warns or refuses.
- **Ranges.** A number is held to its range as typed (a range may admit 0 apart
  from its scale, as Chatlet's message horizon: 0 keeps messages for ever, 1 to
  29 days is refused beside the field); no other kind copies a rule, and a
  refusal is the engine's, in the words its rule wrote for a person.
- **Defaults.** Going back to the default removes the key; an Off a setting has of
  its own (`knowledge.skills_container: ""`) is a value written. A number's source
  names the default it replaced (*Changed from 30 days*); any other kind's says
  *Changed* alone (its default can be long text), its field naming the default.
- **The held pencil** is drawn for every reader, held with the reason for one who
  cannot change the document; the reason is the kit tooltip's, opened by hover,
  keyboard focus and a press, so touch readers are told. A reader the `limits` or
  `settings` row is not served to (an administrator's answers) still gets the row
  with its held pencil, its value from the page's own answer where it has one.

The places: Settings › Limits; Delegated decisions; Settings › Gitlet (scratch
policy, identity domain); Worklet's, Doclet's and Chatlet's Settings under
Integrations (the inbox horizon; the company pages space, tool skills space,
search reach and search by meaning; the message horizon); Atlas › Sources (the
read interval); and Settings › General's **Company clock** (`timezone`, whose
change the engine's check warns moves every budget window and every schedule
without a zone of its own). A budget ceiling's pencil on Company › Budgets opens
the same panel.

**The brand is Company's too, and published.** **Company › Brand**
(`#/company/brand`) is how the company looks and sounds in everything its agents
make. A brand KIT is an artifact of kind `brand` (its `brand.json` and the logo
and font files it names), versioned like any artifact, which agents and editors
may draft; the company's brand is the one version an administrator PUBLISHED
(`brand{}`; an adoption in the engine's word, kept by `POST /brand/adoptions` and
`artifacts.brand.adopt`, while every label a person reads says publish), which
the engine snapshots and serves by its bytes. The page draws that adoption as
four cards in the Principles card grammar:

- Logos (`image`): name and tagline over three `LogoSlot`s (primary on a light
  ground, one for dark grounds, the square mark), each with a download.
- Colours (`blend`): each set role as a `ColorSwatch` with its value to copy, and
  a `ContrastBadge` per pair the adoption measures.
- Typography (`type`): heading and body faces as `TypeSpecimen`s, drawn in
  themselves.
- Voice and tone (`text-quote`).

Beside them is a sticky preview (`BrandSample`, a doc or a slide, light or dark)
in an `AsideLayout` that stacks it under the cards on a narrow page. An
administrator edits one card at a time in place, the preview drawing every
change; Save opens one dialog listing what changes (each colour with both values,
each logo by its bytes), the contrast pairs that fall short and what publishing
makes public (**Save and publish**), then publishes a version of the company's
kit and adopts it, the engine asking for a recent sign-in when proof is stale.
Text on the light ground below 4.5:1 holds Save with the engine's reason; every
other pair warns.

With no brand published, an administrator is offered **Set up your brand**, which
opens the setup on its own page (`#/company/brand/setup`, six steps, each
Continue saving a draft); everyone else reads "No brand yet". A draft nobody
published (one a setup left, or a version an agent or editor published on the
published kit) is offered under the header in a notice saying it is not live
("This draft of the Acme brand is not published yet, so artifacts still use
Crewlet's look.", or "Version 9 of the Acme brand is a draft. Artifacts keep
using the published version 7 until this one is published."), with who last
changed it and when (its version's author and day), and ONE primary action chosen
by readiness:

- **Publish brand** for an administrator once ready (the review of that version,
  then "Publish version 9 as the Acme brand?"), with **Edit draft** beside it.
- **Finish draft** while it lacks a primary logo or colour, beside the sentence
  "Not ready to publish: add a primary logo and colour"; never offered for
  publishing.
- An editor who may not publish reads that an administrator can review and
  publish it.

With none published, the draft itself is drawn under the notice in the four
cards, read-only, its preview tagged **Draft**, in place of "No brand yet". Its
owner or an administrator may **Discard draft**, which confirms and moves the kit
to the trash (`DELETE /artifacts/{id}`, `artifacts.trash`), restorable by its
owner until purged; a newer version of the published kit is a version, not a kit,
never offered for discarding. The engine publishes a draft lacking a primary logo
or colour as a version and refuses only to adopt it. **Run setup again** in the
bar walks every part again, prefilled from the kit. The bar holds the kit's
**History** and **Stop using this brand**.

The brand meets people where they make things: the Make row's `BrandChip` (or
**Set up your brand** for an administrator), the company's theme first in a new
deck's picker, a note under Ask an agent, and a **Brand** fact in an artifact's
Details (current, an older brand that changes at the next publish, or Crewlet's
look; a deck copies the brand when made and never follows it, saying "Made with
the Acme brand of" the day it was made). A kit's own page draws the same cards and
preview for the version on show, says whether it is the published one, and offers
an administrator **Publish this version**.

**Access** is the identity directory, over the routes `/iam` serves to an admin,
split over three pages so no row is drawn twice: People, Service accounts and API
tokens.

**People** (`#/settings/people`) is every principal but service accounts
(`/iam/people`): name with the login under it, kind, stage, **Access** column and
the seat the directory binds them to. The Access column uses the one line the
dashboard says everywhere (`accessLine` in `lib/access.ts`): **Admin** for
anybody holding it (every app is included); otherwise the apps they hold,
**Worklet · Doclet**; **Overview only** for none; and a name this build does not
know appended raw, never dropped. A row opens that person in the frame's
**peek** (`peek=person:{id}`), which reads their row (`/iam/people/{id}`),
credentials (`/iam/credentials`) and sessions itself: beside the list on a wide
window, a drawer on a phone, stepped with `[` and `]`, closed by Back.

- **The reader's own row leads with their Account**: "This is you" and a link,
  where their password, two-step verification, sessions and personal access
  tokens are managed. Their own sign-in gestures are not repeated (no reset link,
  two-step reset, Sign out everywhere or Revoke on their own credentials), and
  Suspend and Remove are held on their own row with the reason ("Another
  administrator can"). Edit stays, and says what a change to their own access
  would do to them.
- A sealed value this node's keyring cannot open reads *Locked*, never blank.
- A service account bound to none reads *No seat*, which is ordinary; a person
  always holds a human seat.
- The resting stage (*Active*) is quiet words; a stage that differs (*Invited*,
  *Suspended*) is a tag, so the row needing a look stands out.

**Service accounts** (`#/settings/service-accounts`) is the machine principals,
drawn as People draws a person and opened in the same peek, with how many act as
a seat in the card's head.

**Human seats**, on People, is every human seat of the running company with
whatever holds it (`/iam/seats`): a person or service account by login and stage,
an open invitation as an **Invited** tag with its address, or *Open seat*; and
where agents reach it (its contact identities, from the company document, admin's
like this screen). The tile above counts **Open seats** as seats held by NOTHING
(an open invitation holds its seat as surely as a person; counted as vacant it
read as a seat still invitable), with "*n* invited" beside the total.

**API tokens** (`#/settings/tokens`) is this node's Tier A labels joined to the
directory rows holding their logins (`/iam/node-tokens`). A token whose login
nobody holds acts as itself, unbound; the row says so in quiet words (*Not bound*,
the Seat column drawn only where a token is bound) and names the one command that
binds it, `crewlet iam create -kind machine -login token:<id> -seat <seat> -grants none`
(a row created on a human seat nothing else holds), since a label mistyped on
either side otherwise looks bound until the token presses something. When the
company document is [managed](../concepts/configuration.md#managed-configuration),
the card names its writers (each row says whether that token is one,
`company_writer`) and that only those tokens may change the company; nothing is
said when it is not managed.

The directory's own report (`/iam/check`), the **Needs attention** card (*All
good.* when empty), is drawn on the page of the principal each finding is about.
It names a company no active person can administer (`no_admin_holder`), somebody
active with no way in, a binding whose seat is gone and a row holding admin that
this node refuses (`admin_clamped_by_node`, on a node whose `api.auth.admin` is
`refuse`), in the engine's order, each kind in words keyed on the engine's list
(`FINDING_KINDS` in `contract/identity.ts`, held against `iamapi.FindingKinds`),
so a kind the engine grows is a compile error, not a raw code on screen. Each
finding is a sentence about the person it names ("Deploy pipeline has no token,
so it can’t sign in.") rather than the engine's detail, which names an API path;
a principal with no way in gets its fix beside it, **Create token** for a service
account and **Get reset link** for a person.

**Invitations**, on People, is every unredeemed, still-good invitation
(`/iam/invitations`): address, seat, access, who sent it, when it expires; **Show
used and expired** asks for every one the estate holds.

**Sign-in policy** (`#/settings/sign-in`) is how the company's people sign in
(`sign_in_policy`, an admin's; ADR-0152): whether a second factor is required,
the shortest password, how long a session lives from sign-in and unused, and how
long a step-up authorises a sensitive gesture. They are the company document's
`sign_in` block, the same on every node, each row with the Limits pencil
(`LimitSetting`, and `TextSetting`'s switch for the second factor), so a change
is checked, confirmed where it warns and applied without a restart.

- A duration is typed as one: seconds, or `30m`, `12h`, `7d`.
- Each row's range is narrowed to the limits the answering node's operator set in
  its own file (`api.auth.limits`); a value past one is refused beside the field,
  saying it is the operator's.
- A weakening change (second factor dropped, lower floor, longer limit) is checked
  with the engine's warning saying what it allows, saved only on **Save anyway**.
- A value the node holds lower than the company's is said in a note under the
  cards, and the node's limits are drawn read-only in a card of their own, each
  from "Node configuration file".
- **Settings names that file one way** (`lib/nodeFile.ts`): "Node configuration
  file" in a source column and a page's note, never `crewlet.yaml` on one page and
  "the bootstrap file" on the next.
- A setting's key (`sign_in.step_up_seconds`, `api.auth.limits.max_step_up`) is
  behind the table's copy control, not drawn under its name.

**Delegated decisions** (`#/settings/delegated-decisions`) is what agent seats
decide in a person's place ([Delegated decisions](../guides/delegated-decisions.md),
ADR-0125), read whole off `delegated_decisions`: whether delegation is on, and
each rule as one numbered row of the kit's `List` (`numbered-divided`, numbered
as the engine numbers it, since an escalation names "rule 2") reading as a
sentence: its kinds in words (Server commands, Merges, Deploys) → who decides
("Release Manager decides", or a panel's two "decide together"), who it escalates
to, how often its decisions are reviewed ("Reviews 1 in 10"), and for a merge or
deploy rule its checks (`required_checks`, each entry's repository and branch as
inline code and its check names, the first two and a count of the rest, every
entry on hover; "what each branch requires" where it names none) and the paths it
always sends to people (`always_escalate_paths`, the first three and a count of
the rest, the whole list on hover). Every seat is named with its face before its
name (`InlineRef` with a `SeatAvatar`), its handle on hover. With no rules the
card says people decide every request.

The limits the engine holds every delegate to, the deadline and the two hourly
caps, are a settings table whose rows are the Limits row (`LimitSetting`): each
value beside the engine's default, and a pencil changing its `delegated_decisions`
key within the engine's range, so none can be switched off. The rules card's head
holds a switch turning delegation on or off and **Add a rule**; each rule's row
ends in a pencil and a bin; each is drawn for every reader and disabled with the
reason for one who cannot write the document. The pencil and Add a rule open a
side sheet filled from the company document as it is then (not the rules this
node applied, which may be older), in four groups:

- **What it decides**: kinds as checkboxes, each with a one-line meaning; a kind
  another rule decides is held with that rule's number.
- **Who decides**: the agent, or two for a panel.
- **Who hears about it**: the people it escalates to, and **Spot-checks**: every
  decision, 1 in 5, 1 in 10 or 1 in 50, or a custom number within the engine's
  range, with a line saying what the choice means; the engine's default is
  written as no value.
- **Conditions**, merge or deploy rules only: required checks, one entry per
  repository and branch, each picked from the company's GitHub repositories
  (`delegated_repositories`), that repository's branches (`delegated_branches`,
  default branch filled in) and the check names on the branch's newest commit
  (`delegated_checks`), typing the fallback for anything the lists do not show;
  and the paths it always sends to people.

Both seat pickers are the kit's `TagsInput`, each option and chip drawing the
seat's face, name and handle. A rule missing a kind, an agent or a person is held
under that field before anything is sent; Save then checks the whole rules list
against the company, each engine problem shown under the field it names in the
engine's words for a person (`said`), the callout pointing there; a rule changed
since the sheet was filled is a conflict to reload, never written over. The bin
asks first, saying the rules after it move up one. All three are one write of the
card (a change is the whole `rules` list, which a merge patch replaces), and
*Saved, applying…* beside the switch says it until this node applied it.

Under them one toolbar (a search over seat, request, server and reason; a verdict
and who gave it, each the kit's `Select`; the day the digest covers, back a
company day at a time, forward no further than today) narrows three grids:
**Decided today, so far** (the running day, `day=today`, which the page opens on
and asks again every minute, its subtitle saying the day is still running), or
**Decided on** the day `day=` names, then **Spot-checks** and **Flagged denials**,
the last two over the week before now. Each row is the requesting seat, what was
decided and where (a merge or deploy names no server, and says so), the verdict in
its state's tone, why the engine changed or made it on hover (each closed word as
a phrase), who gave it under which rule (Crewlet for the engine's own), and the
giver's reason; each grid's foot says "Showing N of M" and whether the log held
more than its page. The read admits an administrator and the people a rule
escalates to, so the row names no grant and anybody else is shown the engine's
refusal. Home draws two notices off the same read for those people, above the
board: "Delegates decided N requests yesterday", put away for its company day and
linking here at that day (`day=`), and "A delegate flagged N requests as harmful",
put away until a newer flag and linking here (`DelegatedNotices`). Home's digest
stays about the last whole day.

**An admin writes the directory from here** (see
[A write control is never hidden](#a-write-control-is-never-hidden) for why the
directory's writes are drawn for an admin alone). A person holds exactly one human
seat from the moment they exist, so a person still comes from the vacant seat they
will hold: **Invite** and **Add person** are on that seat's panel and page in
Company › Structure, and in the Person section of its editor
([Structure is the company running](#structure-is-the-company-running)). People's
primary action, **Invite person**, picks an open seat (one nothing holds,
`?unheld=true`) and opens that seat's own invitation; **Identity trail** and
**Open Structure** sit in its bar's overflow menu. **New service account** is the
primary action of Service accounts. What they write:

- **New service account**: a machine with a login in the colon grammar
  (`ci:release`, checked under the field before anything is posted), a name, its
  access (the picker opens with nothing ticked, since what a scripted credential
  needs is the script's business; Admin may be ticked, a service account being the
  one non-person that may hold it) and an optional **Seat**: a human seat nothing
  holds, for an account that should act as that seat (a deploy pipeline acting as
  its owner's), sent in the same record as the account, since created bare and
  bound after, a pipeline meant to act as a seat acted as itself until a second
  write landed; with **No seat** it acts as itself, under its own login. Then
  **Mint its token**: a label, a lifetime and access out of the account's own,
  opened with all of it ticked that the reader holds too, Admin included (a token
  may carry admin; what keeps it off gestures needing a person present are the
  authority table's two locks, not the picker); one the reader does not hold is
  unticked and disabled, since the engine refuses a token carrying what its minter
  does not hold. The value is shown once.
- **Cancel** on an unredeemed invitation: its link stops working at once and the
  address and seat it names are free again; the same dialog the seat's own
  **Cancel invitation** opens.
- In an **opened person's peek**:
  - **Edit**: one `PATCH` carrying only what changed since the dialog opened,
    measured against that row, not the directory's minute-by-minute re-read, so a
    login or seat left alone never puts back what another administrator changed
    meanwhile. Access goes as what was ticked and unticked, `add_grants` and
    `remove_grants`, which the engine applies to what the person holds when it
    decides, so a permission left alone stays as another administrator left it.
    The picker is the invitation's (Admin one switch that ticks and locks the apps,
    a note under it saying what an unticked app costs). The seat is offered among
    the vacant ones and their own, with **No seat** for a service account only: a
    person's seat is MOVED, never cleared, since the engine refuses a person's edit
    that clears it (`seat_required`), and removing them is what frees it; a person
    recorded with no seat starts on **Choose a seat** with a warning, and the edit
    sends a seat only once one is chosen, so an unrelated change is never refused
    for it. A permission the person already holds may be unticked whoever edits,
    since the engine checks only what an edit adds, while one neither holds stays
    disabled; a name this build does not know, kept on the row, is offered as a
    ticked box of its own, which unticking removes and nothing can add.
  - **Suspend** / **Reactivate**: which of the two is fixed when the dialog opens,
    so its **Try again** after an unknown answer sends the same stage even once the
    re-read shows it landed; a suspension says the person's seat, by name, is
    withheld and stays theirs, so nobody else is put on it meanwhile.
  - Those two stay in view; the rest sit under **More**: for a person **Get reset
    link** (shown once; the outstanding link is listed among their credentials,
    tagged *Not used yet* until opened), **Reset two-step verification** (when they
    hold one) and **Sign out everywhere** or, for a machine, **Create token**, and
    last and set apart **Remove**, confirmed by typing their login, since it cannot
    be undone, which closes the peek once it lands and says who was removed. A
    removal says it frees the seat, by name, which then stands vacant in the org
    chart, and that a person comes back by being invited onto a seat again, a
    service account by being created again (nobody redeems an invitation for one).
    Each credential row has **Revoke**.
  - **Suspend**, **Reset two-step verification** and **Sign out everywhere** each
    say that an outstanding password reset link ends with the sessions,
    **Reactivate** that it stays ended, and **Get reset link** that it is issued
    after those (a link sent first is dead when opened).
  - On the reader's OWN row (the person `GET /auth/session` names, by id) every
    gesture that ends their sessions says first that it is them and signs this
    browser out at once, and speaks to them throughout, title and body alike ("You
    may not act while suspended"). **Suspend** and **Remove** add, where `GET
/iam/check` counts nobody else active holding admin (`people_with_admin`), that
    afterwards only this node's API token could administer people. **Edit** speaks
    to them too, and an edit unticking their own Admin says it is them, that they
    stop administering the company once it saves, and the same sentence where
    nobody else would be left: a WARNING, never a block, since the engine refuses
    no one taking away a permission, the last administrator's own included, and
    Tier A's token is the way back in.

Every one of these — and a seat's **Invite**, **Add person** and **Cancel
invitation** — is one `/iam` write (`lib/iamWrite.ts`): a `403
step_up_required` opens the step-up dialog and the same request is replayed; a
create — a service account's or a person's — carries a fresh uuid7
`Idempotency-Key`, kept for the retry an unknown answer asks for — **Try
again** sends the key the engine handed back, so it lands once, and a
person's create hands back the same first password link — and a request
changed before it is pressed is a new one under a new key, since a create's
key sent with another body is refused as reused — while a token's mint and a
reset link read no key and a retry issues another; a refusal is the engine's
sentence with the access that would admit; a `202` says the change is
recorded and this node is catching up, and — like a stale refusal — leaves
the dialog only **Done**, because the gesture is over and pressing it again
would send it again; and after every answer — a refusal part way and an
unknown one included, since either may have changed something — the lists the
write touches are read again, every seat listing on the page among them. Where
`/health` says `identity: unclaimed`, a callout says nobody has joined yet and
what comes next — drawn once the invitations and the human seats have both
answered or been refused, so it never names one step and then another: with
an invitation open, that its link is where its person chooses a login and
password — naming the address where there is one invitation — and that a
lost link is cancelled here or on its seat and issued again from the seat; on
a node running no company (the seat listing's `409 no_active_revision`), that
there is no seat yet and the company comes first, with **Create the company**
(`#/company/org`) and `crewlet config import` beside it, while the Human seats
card says the same in a sentence rather than as a failed read; in a company
with no human seat at all, that nobody can join until one is added, with
**Add a human seat** (`#/company/org?add=human`); otherwise **Open the org
chart** (Structure), where you choose your human seat and invite or create yourself on it
— and where the listing was refused for any other reason, the callout points
at the chart without claiming anything about its seats. A token is still
declared in Tier A (`api.auth.tokens`) and changes at a restart. **It never
reads a value back** — not a token's, not a password's, not a second factor's.

**Company › Integrations** (`#/company/integrations`) is **every reader's**, under Company because which services and apps the company runs are its decisions. It is a **directory beside a detail** (the kit's `DirectoryList` in a `ListDetail`): the list holds its place while the detail scrolls (above a phone's width the screen asks the frame for the window's height, as the Inbox does). On a phone it is one column: the list until something is chosen, then the detail with a way back.

The directory is **every integration by category**, Crewlet's own services first in each:

| Category | Lines |
|---|---|
| Chat | Chatlet, Slack, Mattermost |
| Work tracking | Worklet, Jira |
| Docs and knowledge | Doclet, Confluence |
| Code | Gitlet, GitHub, GitLab |
| Observability | Datadog |
| Cloud and Infrastructure | AWS, Cloudflare, DigitalOcean, Google Cloud, Scaleway, SSH |
| Mobile apps | Expo, App Store Connect, Google Play |
| Advertising | Google Ads, Meta Ads, Apple Ads |
| Analytics | Google Analytics, Search Console |
| Ad revenue | AdSense, AdMob |

**The growth products are filed by what they do**, ahead of their catalogue entries: a line whose app this build does not serve yet is drawn nowhere, and a category left with no line is not drawn at all, so the product that lands needs no change to the table (`categories.ts`, `shownDirectory`). Where one name covers them all (the growth tools' group and the levels an agent holds on any of them) it is **Growth**, with the levels **View**, **Manage** and **Administer**, by what each lets an agent do.

**Atlassian is listed by product**: Jira under work tracking, Confluence under docs, each with its own state, both opening the one Atlassian page (one key and one account per agent). A line stands at the rail's row step (30px) with its mark, its name (a product's vendor inline after it, in the quiet ink: Atlassian after Jira and Confluence, Crewlet after Worklet, Doclet, Chatlet and Gitlet) and a state only where it has one: **In use** or **Not in use** for a service (never *connected*; none on a node running no company, which is "not known yet"), and for an app the engine's bucket (*Connected*, *Needs attention*, *Setting up*), never *Not connected*.

**The home** (the bare address) is **what the company has in use**, under one fixed description, the same for every reader and never a count (*The tools your agents work with: Crewlet's own services and the apps your company connects for them.*). Then:

1. What needs a look: each issue under its app's name, linking to the app's page with the fix's form already open; or one line saying all is well.
2. **In use**, with a quiet count of every card beneath (`home.ts`): connected apps (Jira and Confluence as their own products) and Crewlet services in use, each a **compact card** (the kit's `CatalogTile` at `density` `compact`: mark, name, state and a figure on one line, the one action at its end, one line of what it gives), two to a row. The action is named for its card to a screen reader (`actionName` in `parts.tsx`: "Open Worklet", "Replace key GitLab"). For an Admin while only Crewlet's services are in use, one line says apps connected from the list show there too.
3. Recent activity (latest deliveries, each app's last check).
4. The **address apps deliver to**, once at the foot, cut to fit with the whole in its title, copied with a press.

Services not in use and apps nobody connected are the list's alone; a home with nothing in use says so and points at the list. A connected app's figure is its agents (*x of y agents ready*) where it gives each agent an account, else its newest delivery. Sections stand one small step apart (the kit's `Section` at `spacing` `tight`).

**The address is the selection**: `#/company/integrations/{kind}` selects an app's key, a surface (`jira`, `confluence`; the `forge` relay and `atlassian` select Jira's line) or a service (`worklet`, `doclet`, `chat`), so any surface's address lands on its tool. An arrival's `open=` names the form to open (`connect`, `continue`, `rotate`, `settings`, `agents`); it is taken out of the address once read and held for the selection it arrived with, so a fix from the home opens its form on an already-mounted page and leaving for another selection drops it.

**An app's page** is its header (the kit's `ObjectHeader`: the vendor's mark, the engine's word for its state, a one-line description, and facts: agents ready and the deliveries this node counted, only when `traffic_known`, and the last check with when the next is due as its note) and three tabs:

- **Agents**, opened first: above the agents, the issues, each a row with what is wrong, its subjects as chips (a long list folded to a count that expands in place), what to do, **who owes the next move** (*Waiting on you*, *Crewlet is on it*, *The app is on it*) and the one control that answers it. It holds the reconcile loop's findings in the engine's words and the facts a surface's row states (a secret that did not resolve, an address that moved, deliveries that reach no agent, a pass that failed with nothing to show), each once. A working tool says so; an advisory (an access wider than asked) is a note, never an issue.
  Then each agent with its standing, its tier where the app grades one (the engine's words, beside the name, weighted by trust only on a scale the engine names), what it reaches (an app by its name, its IDs on hover), and its own step at the app (*Create app on GitHub*, *Install on GitHub*); an agent that is off reads a dash ("None while off") for its access, scope and grants. Where a product could not read what its connections reach, why is said once above the agents and in the chooser. **Check now**, which asks the reconcile loop to look at the tool at once (`POST /setup/integrations/{kind}/check`).
- **Activity**: provisioning passes and each surface's deliveries.
- **Settings**: what the tool is set to, a credential named and never shown. Its sections are the kit's `Section`, headed at the small step inside the tab. A marketing, growth or app store product adds its **Connections** (who Crewlet is at the vendor through each, the roles it holds there, and every account each reaches; a lone connection the vendor gives no name is not headed by its document key, and a lone App Store Connect team, whose issuer the settings above list, is titled **Apps** and lists only what it reaches with its currency, zone and state, drawn as a list that keeps each name whole and moves each ID to its own line rather than break it, breaking only one wider than a line; an App Store Connect team names no roles, since Crewlet holds no key there, and one no agent's key has listed yet reads *No app listed yet.* over the engine's reason; under Google Analytics' list, "Read from" and the Google Analytics logo at 50px, the white-text file on a dark theme, linked to Google Analytics), the vendor's **roles**, folded under *What each role allows* (each with what it allows at the vendor and what Crewlet offers a seat through it, the held ones marked), and for a spending product its **Spending caps**: per account, in the account's own currency, the most one change may add and the ceiling on the daily budgets after any change, both or neither and the first no higher than the second, typed as text and stored at the currency's own digits, a raise confirmed at a fresh sign-in. A stored currency that is missing or not the account's own stays editable in place, and a save over caps another admin changed since the form opened is reloaded, never written over. An administrator also reads the product's **Recent agent changes** there (`growth_changes`, the access log's growth records for that product, newest first; the newest page read again each minute and each older page once, on request, every record drawn once however many reads carried it, and a page this node could not read whole saying the list may be missing some): each step with its target, when, who answered a held act (by chart name) or why a failed one did not run, the account and the agent by its chart name, and each changed field before and after, money in the account's currency and published text by its size alone.

The header's one action is exactly one of four, decided by `actionFor` from the same inputs as the state:

| Action | When | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| **Connect** | nothing configured | opens the tool's settings form in the pane |
| **Finish setup** | a requirement unanswered, or a surface of a partly-connected tool not yet configured | opens the same form |
| **Replace key** | a `credential_expiring` or `credential_rejected` finding on a configured surface | opens the same form, headed *Replace the {tool} key*, with the engine's reason first |
| *(none)* | anything else, including a tool this build answers no form for | the page is the tool's management, or links its docs |

It sits beside **Settings** and **Disconnect** on a connected tool. **The settings form opens in the pane** in place of the tabs, directory still beside it; connecting, finishing setup and replacing a key never leave the page. A tool not yet connected shows, in place of the tabs, what connecting gives the agents, how each gets in, and what to have ready.

**The form's words are split by job**, each from the engine (`GET /setup/integrations`):

- The tool's one-sentence summary opens it.
- The one risk its credential carries, if any, is a warning callout above the first field.
- The steps to take at the app (numbered, vendor links where the engine placed them, permissions to grant as code) are its **Setup steps**: a neutral box in a sticky column beside the form (`AsideLayout`, `fit="pane"`), level with the integration's header, with Cancel and the submit under both columns. It is open while the integration is being connected and put away once it is; a person's choice holds for the page view. Put away, it is one **Setup steps** button at the column's top; open, a close button sits in its corner and Escape anywhere in it puts it away, focus returning to that button. Where the pane is narrower than the layout's pane split there is no column: a **Setup steps** button in the form's title row opens the same box in a side sheet, only when pressed.
- Each field has one hint line, under fifteen words; more sits behind a **More** disclosure. One renderer draws a field's words whatever the row is (an input, or the block a minted key's public half is copied from), so neither drops a link or note.
- A step that connects another integration first (`needs`) says beside it whether that one is connected; while it is not, a warning callout above the fields names it and links its page, so fields that cannot work yet do not look ready.
- A `redirect` row is the address the vendor sends a sign-in back to, the engine's own, copied whole with every word shown and the setting it is built on; with no public address it is a warning naming that setting.
- The form marks an optional field "(optional)" from `required`, a sign-in's included; a label never says it.

A credential the engine can check carries **Test key** under its field: one read-only call to the app (`POST /setup/integrations/{kind}/verify`). The answer (*works*, *refused*, *unreachable*, or not checked) is one sentence beside the control, its facts (what the key reaches, when it expires, the app's own words) as pairs on a line below, each risk or problem its own callout saying what to do; none behind a disclosure. It goes when the value is typed over. A credential the app proves only by using it says how, after its More. Credentials the app checks together (`check_with`, Datadog's API key and application key) share one **Test keys** control after the last: disabled, with an accessible reason naming the empty fields, until all hold a value; one verdict names the key that failed and goes when any is typed over. A check the engine turned away (a `${NAME}` naming no secret) says why and claims no verdict.

**Crewlet's own services** have pages laid out as an app's, filled only with what the engine answers.

- Worklet counts projects and their open tasks, lists the projects, every agent with open, blocked and overdue work, the newest changes, and the `tracker` block's settings.
- Doclet counts spaces and pages, lists the spaces, every agent's own space and onboarding pages, the newest edits, and the `knowledge` block's settings.
- An unset key reads *The engine's default*, not a copy of the constant.
- A service the company runs elsewhere says what does its work instead (*Jira does this for your company*, with the way to Jira's page), what running it here would give, and that the company document decides it. No on/off switch is offered: one that did nothing would be a lie.
- Chatlet counts nothing (the rooms are the reader's own seat's). In use, its page says what it gives and opens it to a reader holding Chatlet (others are told it needs Chatlet access). On a vendor's chat it says which (*Slack does this for your company*, named from the `viewer` answer, which tells it to a holder of Chatlet), with the way to that app's line.
- Gitlet counts nothing (which repositories a reader sees is their own grant's answer). In use, its page says what it gives, opens it to a reader holding Gitlet (others are told it needs Gitlet access), and offers an Admin **Gitlet settings**. Nothing runs in its place (repositories on GitHub or GitLab are integrations agents call), so with Gitlet off its page says *Crewlet hosts none of your company's code* and what running it here would give.

**A reader without Admin** sees the whole directory: services with their states and pages in full (each count read only where the reader holds that service's app), and apps with no state, each page saying an admin connects and manages apps (and offering sign-in to a reader who is nobody). Nothing asks a question the engine keeps for Admins: the `integrations` question, `/setup` and the `config` answer are read only for an Admin, and the address at the foot is the setup listing's, so it is not shown.

On a [managed document](../concepts/configuration.md#managed-configuration), for a credential that is not one of its writers, the page leads with a callout carrying the managed sentence, and **Connect**, **Finish setup**, **Disconnect** and an agent's **Create app on GitHub** are disabled (they write the document). **Replace key** and the settings form stay open: a rotation seals a value the document already names and changes nothing in it, the break-glass a managed deployment keeps for a person. The directory ends at the tools this build serves: every other tool an agent can reach is an MCP server, added on Settings › MCP & tools. See [integration reconcile](../concepts/integration-reconcile.md#what-the-dashboard-shows).

**MCP & tools** (`#/settings/mcp-tools`) is every MCP server the company runs and the tools the engine runs itself, read from `mcp_servers_status` and a server's `GET /mcp-servers/{name}`, which every member may ask. A member's reading names no launch line, header, failure sentence or call; every action is an admin's. It polls every fifteen seconds while open, and refreshes when this node applies a new configuration and when the engine's alarms move. The page decides nothing (a server's state, a tool's risk or level, a failure's class, an alarm's fix, who a server reaches, how many tools an agent holds): the engine answers and the page names it in its words (`words.ts`).

The header holds the title, one plain line, and **Add server** for an admin (opens the wizard below). Views are underline tabs (`?view=`): **Servers**, **Agent access** (an admin's) and **Built-in tools**.
