**Servers** leads, for an admin, with **Needs attention**: a row per server an MCP alarm stands on (`alarms[].entries[]`): its tone, mark, what is wrong in a line, its failure's class or the refused names, and the one fix the engine names in a quiet button:

- **Restart** (every instance, or the named agent's)
- **See its sign-in** (the server's Connection tab, where its integration's Agents tab is linked)
- **Change its prefix** (the wizard at its Connection step, where the tool prefix is)
- **Answer it** (the calls the server's tools hold for approval, `?flow=approve`, each answerable there)

The engine's measurement and remedy open under the row; past three rows the rest fold to a summary. A member reads *Read-only. Changes take Admin access.* instead.

Then four figures (three for a member): servers and how many are off, how many enabled ones run, MCP tools and how many are not offered, and for an admin **Waiting on you** (calls held for their answer and servers whose changed tools wait for a review). Then a row per server:

- mark, title and, for an admin, its host or command (whole on hover, any credential withheld by the engine), or for a member what it is for;
- **Connection** (*Remote* or *Local*, *Company-shared* or *Per agent*);
- **Status** (the engine's state, *n of m* for a partial one, *n agents* for a per-agent one running for several);
- **Tools** (how many it lists, how many are not offered);
- **Used by** (the first agent the engine grants it and *+n*, from the answer's `agents`, all on hover);
- **Last error** (the longest-down node's failure in its class's few words, the agent and when under it, the engine's sentence on hover for an admin);
- for an admin, a pencil that opens the wizard on the server (on hover or focus, always where there is no hover) and the server's menu: **Test**, **Edit**, **Restart**, **Disable** or **Enable**, **Remove**.

A row opens the **server's page** (`servers/{name}`): an object header (mark, title, name, state, connection on one line, tool count and reach), **Edit** beside the menu in the page bar for an admin (on a phone the menu folds into *More*), and five tabs (`?tab=`), **Access** an admin's.

- **Overview**: a disabled server is said off, with **Enable**. For an admin, each call the server's tools hold for approval (the Inbox's held-call row in a card, answered in place, the tab marked while one waits). Then the server's own alarms (a waiting call's alarm left to its row); each instance (the agent it runs for or *The company*, its node, state, tools or what is wrong in a few words, the class's title on hover); a line naming any node that did not answer the instance read; when it last answered; its last failure; for an admin its latest test (passed or failed, by whom, when) with **Test now**; what it reported itself as and its protocol; and for an admin the instructions it reports, said not to be the agents' (a seat's harness is handed the entry's `description`).
- **Connection**, for an admin: the address or command, transport, where it runs, instances, the start and call timeouts with which are the default, and its tool prefix (from the entry as written), with **Edit**, which opens the wizard's Connection step, where the timeouts are changed too (an empty one is the engine's default, `MCP_DEFAULT_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` and `MCP_DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`). Also how the engine signs in (and an integration's link to its Agents tab), and every header or variable it is sent, from the engine's `values`: its name and the `${VAR}` it reads (*Set in the configuration* for a value written there, *Each agent's own* for a key an integration fills), whether the store holds it, who stored it and when, **Replace** or **Set** for each key an integration does not fill, and **Edit**; never a value. A member's reading counts no agent's tools, so a member's list draws no **Used by** and a server's page no reach, rather than *No agent*.
- **Tools**: the names no agent is offered, with the engine's reason; for an admin the server's default level (*By each tool's hints*, or one of the three, with **Edit** opening the wizard's approvals step); then every tool the fleet lists with description, the engine's risk (*Read only*, *Writes*, *Destructive*, starred where the server declared nothing), calls over the week and level. An admin's level is a select of *Always allow*, *Needs approval* and *Blocked* (a tool with a level of its own marked *Custom*, with the way back to the server's default); a member's is in words. There is a search, the risk's chips, *Custom*, and for an admin **Set N shown**, which sets every tool shown. Each change is one `PUT /mcp-servers/{name}/tools`, by the server's own name for the tool.
- **Access**: what a team lead's `mcp_limits` hold the server to for each agent, as the engine resolved them (off for it, or tools held back, and by whose lead; the Tools tab marks such a tool *Held back*). For a server an integration signs in for, a note linking the integration's Agents tab; otherwise **Who gets it**: every agent or chosen teams and agents (each team listing every agent, an agent of a chosen team left out by unticking it), saved through the entity route with **Save access** once it differs. Then **What each agent can call**: every agent with why the engine says the server reaches it (`reaches`) or that it does not, and the tools it may call there.
- **Activity**: the week's calls per tool, every reader's; for an admin also the newest calls (when, agent, tool, how it ended, how long, never arguments or result) with any data node that did not answer, and calls held for approval with how each was answered while its run holds it.

Flows are the address (`?flow=test`, `value` with `key`, `restart`, `disable`, `remove`, `approve`, `drift`, with `server` and `seat`), so an alarm's fix and a menu item open one dialog.

- **Test** runs on open and on **Test again**, never otherwise, on every node that runs the server (a per-agent one as the first agent the engine grants it; another chosen in **Test as**). Each stage shows in the kit's step list with its time and what it found, stages never reached said so, a failed one giving its class's title and remedy. It never calls a tool.
- **Replace** (or **Set**) takes a new value write-only and sends it to the engine, which tests the server with it before sealing it and pointing the key at it. A value the server refuses is said on the field with what the test found, and stores nothing. Where no node answered the test, **Save untested** stores it anyway; a per-agent server's own value is stored untested, since it is tested as each agent. Both ask the engine's recent step-up, which the dashboard's one ceremony answers and replays.

**Adding and editing** is a wizard, a page of its own in the list's place (`?flow=add`, or `?flow=edit&server=` with `step=` for the step an action is about). Steps:

- **Source**: the curated catalogue (what the company already runs apart as *Added*); an address the engine checks before anything is added, saying what answers there, the sign-in it asks for and its tools; a pasted `mcpServers`, VS Code `servers` or registry `server.json`, read and never run, values left out; or a community search, sent when asked, each result marked *Not reviewed*.
- **Name**
- **Connection**: an address, or a command, its arguments and variables.
- **Sign-in**: the vendor's integration where the catalogue names one, a header, or none, with what the address check or catalogue found said above.
- **Who gets it**: one connection or one per agent, and the Access tab's grant picker.
- **Tool approvals**: the default level and each tool's, over the tools a test of the draft lists, each at the engine's starting level.
- **Test**: the draft as it would be written, without its levels, run as it opens and again on request.
- **Review**: who gets it, the tools at each level, a destructive tool left at Always allow pointed out, and the engine's dry run of the entry, its problems on the fields they name and the steps holding them marked.

An edit has no Source, keeps the server's name, opens at the step its action names and writes back every field of the entry it does not draw. A value typed in the wizard is never written into the entry: it is tested with the draft, sealed across the fleet, and stored write-only after the entry is written, each through the same route as **Replace**, which tests it with the entry as the fleet's active revision states it. A value the server refuses leaves the entry saved and the wizard open on what is left. Enter moves on from a single-line field, a choice or a step's heading.

**Remove** first asks the engine's dry run what names the server (an agent's or a team's `mcp_env`, a box's `sandbox.mcp.servers`) and which stored values nothing else reads. It holds **Remove server** until the reader clears those in the same change, offers each value to delete with it, and states the revision of the entry it read; **Disable instead** is beside it.

**Agent access** (`?view=agents`, an admin's) is the answer's `agents`: a row per agent, a column per server, each cell the tools the agent may call there, the server's state where it is not running, or a marked absence where it does not reach it. It shows the agent's total, with *Over 100* where the engine flags it (`over_budget`, against `tool_budget`); a callout naming every agent over the budget; and a note naming servers whose agents an integration decides. A row opens the agent's tools (`?agent=`): its total against the budget, every server it reaches with why and how many tools sit at each level, and how many built-in tools it is offered (`builtin_tools`). On a phone a row is the agent and its total. While the engine is still counting, the view says so rather than drawing zeros.

**A held call** (a run parked on a call to a tool at *Needs approval*) is one row wherever it waits on a person: the Inbox and Home as the run's decision, a server's Overview in a card. It shows the agent and work item on its head, its title, that its run is parked, and under it what the call would send under **Arguments**. THE TITLE IS IN PRODUCT WORDS, read from the call's own arguments where the reader is shown them: *Merge pull request 88 in acme/web?* (or *Merge change 42 in web?* for a Gitlet change), *Deploy web to production?*, *Run a command on web-1?*. A reader not shown those arguments, and any other call its tool asks about every time, reads the engine's own question, which that tool words; an MCP tool's call is *Call `tool` on Server?*. One function words it for the row, the Inbox's list and its pane (`heldCallTitle`); where the title is in product words, the call as made (tool and server) is the first line under **Arguments**.

**Allow once**, **Always allow** and **Deny** answer it through `POST /mcp-approvals/{id}`, never the run's own answer; Always allow asks the engine's recent step-up first. The row then says what the answer did and keeps that line until the list is drawn afresh; an answer whose delivery the engine could not confirm says answering again is safe and keeps its buttons. The live run's banner and a seat's page, where a parked run is answered with **Answer**, offer the run the same three answers instead.

**A call a delegate decides first** ([Delegated decisions](../guides/delegated-decisions.md)) waits on nobody's decisions until escalated: the live Executors board draws its status as **with delegate**, and its banner names the delegates and the rule ("With delegate Security Engineer (rule 1)") above the same answers, which a person who may approve it can still give. **An escalated call reads its delegates before the call itself**, in the Inbox's pane and on its row alike (`EscalationNote`), as one quiet callout (the kit's `Callout` at `appearance="quiet"`: the warning on its glyph and leading edge, words in the page's own ink).

- Its heading says who put it to people, under which rule and, where one delegate's answer is the escalation, how sure it was ("Escalated by Security Engineer (rule 1), low confidence", or Crewlet where no delegate escalated); that answer has no line repeating its name, verdict or confidence.
- A panel's answers, or one the engine overruled, each keep a line: the delegate, its verdict in its state's tone, its confidence.
- Under them: the delegate's reason and findings in the order given (the kit's `FindingList`, compact), then the engine's sentences under **Why it reached you**; the call and its answers follow unchanged.
- A delegate's words are a model's, so all are plain text.

**A held merge or deploy** (`ask_to_merge`, `ask_to_deploy`, `approvers: release`) is a fixed call, answered **Review and allow once** or **Deny**. For a reader the run's row sends its arguments to (an administrator, the agent's lead), the Inbox's pane draws it from them after the delegates' answers as a description list (`ReleaseRequestFacts`): a merge's **Change**, **Head**, **Method** and **Reason**; a deploy's **Repository**, **Commit**, **Changes**, **Environment**, **Rollback** and **Reason**. Every value the agent wrote is plain text kept to its lines, never Markdown, never a link (an address included); a commit is its short id in monospace, the whole id on hover and copied whole by the kit's `Copyable`. A caption says what Allow once does and who may answer: administrators, the agent's leads and the people its rule escalates to, at a recent sign-in. A reader sent no arguments (a person the rule escalates to) reads the engine's own words, as for a command, and the same caption. The review dialog (**Review the merge**, **Review the deploy**) and a decision row's **Arguments** draw the same list; arguments that do not read whole as the tool's (a key it does not take) are drawn as sent.
An answer a delegate gave carries **Decided under delegation, rule N**, off the `delegated_rule` its `executor_answered` and `executor_answer_given` record: on the turn's rows, the event log, the event's page and the executor's page.

**A changed tool** (`?flow=drift`, opened by the Tools tab's **Review** and the alarm's fix) is reviewed in a dialog over the detail's `changes`: the changed tools in the kit's rail (one that now claims less risk first and flagged; it folds into a picker only on a narrow window), and for the one chosen its title or description as a text diff, its arguments a line each and the hints that moved keyed by the hint, old word removed and new added, all in `DiffView` ([Every diff is tinted](#every-diff-is-tinted)). Actions are **Accept change**, **Accept the new tool** or **Accept that it went**, and **Keep blocked**, each sent by the digest of the definition shown. Each thing is said once: the one subtitle is how many tools ask for approval until decided, a rail row is the tool's name alone, the chosen tool is not named again over its diff, a part is named by its label alone, one it cannot show saying "This part changed". On the Tools tab a changed tool is marked *Changed*, *New* or *Removed*, the changes are counted with **Review**, **Changed** filters them, a held tool's *Always allow* says it applies once its change is reviewed, and the tab is marked while any wait.

**Built-in tools** is the engine's own tools by its groups: a rail of groups with counts beside the list (a picker under 44rem of its own width), a search and capability chips over it, every group a band while none is chosen, and a row per tool with name, line, what it can do (the engine's risk) and who may call it (its `gate`). The filters are the address (`q`, `cap`, `group`). A row opens the tool in the drawer (`?peek=tool:<name>`): description, group, who may call it, arguments. A tool's own address (`{tool}`, ONE tail segment, told from a server's page by LENGTH since a tool name is a third party's string) opens a built-in in that drawer and a server's tool on its server's Tools tab, searched for it.

**Add server** opens the add form for an admin:

- a name: its example is never a name the company already has; a name the configuration carries is refused; one only a node still runs from an earlier revision is free and said beside the field, since the engine's create judges the configuration alone;
- how it runs (*Launch a command* or *Connect to an address*), and one for the company or one per seat granted it;
- the command and its arguments one per line (or the address);
- the environment or headers as `NAME: value` rows whose value is a secret field (`$` offers the sealed entries), each with a **may be unset** box. Ticked, the row's key is sent in the server's `optional_keys`, so a value whose secret has no value is left out rather than keeping the server from starting (said once above the rows; refused before the round trip for a row whose value names no secret, since a literal cannot be unset). Two header rows spelling one header apart (`Authorization`, `authorization`) are refused the same way, since HTTP and the engine read them as one.

Add checks the whole company with the server in it (the create-only `PUT /config/mcp-servers/{name}` with `If-None-Match: *` and `dry_run`), says any warning the add introduces (not one the company already carried), places a refusal beside its field, then stores the revision and opens the new server's page.

**Models & Fleets** is every model the company runs, the LLM fleets that group them, who runs on which, and every task an operator does on them, read from `llm_entries` and `llm_fleets`, which every member may ask: a member's reading names no credential, account or vendor sentence, and every action is an admin's. It polls every fifteen seconds while open, and refreshes when this node applies a new configuration and when a seat's provider limit moves on the live state. The page has no lenses and no lede. Above the figures: the model alarms (`llm_credential_expiring`, `llm_credential_expires_soon`, `llm_sign_in_refused`, `llm_limit`, `llm_limit_waiting`). Each names its cause and what it stops, groups the models one credential or plan holds, keeps its vendor's sentence behind **Details**, and offers the one gesture that fixes it. A limit that holds seats also offers **Use a different model for these seats** (a menu of the models that answer now, never one on the limited plan, for coding only a harness that runs it; or a line saying none can) and **Add a model**. Each opens the wizard on Review with every seat's category on the limited models added (`?add=`), for Review to show before anything is written. The address only preselects: a seat the company no longer has, or coding on a harness that runs none, is dropped. Then four stat tiles, each its label and value alone: the models; how many are ready, of how many; an admin's week of tokens; the fleets.

**Models** is a card headed by its glyph, title and one line (*A model and its sign-in: a plan, an API key or a gateway.*), a row per model: its harness's mark, key and model; status, its word and dot on one line with when it changes in the tooltip ("Sitting out, back in 52 minutes"); its usage limits; how it signs in, the method alone; when it last answered; its menu. The model's page names the secret it reads.

**Fleets** is a card of one table of parents and children, the kit's `OrgTable`: each fleet a row with its name and an add control that opens its Settings at Members, its status (*n/m ready*, toned by how many, or *Empty*), its utilization strategy (*Balanced* over *Within N points*, or *Sequential* over *In order*), its usage averaged over its plans, who it serves now (faces, their names on hover) and **More actions** (Settings, Delete fleet). Its members are child rows, each read as the Models table reads its model, with a trash to remove it and, in a Sequential fleet, a handle to drag (or Alt with Up or Down on its row). A fleet with no members has one *No members yet* row. `default-fleet`, which the engine makes, is listed like any other and never deleted: its **More actions** holds Settings alone. **Create fleet** is the card's primary action. A fleet with no member that can take work raises one alarm above the card, naming who waits and the first room. Removing a member says who moves to the other members, who waits where it was the last, and who stays pinned to it, then offers Undo; deleting a fleet moves whoever runs on it to another fleet or a model of its class, or to the default fleet, as one revision.

**Who runs on which model** is a card of one table: Ask Crewlet, the Advisor and every seat, sorted by name, each with its picker under *Runs on* and its *Status*. A seat opens to a row per job the engine resolves for it, named by the org editor's words (`lib/seatJobs.ts`). Every picker lists **Fleets** (each with how many of its members have room, the default saying *Default*) then **Models** (each with its condition in one column at the row's end, a fast model marked in the pickers of a job with a deadline); a fleet with no members is an ordinary choice, and a seat on one reads *No members yet*. A seat whose jobs differ reads *Mixed* and its status is its worst job's. A member reads every value in a picker that does not open.

- Every model is named in full on a picker's trigger and each option: harness mark, key and, quieter, the model it runs by name ("sub-4 · Claude Opus 5.5"), read from the entry's model id through the engine's `llm_models` answer (the harness's aliases with the version each follows, and the public catalogue's names); an id nothing names is said as itself. The list's model line, a model's page and the wizard's Review name it the same way.
- Every pick asks once (*Move <name> to <target>?*, from where to where, any fallback the write drops), then saves. A helper's writes its one key in a step (the dry run, then the write under the revision it read) and lists a model no helper can run on disabled beside the engine's reason. A seat's writes the document: every job writes `llm` alone and clears the satellites; one job writes its own field. While the confirm is open the row says what it ran on (*Was …*).
- With no model there is nothing to pick, so the page draws one empty state in place of the tiles, the table and the cards: *No model yet*, what a model is in one line and, for an admin, **Add model**. Nothing else stands in it.

**The fleet flow** is a page of its own, as the wizard is: *Create a fleet* or *Edit <fleet>*, with the steps Members (a framed checkbox per model, another class held with *Runs <class>; this fleet runs <class>.*; the name follows the first member's class until typed), Utilization (*Balanced* or *Sequential* with a moving diagram, Sequential adding its order) and Review. Creating a fleet moves no seat; a fleet with no members is created, and gains them from its Settings.

A model's page (`models/{id}`) has its sign-in (the route, the secret, when and by whom stored, its expiry, and on a harness login each node's state with the command that makes it there), its sit-out with **Retry now** and **Clear sit-out** for every model on its plan, its last answer and failure, usage over seven days, limits, and every place that runs on it, grouped by category with backups apart and Ask Crewlet and the Advisor named. **Test** runs the harness's own checks on the answering node and says each in words. A Codex model signs in with a device code: the page shows the address and code and follows the session until it ends.

**Remove** says in one line what uses the model ("Used by 9 seats, Ask Crewlet, and the Advisor.", or that nothing does) and asks one question, where all of it moves: a model that fits every place, or Leave unset. It preselects a model only where every place already runs on it (a backup in its field, another of the seat's jobs, the other helper's model); otherwise it asks, *Choose a model*, and holds the button. *Choose per seat* opens a row per place, its name (a seat's jobs in the page's categories) and a picker, for the rare split. The list is read (`GET /config/llm-providers/{id}/references`), never asked as a refused dry run, and each complete set of moves is checked with a dry run as it changes; a refusal is said in its own words under the choice. A removal that moves everything to another model needs only the button; one that turns Ask Crewlet off, runs the Advisor with no model, or leaves seats with no model at all (the last model) asks for one tick of a box that says so. The model and every move are removed as one revision, and no config path is printed. Its own stored secrets (the ones nothing else reads, as the references read lists them) go with it by default, said in one ticked line naming them ("Delete its secret ANTHROPIC_API_KEY_SONNET"); one another model or setting still uses is said to stay. A caller the engine refuses `secrets.write` is told the secrets stay and that an admin deletes them in Settings › Secrets, and the model is removed without them. A secret the engine could not delete is said in the toast after the removal, with where to delete it.

**Adding and editing a model is one wizard**, a page of its own in place of the list: the name and harness (fixed once the model exists), how it signs in, the model (the harness's aliases, each with the version it resolves to on the vendor's service where the engine knows it, the public catalogue's models, or any name as text), where it runs a seat's executor (for a harness with a runner), its limits, and a review of exactly what changes (where adding a model offers to add it to the default fleet, on where it runs that fleet's class; a company's first model always joins it, with every seat job and both helpers on no fleet set to the default fleet rather than pinned to it), where the test call is run with its button and said in one line (the failure's own words, the engine's detail on hover).

**Finish and save** stands beside Continue from the first step where nothing the model needs is missing, so optional steps keep their defaults; on Review it is the primary action. It runs the test call where it has not passed (a new device sign-in has nothing to test until saved), the engine's check, then the save; a model saved after its test passed reads as having answered. A company with no place to run coding gets this engine's host, set up by the save of its first coding model, as Where it runs and Review say. A reload with something typed asks first. A pasted credential is tested before anything is stored and sealed before the document that names it is written; the document is checked with a dry run against the revision it edits and stored with `If-Match`, so a colleague's save in between is a conflict to re-read. A model joining the default fleet is written into it in the same revision as the model.
**Secrets** lists the names the fleet holds, their key ids and provenance, and
can store, rotate and remove one over the CLI's guarded routes. Every row is
sealed in the fleet's store. **Source is provenance**: the path that last wrote
the row, in that path's own word, never one a request chose. Drawn as: `api`
(API: this page, `PUT /secrets`, the CLI against a running node), `setup`
(Integration setup), `provision` (Provisioning pass: the engine's own, or a
provisioner's `-secret-store` run made with its node's engine stopped), `cli`
(CLI: `crewlet secrets set`) and `llm-login` (Harness login: stored by
`crewlet llm`). `cli` and `llm-login` write the fleet's store directly with
the node's engine stopped. The credential's peek says what the word means. These
five are all the listing can carry; any other is said as one this build does
not know, never guessed.
Three tiles count the credentials, the names **read by nothing** (no field in
the active configuration points at them: a forgotten `${VAR}` or an unneeded
credential; not known, never 0, when the reference check did not answer) and the
distinct key ids. The peek says each property once: its header carries the name,
**Where it came from** carries Source, Key id, Set by and Updated.
**It never asks for a value**: no reveal, and a rotation asks for the new
credential. **The name is the table's one flexible column and is never cut** (a
reader matches it against the `${VAR}` in their configuration); every other
fact is its content's width. Where the row cannot hold them all, whole columns
give way in this order: **Key id** (one id covers every row until a rekey),
**Set by**, **Source**, **Updated** (each carried by the peek), then **Read by**
(what would break if the name went, never does). Beside a peek at 1440 the name,
Read by and Updated stay. See [the secret store](../concepts/secret-store.md).

A node, a secret, an MCP server, a model and a backup domain are each **titled
by their own name**, so the trail draws that word as a name too, in the page
title's face, never the mono face kept for a key still waiting for the name a
screen publishes. A tool's trail follows its title, as its header does.

**Nodes** is every live node's lease, broker kind, posture, config epoch and
uptime. **The node is the table's one flexible column and every other fact is
its content's width** (role chips on one line, a count as wide as its head); a
share-of-row column left one digit in 150px of air while chips wrapped, and under
a peek fell to a letter with empty pills. Where the row cannot hold every fact,
whole columns give way in this order: **Lease** (every listed node's is
unexpired by definition), **Broker** (changes with a restart at most, named
again by Broker members), **Up since**, **Roles**, then **In flight**. Each is
carried by the node's peek (**Roles** and **Broker** among its header facts) and
the grid names what it hid. At 1280 Lease and Broker give way; beside a peek at
1440, Node, Seats, In flight, Posture and Config stay.
- **Broker** is the kind the node's presence advertises: `member`, `leaf` or
  `client` as a neutral tag, `unknown` (a guess) as a warning.
- **Posture**, as on a node's page and peek, is the node's own word: `serve` a
  success tag, any other a warning. Its dash says which absence it is, in its
  title and to a screen reader: a node that could not read the control plane on
  its last heartbeat publishes the rest of its status without a posture (not the
  `serve` its readiness probe falls back to); one whose last heartbeat carried no
  status has no in-flight count either.

Then **Seat placement**: each seat, its node, its lease and **Since**, the
tenure's start (`acquired_at`), stamped when the epoch is minted and carried
through every renewal, so "since 2h ago" means the seat has not moved node in
two hours. A node's own page draws the same column for its seats. The seat (and
the duty) is each lease table's one flexible column; **Held by**, **Since** and
**Lease** size to content. Seat placement and Company-wide duties sit side by
side only where each panel is at least 480px wide (about a 1520px window), else
stack. **Held by** is the same link to the node's page in both tables, at the
body's weight, so the seat or duty stays the strongest text in its row. A node's
build version is one token in its header, with the whole string in its title.
Neither screen repeats in its page bar a count a tile already shows. **Broker
members** is the fleet broker's membership twice, as the nodes advertise it and
as the metadata group counts it, with every disagreement named and a dead
member's removal behind a typed confirmation; its count is the rows it lists.
Under the last card, **Backups & retention** is a related row (`RelatedRow`, the
quiet linked row Company › Principles points at Settings › Limits with, drawn
only for a reader who may open the page it names), since every log's position is
where "which node is behind" goes next. See [seat
ownership](../concepts/seat-ownership.md) and [the fleet guide](../guides/fleet.md).

**File storage** (`#/settings/storage`) is a page of its own in the Engine
group. It is the object store: which store holds the company's files (the
fleet's own NATS bucket, or the S3 bucket it names) as a settings table row with
its key `store.objects.backend`; then the collector's passes under a head naming
the node that ran the last, one row each (hourly collection, daily audit) with
when it ran and what it found. A collection: objects deleted because no file
names them, unfinished uploads abandoned. An audit: files asked about, and how
many were missing, damaged or unanswered. It reads the fleet's record, not this
node, so every node serves the same screen.
- **Files that are missing, damaged or unanswered** are what an operator opens
  it for: when the last audit to run to its end found any, a danger callout above
  the passes names the first (each file, which of the three, its object) to
  restore from a backup or upload again. An audit that failed afterwards is said
  in its row and never clears the callout.
- A collection that stopped judging keeps what it deleted first in its row; a
  refused sweep of unfinished uploads is a warning naming the permissions an S3
  identity needs.
- A record the coordination store would not give up is said as that, not as a
  collector that has not run.
- Nothing to press: the store keeps its own copies.

Under the passes, **Storage quotas** is what the company holds against the plan's
quotas in each node's file (`artifacts.limits`): the artifacts' files, their
count and the datastores' footprint, each a figure over its ceiling with a bar
and its key, counted over every artifact, private ones and the trash included.
They are an administrator's reading about the engine, so they live here and the
Artifacts › All gallery keeps no pointer. See
[the object store](../concepts/object-store.md).

**Backups & retention** says each problem once, and first. One retention report
is read for the whole page and handed to every panel, so alarms and panels agree.
Order: **Alarms**, the record of backups, **Replication**, **Log retention**,
then **Snapshots and joining** (a single node, which takes no snapshots by
design, reads as one sentence, not a table of `sole_node`).
- **Alarms**: each kind once, in words, with the engine's measurement as a
  sentence, the logs it stands on and the engine's remedy, each a row of the one
  Alarms card with its warning glyph (not a callout inside it). Logs one term
  holds are one line ("Trim held by the backup on tracker, vectors, pages and
  usage, for 46h") with each log's own measurement under it (what a log keeps
  past its replay window is why it is listed, and no shared date says it); each
  log links to its page. A measurement that is the alarm's alone is said once
  with the logs it was taken on beside it ("tracker, vectors, pages, iam and
  usage: No verified backup has been recorded…"); the engine carries a sentence
  measured alike on several logs once, naming them, and the page draws what it is
  given. The backup they ask for is the page bar's **Take a backup**, the only
  one on the screen.
- **Log retention**: a row per log with its facts and what holds its trim in
  words ("held by the backup"), said once in the card's head where most logs
  share it ("Held by the backup on every log"), so only a differing log carries
  the tag; its six checks sit behind a disclosure, each in words beside the
  term's own name, the remedy printed only for the check that decides the trim.

The record reads `backups`. **Take a backup** asks the node serving the page for
a copy (`POST /backup`) in a directory on **that node's host**; the dialog names
the host first, since nothing is downloaded. It offers a fresh directory beside
that node's last copy when it has one (stamped to the second, never one a backup
already went to, nothing when that copy sat directly under `/`). A relative path
is refused before the round trip; the engine's refusal of a directory (occupied,
or one its host cannot create or write) is said on the field.
- A backup already running on that node (`409 backup_running`) is said as that,
  not as a failed copy.
- A refusal the fleet's own state causes shows the engine's own hint: an object
  store that did not answer (`503 objects_unreachable`), a newer build's record
  on a log the backup replays (`409 record_unreadable`), a record signed under a
  key the node does not hold (`409 record_unverified`), a copy keyed to a
  recreated log (`409
  log_recreated`) or a log missing records the copy needs (`503 log_gap`).

The request waits up to 12 hours, the CLI's own wait; closing the dialog does
not stop the copy, and the outcome arrives as a notice either way. Figures:
- **Oldest backup in use**: the oldest any log's trim reads (each log reads the
  newest counted backup covering it, so under `operator` there is one per log
  acknowledged; the stalest is the one the backup-age alarm leads with).
- **Backups that count**: the `backup_floor` policy in words ("Any node's" or
  "Confirmed only").
- How many were requested and failed, over the span the event log reads (named
  from the `event_history_seconds` the engine reports, not written into the
  screen, or "in the newest N" when the history filled its page).
- **Backup owner** (`retention.backup_owner`, "Nobody named" where nobody is,
  with where that is set in words).

**An alarm or a trim check the page can clear says so first**: the backup alarm
points at Take a backup, the backup check links the dialog that takes one, and
the engine's remedy (written for the command line it shares with
`crewlet retention status`) is folded under "From the command line"; one the
dashboard has no gesture for keeps the engine's sentence. A check is named in
words alone, never with the engine's term (`min_hold`) under it, and a log's own
page calls itself a log. **Evict is held with its reason** on the fleet's only
node and on the node answering the reader: eviction is for a node that has gone.

With nothing backed up and every node's history read, the figure says "none yet"
and the two lists are not drawn. Otherwise:
- **Newest per node and log**: each node's newest copy and the operator's newest
  acknowledgement of each log, a row per log, with directory, size (none for an
  acknowledgement, never 0), reach, and whether the trim counts it. A row reads
  **counted · newest** where some log's trim reads it (the engine's choice, not
  the latest date), so a newer copy nobody verified reads **not verified**.
- **Backup history**: every backup a person asked any node for over the event
  log's 30 days, with the node that holds it, the person, the directory and
  whether its manifest was written. A failure is drawn as one.

Neither table is derived from the other: the register keeps only each node's
newest point and each log's newest acknowledgement, so a failed night shows in
the history alone.

**Audit log** reads five sources over one window: Worklet's feed, Doclet's
changes, the configuration history, the credential rows, and **Tool calls**, the
runtime audit (`events{source: "operator"}`): every call a person made through a
running node whatever became of it, meaning each operator tool call that is not a
proven read (through the act route, an assistant over `/operator/mcp` or the
human write surface, whose chat erase, prune and horizon are rows named by their
verbs: `chat.erase`, `chat.prune`, `chat.channel.retention`) and every backup.
**Chatlet is not a source of its own**: the other four are change records and a
transcript is content (a private room's is not an administrator's to read),
while what a person *did* in chat is already here, every chat write being a call
this source records.
- A runtime row names the tool (or "backup" and its directory), who made the call
  as the engine recorded it (`actor` and `actor_kind`: the seat a bound person
  acted as, or a credential's own login) with the credential it came through
  (`operator_id`) beside it, and the node that served it in its detail's title.
  Arguments are never recorded and the cell says so.
- **Where is where the call was made**: the tool's app in the act contract
  (Chatlet, Gitlet, Worklet, Atlas) or the screen a gesture belongs to (Models,
  MCP & tools, Backups, Ask Crewlet), else "Other tool calls"; the filter offers
  each.
- **Detail is the outcome** ("Applied.", "Refused (conflict)."): the engine's
  summary less the author and tool the other cells say.
- **The credential is said in words** ("Personal access token", "Signed-in
  session") with its id behind a copy control (`components/Credential.tsx`); the
  export keeps the engine's id.
- A refused or failed call is marked as a failure.

Worklet's feed and the runtime audit are windowed by the engine, the other three
narrowed here. A page that filled before reaching the window's start is named in
a notice above the card, windowed or not, as long as the Where filter shows its
rows. A window starting before the event log's span (`event_history_seconds` on
the health push, 30 days) says in a notice that tool calls reach back only that
far, since only the runtime audit is bounded by it. On a phone Export CSV folds
into the bar's More menu. A long value in the To column is cut with an ellipsis
and carries the whole on its title (wrapped on a phone card); an empty one says
why in the row's terms (a tool call's arguments are "Not recorded"; a backup row
with no directory says so). The export carries the node and the failure beside
the eight columns on screen.

**Configuration** reads the company document through four lenses: the active
revision, its entities (kinds declared once, `ENTITY_KINDS`, held against the
engine's by `entities_client_test.go`, drawn as a list of handles down the left
edge beside the one opened), the revision history and a diff. The lenses are the
frame's **lens chips** beside the page's name (`PageLenses`, as MCP & tools'
are), which on a phone take a row of their own under the bar and scroll sideways
rather than wrapping. **The active document is the Active lens's whole
content**, so it takes the whole view (`--record-view`), not a 460px box, and
still fits the view it is scrolled to. `#/settings/config/revisions` is the
history, so it lands on the History lens.

**The Diff lens draws the changes first** and the revisions they are picked from
under them (beneath fifteen rows the changes began off screen); a revision
pressed further down brings the changes back on screen, only when they are off
it, and focus stays in the list. **A change is drawn whole**, as a
[diff](#every-diff-is-tinted) draws a setting: added is its new value added,
removed its old value removed, changed both (old removed, new added, the run
that moved underlined). Each has its mark (`+` or `−`, said as a word to a screen
reader), its path wrapping rather than cut, and its value as JSON (an object or
list in the document's own indented shape) in tracks every line shares, so
values start at one edge; on a diff narrower than a phone's 640px the value
takes the line under its path. **A value of several lines is that many lines of
the diff**, each with its own mark and tint, its path written once on the first,
and paired with the other side's lines of that path by the rule a text's lines
are ([Every diff is tinted](#every-diff-is-tinted)); drawn as one line, a removed
seat was marked on its first row alone. **An empty diff names the side it was
read against**, from the one function the card's subtitle reads ("Identical to
revision 01JCFGBBBB."); the active revision against itself says it is the active
revision, not "No differences".

A revision's peek and page say each property once: the header carries its id,
summary and state; **Where it came from** its full id and parent (mono face),
Source, creator, credential, when created and when activated.
- **The author is the reader's name for them**: a seat by its name on the chart,
  a Tier A token as "founder (API token)", never the recorded key
  (`token:founder`).
- **The credential is its kind in words** ("Personal access token", "Signed-in
  session"), its id one press away on a copy control. Beside an author it reads
  "jane.doe (through a personal access token)"; in a table (the history's By,
  Secrets' Set by) it is a caption line under the name (`AuthorCell`,
  `authorParts` in `lib/attribution.ts`), since one line cut it.
- **Across the fleet** counts the nodes running the revision in a sentence whose
  verb agrees with the count ("1 of 3 nodes runs this revision", "The fleet's
  only node runs this revision").
- In the history (and the Diff lens's revision list) **Summary is the one
  flexible column**: the revision id and its *active* pill are exactly their own
  width, When and By size to theirs, so the id is never cut and the summary takes
  the rest, never less than 12rem. **Beside a peek, When gives way** (the peek
  draws Created) rather than the summary. **By puts the name before its kind**:
  where narrow, the kind's chip leaves before the name gives up a character, and
  the name's title keeps both.
- A picked handle is a **list selection**, drawn as the column's current row is
  (raised neutral surface and hairline), never as the primary button: the accent
  belongs to the one primary action, and a violet fill under a handle in its own
  grey ink was 1.5:1.

**A revision's own page is the revision**: its header, where it came from and
which nodes run it, with no lens bar and no running document. A node whose last
attempt of it failed is listed as refusing it, naming what it runs, even when
that is this revision (the refused re-activation a credential rotation makes),
and is not counted among those that run it. **See its changes** opens the Diff
lens against the revision's *parent*, which is what that save changed (against
the active revision, the active revision's own changes were empty). **It changes
the document whole**, as its page note says on every lens, where every other
screen changes a part:

- **Revert to this revision**, on a revision's page and peek (disabled on the
  active revision, whose re-publication is a reload; its header says so under its
  title, the same sentence the button holds as its reason: "This is the active
  revision. Reload it from the Active view to publish it again."), opens a
  confirmation drawing what the revert changes in the active revision
  (`config_diff` against `active`, the cut said where the answer is a page of it)
  and a summary field, and sends `POST /config/revisions/{id}/revert`.
- **Reload**, on the Active lens, re-publishes the active document with the
  summary the person writes (`POST /config/reload`). It stays open on a managed
  document, where every other write here is disabled with the managed sentence:
  the break-glass that carries a rotated credential.
- **Edit**, on the Active lens, turns the card into the document as YAML
  (`GET /config?format=yaml`, the kit's `SourceEditor`), with **Import a file**
  to load one over it and **Check** (`PUT /config?dry_run=true` under the read's
  entity tag). The engine's problems are listed in its words, one the parser
  placed on a line marked in the gutter and offered as **Line N**. Save checks
  again, asks a second press for a warning the document introduces (the dry run's
  `introduced`), and stores it with the summary under the same tag, so a
  colleague's save in between is a conflict. A document saved as read sends
  nothing; leaving with unsaved writing asks first. Credentials are read masked
  and sent back masked: the engine restores each mask from the revision the write
  is conditional on, matched by identity, and refuses one it cannot match rather
  than clearing a secret. An active revision stored without a seal opens to
  nobody; the lens then offers **Replace the document**, the editor empty and
  conditional on the revision the refusal named.

The summary is required in each, and travels in `X-Summary` as UTF-8 bytes
(`fetch` takes a header as bytes and the engine reads them as UTF-8). Each
refusal is the engine's: a managed document names its writers, a conflict offers
a reload, and a write whose activation went unanswered (`503` with
`outcome: "unknown"`) names the revision it stored and the node holding it, and
says not to send it again.

**A write of part of the document that changes nothing is already so.** The
engine answers a `PATCH /config` or an entity's `PUT` that leaves the document as
it stands with `200` and `changed: false`, storing no revision
([A write that changes nothing](api-endpoints.md#a-write-that-changes-nothing)).
Every screen writing part of it (a setting, a ceiling, a schedule, an advisor's
fix, an MCP server switched on or off or edited in its wizard) reads that as the
change holding, drawn as the state it draws when it finds nothing to send
("Already the limit."), never as "the engine checked the change but stored
nothing", which is a check's answer (`protocol/configWrite.ts`, `outcomeOf`).
## How it is built

```
dashboard/                  the source — React 19 + TypeScript, built by Vite
  src/contract/             every declaration an engine test holds against the
                            engine — data and shapes, importing nothing else
  src/protocol/             the wire, typed. NO React, NO DOM at module scope
  src/app/                  shell, hash router, IA, command palette
  src/lib/                  store bindings, one clock, formatting, derivations
  src/ui/                   the component library and the chart kit
  src/components/           the pieces more than one screen draws, composed
                            out of the design system
  src/routes/<dir>/         one directory per group of framed screens, each
                            its own lazy chunk, as ScreenDir in
                            app/lazyScreen.ts declares them (home, inbox, me,
                            advisor, worklet, gitlet, atlas, chatlet, agents, live,
                            doclet, artifacts, brand, spend, settings,
                            account), with
                            one file per screen inside it and an index.ts
                            naming what its chunk exports. Five things sit
                            outside that shape: NotFound, which belongs to no
                            directory and is what the dispatch falls through
                            to; routes/org/, the organization builder, one
                            screen big enough to be a directory, and a chunk,
                            of its own; routes/signin/, the screens drawn
                            outside the frame, a chunk the idle prefetch
                            leaves alone; routes/gitlet/repo/ and
                            routes/gitlet/change/, Gitlet's repository and
                            change pages, each a chunk beside its section
                            pages'; and routes/artifacts/new/, where each
                            kind's create page is a chunk of its own, never
                            prefetched either (see below)
  src/styles/               tokens, base, components, shell, frame, screens —
                            what the design system does not draw
static/dashboard/           THE BUILD OUTPUT — committed, and what the binary embeds
static/artifacts/           the third build target's output — the page runtime and
                            the artifact kit — committed and embedded beside it
static/protocol/            the second's, the wire protocol alone — committed, and
                            embedded nowhere (see below)
```

**The build output is committed**: `go build ./...` and `go install …@latest` must work on a clean checkout with no Node, and an embed directive cannot run a bundler. A stale bundle would compile, embed, serve and pass every Go test while running code nobody wrote, so CI rebuilds all three trees (the Makefile's `UI_OUT`) and fails on any difference from the commit (`make dashboard-check`), like `go mod tidy -diff` and the generated `schema/`. A difference includes a file the rebuild wrote that the commit lacks: emitted names are content-hashed, so a changed chunk is a new path that `git diff` cannot see and `git commit -a` never stages.

| To | Run |
|---|---|
| change the dashboard | `make dashboard && git add -A -- static/dashboard static/artifacts static/protocol` — then commit it with your source change |
| develop against a running engine | `make dashboard-dev` (proxies to `localhost:8000`) |
| run its suites | `make dashboard-test` |
| check the committed bundle is current | `make dashboard-check` |

**The dev server forwards exactly what the source reaches.** `make
dashboard-dev` proxies to an engine on `localhost:8000`, and
`protocol/proxy.test.ts` reads every URL the tree hands `rest`, `fetch`, a
socket or a beacon, and every path a JSX `src`, `href` or `poster` names (the shell's `index.html` included, up to its first substitution), against the proxy table in `vite.config.ts`. Markup is read because the browser fetches it with no call to read. It fails when:
- no entry forwards a path: Vite would answer 404 itself, which a screen cannot tell from the engine's refusal;
- a socket's entry does not upgrade;
- an entry nothing reaches: it reads as a dependency somebody relies on and outlives its screen;
- an entry's prefix covers the dev server's own `base`, which would hand the dashboard's modules to the engine;
- a call's path cannot be read, unless it is the REST transport forwarding its caller's path, which is named with its reason.

**What the engine owns is declared once, in `src/contract/`.** The dashboard is a separate build in another language and cannot import a Go identifier, so where a screen must know a set the engine owns (event categories, turn bands, wake reasons, Worklet's sort keys, change kinds and grouping axes, config kinds, query error codes, push kinds, the feed length, the write vocabulary and its refusal codes, the questions a write is read back through) or read an answer an engine test holds it to (the integrations row, a seat's memory, the health envelope), the declaration lives in one module per concern there, nowhere else. ONE Go test holds each against the engine through `internal/clientsource`, which finds a declaration by name and reads its syntax; its `Contract()` table names every one with its reader and owning gate, held both ways: every row is declared in `src/contract/`, and every name that directory exports is a row. A second copy in a screen is two declarations, which the reader refuses.

A contract module is PURE, and `contract/contract.test.ts` says so: it imports only its siblings (not React, the design system or a screen's helper), declares no behaviour, loads under plain `node` exporting only plain data, and every name it exports is imported from outside the directory. That lets `protocol/` compose the contract's shapes into `protocol.js`; it imports them by a RELATIVE path, because that second build has no `~` alias and an import through one is left unresolved there rather than failing.

**The dashboard is held to writing as you.** Three gates, each owning one side:
- `TestEveryActionTheDashboardTakesIsOneTheActTransportServes`: `ACTIONS` against the real operator catalogue, every seam wired so the catalogue is the largest any company serves.
- `TestTheDashboardKnowsExactlyTheActRefusals`: `ACT_ERRORS` against the transport's codes and the tool refusal classes, both ways.
- `TestEverySessionQueryTakesAFreshnessFloor`: `SESSION_QUERIES` against the questions the engine serves at a floor.

On the dashboard side `app/source.test.ts` holds every `act(` and `useAct(` to a literal tool, and `app/writeGate.test.tsx` holds the one write to one hook and renders every write control for every kind of reader. The button is the call; there is no block of copyable tool calls.

`static/protocol/protocol.js` is a **second** build target: the protocol layer alone, unminified, importable by plain `node`, committed beside the served tree and never embedded, since no page loads it. `internal/e2e/golden_test.go` runs a real company, captures every frame its socket pushed, and replays those bytes through it, so the gate asks "does the client understand what the server sent", not "did the server send something". It caught a full turn's `agents` pushes sent as an object keyed by role while the client guarded on `Array.isArray`: both sides' suites passed and the seat rendered idle throughout.

The captured company gives every field a live screen keys on a real value, never a null:
- its turn is woken by a TASK assigned to the seat, so a live call names its `work_item` whole and states its `max_rounds`;
- a seat's `turn.stage` is seen in `phase`;
- a second seat caps its own day below one model call, so the gate really refuses it (a round's charge, or the call the seat's meter holds once its own context assembly has filled the day, which the meter records as the gate's refusal), and its meter arrives with `refused_at`, `resets_at` and `state: refusing`;
- the health push counts its live `nodes` and names the worst standing `alarms` (the company has never taken a backup, so one stands).

The replay and the Go half each hold all of it, so a red run says which side stopped.

The captured tab is a **person's**: a browser holding a password sign-in's cookie, bound to the founder's seat, holding `admin`, so it is sent every kind of frame. Only such a socket is pushed the company's own chat (every chat frame is decided per recipient seat; one tab is one person, as on the dashboard). The capture carries the founder using **Chatlet**:
1. a room made from the tab with a seat in it, looked at (`presence` frame);
2. a message said and reacted to, and the seat asked in its thread;
3. the seat's turn claims to have answered, is refused for saying nothing, replies in the thread (held on that round until presence shows it at work, true only while its turn runs), and submits citing the reply: three rounds, the captured company's cap, so the turn ends on its own `delivered`, not the engine's rescue (the Go half reads this off the turn's phase record);
4. the first message edited and deleted, the room read through the seat's answer with `mark_chat_read`, left, and pruned through `POST /chatlet/channels/{channel_id}/prune` (an administrator's gesture, with the step-up the sign-in just proved).

Every other change is a press of the act transport. Every chat push kind is on the capture, held against `stream.ChatPushKinds`, so a kind the engine adds fails the capture until produced.

The replay is handed an account of the room written beside the frames, never read from them: its id, the person and the seat, the highest `channel_seq` minted, every record (op, message named, author and kind, a post's thread), where the last record sits and the cursor the founder flushed. Engine-minted values (room id, message ids from post receipts or the seat's transcript, numbering, the prune's position) are read from its answers. Each record is the gesture as made (the founder as the human seat, the seat as an agent in its thread), so a wrongly recorded author or thread fails. The store must hold:
- the room filed with that high-water mark;
- a frame per record naming exactly what the capture did, and none other (the Go half holds the frames to the same account first);
- its newest moment the prune's position;
- presence that at some frame showed the founder looking and the seat working;
- the founder's read state with that cursor and a revision.

Each record is held on its own: an edit, delete or reaction filed under the wrong message re-reads the wrong range, which only a per-frame comparison sees.

The capture also carries two **writes** whose floors the replay holds, each made AS THE PERSON THE SESSION RESOLVES TO under its own `Idempotency-Key`, as the dashboard's `act` sends it: the founder pins a project through `POST /operator/act/set_pins` after the frames are taken, and the founder's first message is `POST /operator/act/post_message`. The route is the node's own operator surface, the one `crewlet run` builds inside `api.NewHumanSurfaces`, whose catalogue is built from what the node serves then (no second catalogue), and the viewer names each write among its `acts` before it is pressed. The Go half holds each answer to the read it promises: its `position` is in the grammar a read accepts back, and `GET /worklet/people/{handle}` (pin) or `GET /chatlet/channels/{channel_id}/messages` (message) at `read_level=session&min_position=<position>` is served at `session` and already holds the write. The replay hands the same answers, byte for byte, to the client's `act` and one tab's `SessionFloors`: the `tracker` floor must be the pin's position and the `chat` floor the message's, and a read of `work_person` or `work_items` (or `chat_messages` or `chat_channels`) must name its log's as its one `min_position`. An unparseable floor raises nothing, and the pressing screen would redraw from before the press silently.

The suites run in **Europe/Berlin** under jsdom (`vitest.config.ts`), and `src/test/environment.test.tsx` checks it by what the zone produces (both offsets, the 23- and 25-hour days), not by reading the config: under UTC, every runner's zone, a whole family of date bugs cannot be reproduced. The same suite renders one design-system component, because every kit component imports its own stylesheet and a suite that cannot load a `.css` file fails to LOAD, reporting no tests rather than a failure.

**The engine's own suite loads the shell the way a browser does.** `internal/api` fetches `/dashboard` from the server, never from disk, and follows every file a browser is sent to: the shell's script, preload and stylesheet links, every static `import`, every lazy `import()`, the preload list Vite writes beside one (`__vite__mapDeps`, the only place a lazy chunk's own stylesheet is named, entries relative to `base`), each stylesheet's `url()`s and any `/static/` path a module holds. A file that does not answer 200 with the type a browser requires fails the build, naming the file still asking for it, because that is where the fix is. The converse fails too: a file under `assets/` that nothing reached is dead weight in every binary or a reference the crawl cannot read, and a crawl that silently skipped a lazy chunk would certify a screen nobody can open. Every stylesheet the crawl reaches, a lazy one included, is also held to the Content-Security-Policy.

**A chunk per screen directory, and the next one fetched while nobody waits.** `app/lazyScreen.ts` loads every screen: one chunk per directory in the tree above (`routes/<dir>/index.ts`, held to `ScreenDir` by `app/lazy.test.tsx` both ways), plus one for the org builder (Company › Structure, larger than any whole workspace), one for the sign-in screens, and one per kind's create page (`routes/artifacts/new/`). Gitlet is three chunks, by address: section pages, a repository's pages, and a change's page with its peek. A screen's peek lives in its directory's chunk.

The entry holds the frame (sidebar, page header, socket client) and nothing a screen draws, so a reader of the Inbox does not parse the org builder. The command palette and Ask Crewlet's panel are layers mounted only while open, each its own chunk and the first two the idle prefetch fetches; `app/lazy.test.tsx` refuses a static path to either from `main.tsx`.

The artifacts' contract is split the same way. The frame reads `contract/artifacts.ts` (the kinds, the roles, what a history row is filed under, the trash's days, the pinned list's page), so it is in the entry. Everything only the artifacts workspace reads (each format's files and bounds, the datastore's vocabulary, the slide subset, a board's closed sets) is `contract/artifactsworkspace.ts`, fetched with the first artifact screen opened. `app/lazy.test.tsx` refuses a static path from `main.tsx` to the second, and a declaration in the first that the entry does not read.

Two things keep the second click fast: hovering or focusing a sidebar row starts fetching its chunk, and once the first screen is up every other chunk is fetched in turn, one at a time, each in an idle moment the browser reports (not at all for a reader whose browser asks to save data), except the sign-in screens and the create pages, which a signed-in reader, or one who opened Artifacts to look, never needs. `app/lazy.test.tsx` refuses a static import of a screen's module from outside `routes/`, because the bundler follows one wherever it is and would pull that directory into the entry with nothing failing.

**A chunk that does not arrive says so, and can be retried.** The usual reason is an upgrade: chunks are named by content hash, and an engine upgraded while the tab was open serves different ones. The screen names what is missing ("The Spend screens could not be loaded"), says "The engine was updated. Reload to continue.", and offers Reload, which fixes it, beside Try again for the other reason, a dropped request.

Try again really asks again: a failed load is forgotten rather than cached for the life of the page the way `React.lazy` caches one, but only once no place on the page can show the failure any more. A screen, a peek and each layer is such a place; one stops being able to show it when it draws it, when it goes, or when the reader moves it on to another path or object. Until then React's replays of the render that waited read the same rejection instead of each starting a request nobody reads, so a gone chunk costs one request, not one per render React makes before giving up (five, and seven under the whole frame when the cache forgot a failure as it happened) or one per each of two places drawing it at once (a screen and the object peeked beside it). The reader's next attempt (Try again, another navigation, a layer opened again) is the one that asks. A load nobody was drawing (a hover's or the idle prefetch's) is forgotten as it fails, and so is one whose screen the reader left before it failed: nobody was told, so the next hover, prefetch or navigation asks afresh.
**The bundle has a budget, measured as the engine sends it.** The split above is
undone by one static import of a screen's module from the frame — the bundler
follows it and the workspace is back in the entry with every other test green —
so `internal/api`'s `TestTheDashboardFitsItsBudget` measures the crawl described above
and fails a build over any of four numbers:

| What | Budget | Measured as | Why this number |
|---|---|---|---|
| The initial load: the entry, its static imports and the linked stylesheets | 445 KiB | gzip at the best level, which is what the engine serves | Under two seconds on a 1.5 Mbit/s link.
